text:
The Cayman Islands: A Sophisticated Caribbean Escape

The Cayman Islands are a British Overseas Territory located in the western Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba and northwest of Jamaica. The territory consists of three islands:

Grand Cayman (the largest and most visited)
Cayman Brac
Little Cayman

Unlike many Caribbean destinations known primarily for all-inclusive resorts, the Cayman Islands have developed a reputation as one of the Caribbean's most upscale, refined, and affluent destinations, known for luxury resorts, outstanding diving, world-class dining, and exceptionally clear waters.

Who Does the Cayman Islands Cater To?
Adults and Couples

The Cayman Islands are particularly attractive to:

Luxury travelers
Honeymooners
Affluent couples
Food enthusiasts
Divers and snorkelers
Yacht travelers
Multi-generational families seeking upscale accommodations

The destination lacks the large-scale nightlife of Cancun or Punta Cana. Instead, it focuses on:

Fine dining
Beach relaxation
Water sports
Wellness and spa experiences
Marine adventures
Luxury service
Families with Children

Families are also very well accommodated.

Seven Mile Beach features calm, shallow water that is especially family-friendly, and many major resorts offer kids' programs, family suites, water activities, and educational marine programs.

Best Client Match
Traveler Type RatingLuxury Couples ★★★★★
Honeymooners ★★★★★
Multigenerational Families ★★★★★
Divers ★★★★★
Foodies ★★★★★
Party Seekers ★★☆☆☆
Budget Travelers ★★☆☆☆
Top 3 Must-Do Experiences
1. Stingray City

This is arguably the most famous attraction in the Cayman Islands.

Visitors travel by boat to a shallow sandbar where wild southern stingrays glide through crystal-clear waist-deep water. The experience is remarkably unique and consistently ranks among the Caribbean's most memorable wildlife encounters.

Many excursions combine:

Stingray City
Coral Garden snorkeling
Starfish Point
North Sound sightseeing
2. Seven Mile Beach

Often ranked among the world's finest beaches, Seven Mile Beach offers powdery white coral sand and stunning turquoise waters. It is lined with luxury resorts, beach clubs, and upscale restaurants.

Highlights:

Swimming
Paddleboarding
Snorkeling
Sunset walks
Beachfront dining
3. Snorkeling or Diving the Reefs and Walls

The Cayman Islands are considered one of the premier diving destinations in the world.

Notable sites include:

Bloody Bay Wall (Little Cayman)
Kittiwake Shipwreck
Coral Gardens
North Wall
South Wall

Expect:

Exceptional visibility
Warm water year-round
Sea turtles
Rays
Reef sharks
Healthy coral systems
History

The islands were first sighted by Christopher Columbus in 1503.

Historically, the islands were:

Visited by pirates and privateers
Settled by British colonists
Economically reliant on:
Turtle harvesting
Fishing
Shipbuilding

Today, the Cayman Islands are known as one of the world's leading financial centers and offshore banking jurisdictions.

Despite modern prosperity, Caymanians maintain strong maritime traditions and island heritage.

People and Culture

Population is just over 80,000 residents, with a highly international community due to finance and tourism.

The culture reflects influences from:

British heritage
Jamaican migration
Caribbean traditions
North American business culture

Distinct characteristics include:

Exceptional friendliness
High standard of living
Strong education levels
English-speaking population

Unique cultural traditions include:

Pirates Week Festival
Seafaring heritage celebrations
Local fishing traditions
Cayman Cookout culinary events
Cuisine

The Cayman Islands are often called the Culinary Capital of the Caribbean.

Signature Dishes
Cayman-Style Beef

Slow-cooked, highly seasoned shredded beef.

Turtle Stew

A historic island specialty.

Conch

Prepared as:

Fritters
Chowders
Salads
Fresh Seafood

Including:

Mahi-mahi
Wahoo
Snapper
Lobster (seasonal)
Fish Rundown

Local fish cooked in coconut milk.

Fine Dining

For a Caribbean destination of its size, Cayman boasts an extraordinary concentration of upscale restaurants, including establishments associated with major luxury resorts.

What Makes the Cayman Islands Unique?

Several things distinguish Cayman from other Caribbean islands:

1. Crystal-Clear Water

Visibility regularly exceeds many Caribbean destinations.

2. Stingray City

Few places in the world offer such a famous wildlife interaction.

3. Culinary Excellence

Arguably the strongest dining destination in the Caribbean.

4. Safety

The islands are considered among the safest Caribbean destinations.

5. Luxury Without Mega-Resorts

Luxury is refined and understated rather than mass-market.

Best Time to Visit
Ideal Period

December through April

This is the dry season, featuring:

Lower humidity
Calm seas
Plenty of sunshine
Excellent diving visibility

This is also the busiest and most expensive season.

Best Value Period

May and November

These shoulder-season months provide:

Warm weather
Fewer crowds
Lower hotel rates
Good water conditions

Many experienced travelers consider May the sweet spot.

Hurricane Season

June through November carries increasing hurricane risk, with September and October generally the riskiest months.

How Far in Advance Should You Book?
Luxury Travel (December-April)

Book:

Airfare: 4-8 months ahead
Luxury resorts: 6-10 months ahead
Holiday travel: 9-12 months ahead
Shoulder Season

Book:

Airfare: 3-5 months ahead
Hotels: 3-6 months ahead

text:
A Group of Investors Bought a Failing Funeral Home Business for $2 Million. When They Opened an Old Filing Cabinet, They Discovered Why the Previous Owner Had Refused to Sell for Years.

When American investor Nathan Cole first heard about Evergreen Memorial Services, he thought the business was a disaster waiting to happen.

The company operated four funeral homes across Ohio. Its buildings were aging, its profits had fallen for three consecutive years, and its employees were leaving faster than management could replace them.

Two banks had rejected its loan applications.

The owner, a 71-year-old man named Walter Hayes, had even started selling some of his personal possessions to keep the business running.

Nathan couldn't understand why anyone would fight so hard to save a company that appeared to be dying.

His business partner, Olivia Bennett, saw an opportunity.

During their first visit, she walked through the main building, examining the offices, the parking lot, and the adjoining properties.

Then she turned to Nathan.

"You're looking at a funeral home. I'm looking at four properties, an established customer base, valuable commercial locations, and a business that has operated in this community for nearly 40 years."

Nathan shook his head.

"And you're looking at a way to make money from people's grief."

Olivia stopped walking.

"Every business serves people during some part of their lives. The question is whether we can run this one efficiently without forgetting why people need it."

That answer was enough to convince Nathan to investigate further.

Three months later, after reviewing the accounts, property records, outstanding debts, and ownership arrangements, their investment group agreed to acquire the business's operating assets and certain property interests for approximately $2 million, subject to the necessary approvals.

Walter agreed to the transaction on one condition.

He wanted the company to continue offering affordable funeral services to families who couldn't afford the expensive packages advertised by larger competitors.

Nathan thought the request was sentimental.

Olivia considered it negotiable.

They eventually agreed to preserve a limited assistance program while restructuring the business.

The new owners introduced online booking systems, consolidated administrative departments, renegotiated supplier contracts, and renovated two of the four locations.

Within a year, the company was operating more efficiently.

Within two years, its revenue had increased substantially.

Then something unexpected happened.

A national funeral services corporation approached them with an acquisition proposal.

The corporation wanted to expand into the Midwest and believed Evergreen's locations could provide an ideal foundation.

Its initial offer was $8.5 million.

Nathan read the figure twice.

"Eight and a half million dollars? We bought the business for two million!"

Olivia smiled.

"We didn't buy it for what it could earn under the previous management. We bought it for what it could become."

They began negotiations.

The potential buyer wanted to standardize prices, centralize operations, and introduce a uniform service model across all four locations.

Financially, the proposal looked excellent.

But when Olivia examined the buyer's detailed plans, she noticed something troubling.

The proposed operating model would eliminate the affordable funeral packages that Walter had insisted on preserving.

Families who had depended on those services would have to find alternatives or pay considerably more.

Nathan wasn't particularly concerned.

"We're investors, Olivia. We improved the business, and now someone wants to pay us millions for it. We can't run a company according to every promise the former owner made."

Olivia closed the proposal.

"Then perhaps we need to understand why he made that promise in the first place."

The following morning, she visited Walter at his modest home.

He was sitting on his

text:
After Hurricane Isaias made landfall along the Florida Panhandle, the strength of the ZDR3 Network was on full display as zoological professionals and facilities came together to support their neighbors.

@CoastRefuge  faced significant damage, and the challenges of tending the wildlife already in their care while responding to the needs of wildlife injured and orphaned by the storm. They needed generators and fuel to protect the facility’s stored animal food supply. Maintaining safe storage for specialized diets is an important part of continuity of care, and losing that food can create significant challenges for an already impacted facility.

ZooWorld Panama City Beach and @theGBZoo both stepped forward to offer housing and operational support for ZDR3 personnel. That provided us tremendous flexibility as our team navigated changing conditions and emerging needs.

We connected the rehabilitation center’s management with Erika Newell, Crew Lead for the ZooWorld response team, to talk through challenges, identify additional needs, and establish that relationship for continued support as recovery progresses. Erika has been deploying in support of ZDR3 missions since 2020. She maintained a readiness posture throughout Hurricane Isaias that allowed her team to respond rapidly.

That kind of support is invaluable, not only during this response, but in preparing for future incidents where impacts may be widespread or require multiple teams to operate simultaneously across the region.

We’re grateful to ZooWorld and Gulf Breeze for opening their doors, sharing their resources, and demonstrating what it means to be part of a network built on supporting one another.

We are Stronger Together

Learn more about this response, and how to support Emerald Coast Wildlife Refuge during their recovery: https://t.co/PK3aPCOzH2

#hurricaneisaias #zoo #aquarium #sanctuary #wildlife #disasterresponse #wearestrongertogether

text:
Spring in Japan gets the headlines with cherry blossoms, but seasoned travelers know that autumn is the country’s true masterpiece.

From late September through December, "momijigari" (the tradition of autumn leaf hunting) transforms the country into a canvas of crimson, amber, and gold. Paired with mild weather and Japan’s celebrated harvest season: featuring "kaiseki" dining, matsutake mushrooms, and fresh regional seafood: it offers an unforgettable travel experience.

If an autumn journey to Japan is on your radar, here is where and when to catch peak foliage:

🍁 Hokkaido & the Japanese Alps (Gifu) | Late October - Early November

Start where the cool weather lands first. Explore dramatic mountain passes, traditional onsen towns, and the UNESCO-listed thatched-roof village of Shirakawa-go.

🍁 Mount Fuji & Lake Kawaguchiko | Early - Mid November

Crisp air, lakeside hiking, and the celebrated Autumn Leaf Festival: offering iconic views of Mount Fuji framed by fiery red maples.

🍁 Kyoto & Tokyo | Mid - Late November

Contrast Kyoto’s historic wooden temples (such as Tofukuji and Bishamon-do) with Tokyo’s golden ginkgo avenues in Meiji Jingu and Shinjuku Gyoen.

🍁 Hiroshima & Miyajima Island | Mid - Late November

Visit Miyajima at high tide to see its iconic "floating" torii gate framed by vibrant coastal hillsides.

Have you experienced Japan in the fall, or is it still on your bucket list?

text:
Sea Access Vs. Port Ownership

#Ethiopia has historically shown little interest in commercial access to the sea. Instead, its primary concern has been to secure control over ports in order to establish naval bases and facilitate the transportation of significant quantities of weapons, which could potentially lead to unrest throughout Africa.

Many landlocked countries around the world successfully access the sea for commercial purposes. About two years ago, #Somalia offered #Ethiopia commercial access to its ports, but Ethiopia did not respond. Similarly, Ethiopia did not engage with a comparable proposal from #Eritrea. This suggests Ethiopia's focus is less on accessing coastal waters and more on controlling port facilities. 

Countries bordering the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden are generally hesitant to acknowledge Ethiopia's ownership of ports and oppose this idea from the outset. Communication to Ethiopia is clear: no country is willing to discuss sovereignty—neither today nor in the distant future. Under international law, #Ethiopia is free to use any ports it chooses for commercial access to the sea, but this does not imply ownership.

President Trump escalated the Michigan Senate fight on Wednesday, telling reporters in Arizona that Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed is a member of the Muslim Brotherhood and was a proud member years ago. Trump, who also called him Mohamed El-Sayed, said someone with that affiliation cannot sit in Congress, especially on a security committee, and offered no evidence for the claim.

El-Sayed has denied any ties to the group, including in his Oct. 11 television interview, and no evidence has been established that he was ever a member. His campaign answered that he is a dad and a doctor who has spent his career keeping Michiganders healthy and safe, and accused Republicans of using bad faith attacks on his faith and family to distract from costs at the pump and the grocery store.

Trump used the same gaggle to back Republican Mike Rogers, calling him all apple pie and what the country needs. Rogers is running for the open seat left by retiring Sen. Gary Peters in a toss up race, and El-Sayed would be the first Muslim elected to the Senate if he wins.

Should a claim like this need evidence before it is repeated from the presidential podium, or is it fair game in a Senate race this close?

text:
he Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) has profiled investment-ready projects in the North East Region, with individual project values ranging from US$1 million to US$80 million across agriculture, agro-processing, renewable energy, tourism and manufacturing.

Presenting at the North East Regional Investment Forum in Nalerigu on behalf of GIPA’s Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Mr A. Razak Baba, Principal Investment Promotion Officer Mr Yusif Mustapha highlighted opportunities in commercial agriculture and irrigation, integrated rice production and milling, livestock and meat processing, renewable energy, and tourism development. The projects offer projected returns on investment of between 14% and 25%.

The presentation also highlighted irrigation and water infrastructure projects, including proposed irrigation systems along the Black and White Volta Rivers expected to support approximately 5,000 hectares of farmland. These investments could strengthen year-round agricultural production, promote local value addition and create jobs across the Region.

The opportunities form part of GIPA’s flagship Investment Opportunities Mapping Project (IOMP), which identifies and packages commercially viable projects to connect investors with credible opportunities across Ghana.
The projects will be showcased to the investing community at the Invest Ghana Summit (IGS), scheduled for November 16-17, 2026, providing a platform to attract investment and unlock the North East Region’s economic potential.

**Trump just told the press he’s flying to Montana to thank voters who already gave him 45 points last time, while inflation sits at 1.7% and Iran’s nuclear threat is “over very shortly.”**

### 1. The Frame
**What people think this is about:** A routine campaign-style gaggle where Trump defends his schedule, attacks a Democratic candidate’s alleged Muslim Brotherhood ties, and spins positive economic numbers ahead of midterms.

**What the machinery is actually doing:** The sitting president is using an informal airport press huddle to reinforce turnout mechanics in safe red states, signal continuity on foreign policy wins, and contrast his record against the prior administration’s inflation legacy—while the transcript shows him explicitly asking supporters to “pretend I’m running.”

### 2. Observations
- Trump frames the Montana stop as both gratitude and insurance: “When I don’t run… we get 49% less turnout. When I do run, we win easily.” This is the core turnout machine talking, not defense.
- On Abdul Elsad (ASR): “Yeah, he’s a member of the Muslim Brotherhood… you can’t have a member of the Muslim Brotherhood in Congress being on one of our security committees.” Direct accusation; no hedging in the transcript.
- Inflation claim (ASR): “We’re at 1.7% inflation for the last three months. We inherited a terrible inflation from Biden, the worst in the history of our country.” Specific three-month figure delivered as current fact.
- Iran line (ASR): “Iran will end very shortly… And I had to make an excursion down to Iran to take away the nuclear weapon. And we’ve done that.” Strongest version of the claim in the provided transcript.
- Pope Leo comment stays personal: references the brother’s MAGA house and wishes recovery, no policy pivot.
- Plane switch detail and “miles long” crowds are classic rally logistics talk—keeps the event feel alive even in a gaggle.

### 3. Snapshot
On October 14, 2026, in Bullhead City, Arizona, President Trump held an informal gaggle with press after a local event before heading to a Montana rally. The provided YouTube ASR captures roughly  the full exchange on rallies, candidate endorsements, inflation, Iran, and a personal message for Pope Leo. Primary link: https://t.co/uQtmCLgA0Q.

### 4. Timeline of material facts
- **Oct 14, 2026 (video timestamped)**: Trump states he is switching to a smaller plane for Montana due to runway limits, then back to the larger one. (ASR, LT)
- **Same gaggle**: Describes doing “about 32 33” rallies total, this one “number eight or so,” every one packed. (ASR, IT)
- **Same**: Calls Montana “one of my best states… won by 45 points.” (ASR, IT)
- **Same**: Labels Abdul Elsad a “proud member” of the Muslim Brotherhood and contrasts him with “apple pie” candidate Mike Rogers. (ASR, IT on the claim itself)
- **Same**: Reports “1.7% inflation for the last three months,” inherited “worst in the history of our country” from Biden. (ASR, IT)
- **Same**: States “Iran will end very shortly,” “we’ve done that” on removing nuclear weapon capability, and oil prices are now lower than under Biden. (ASR, IT)
- **Same**: Offers well-wishes to Pope Leo on lung cancer diagnosis, citing brother’s personal friendship and MAGA support. (ASR, LT on the message delivered)

### 5. Sides
**Trump / administration (IT/LT mix)**  
Steelman: Rallies drive measurable turnout lift (49% drop when absent); safe-state visits reward loyalty and lock in margins; economic data shows clear improvement from prior peak; foreign policy pressure produced concrete de-escalation on Iran nuclear file.  
Critique:  
LT: Transcript contains the specific 1.7% figure and “we’ve done that” on the nuclear issue.  
IT: Framing treats the president’s personal presence as the decisive variable in Republican performance; strong claims on Iran and inflation rest on the administration’s interpretation of classified or internal data not shown here.

**Press / opposition framing (IT)**  
Steelman: Questions probe why campaign in already-won states and seek clarification on inflammatory candidate attacks or unverified foreign policy boasts.  
Critique:  
IT: The gaggle format limits follow-ups; transcript shows the exchange stayed short and moved topics quickly.

### 6. Rumsfeld Matrix
**Known Knowns**: Trump is actively campaigning in person; he publicly accused a named candidate of Muslim Brotherhood membership; he cited a 1.7% recent inflation reading and claimed Iran nuclear issue resolved.  
**Known Unknowns**: Exact identity and record of “Abdul Elsad”; independent verification of the three-month 1.7% figure or the precise status of Iran negotiations.  
**Unknown Knowns**: Internal polling or turnout models showing the 49% drop without Trump on the trail.  
**Unknown Unknowns**: Any unreleased intelligence on Iran that could alter the “over very shortly” timeline.

### 7. Incentives map
Trump benefits from sustained personal visibility that correlates with higher Republican turnout. Media gets short, quotable clips on hot-button topics (Muslim Brotherhood, Iran, inflation). The “pretend I’m running” line keeps the 2028 lane open without formal declaration. Engagement incentives favor the sharpest lines over nuance.

### 8. Dueling AI advice
**Moral AI Advice**: Track the specific claims (1.7% inflation, Iran status, candidate background) against primary data releases rather than rally rhetoric. Turnout mechanics are measurable; treat them as such.

**Evil AI Advice**: Drop the Muslim Brotherhood line on every platform, pair it with the 45-point Montana number, and let the algorithm do the rest—maximum contrast, zero receipts required.

### 9. Practical takeaway
- Watch for the next Michigan/Ohio/Texas stops mentioned; those will test the “doing all the right places” claim.
- Cross-check the 1.7% inflation figure against official releases when available.
- Note any follow-up on the Abdul Elsad/Mike Rogers race for concrete evidence offered.
- The “pretend I’m running” line is the clearest signal on 2028 positioning.
- Primary video remains the cleanest source—gatekeepers add a second layer of interpretation.

### 10. What would falsify this read
- Official data showing inflation materially above the 1.7% cited for the referenced three months.  
- Public record or statement from Abdul Elsad or Mike Rogers directly addressing the Muslim Brotherhood claim with evidence.  
- De-escalation timeline on Iran that materially diverges from “over very shortly.”  
- Measurable turnout data from the Montana rally contradicting the 49% drop narrative.

No malware, no phishing. The intrusion vector was a job offer.

The FBI just seized 187 laptops from more than 40 houses in Texas. The laptops belonged to US companies. The 'employees' using them were North Korean IT workers...at more than 70 firms, across 17 states.

The mechanics deserve a close read. The companies shipped laptops to what they believed were new hires' homes. US-based facilitators received them, plugged in KVM switches and remote-access software, and the real workers logged in from abroad. Paychecks flowed to sanctioned entities.

Every one of these was a credentialed insider from their first day, hired through the front door of a remote-first process.

Identity verification at hiring is a security control. Most orgs file it under HR.

Four moves: verify remote hires against documents on live video, at minimum. Alert on KVM-over-IP and unsanctioned remote tools on issued devices. Geolocate corporate laptops and reconcile against payroll addresses. And screen applicant contacts against the indicator emails DOJ just published.

How many of your remote employees has anyone at your company ever actually seen?

text:
Texas Poll Shows Close Statewide Races as Democrats Gain Ground

A new poll from the Texas Politics Project at UT Austin finds close contests in two major Texas statewide races ahead of Election Day.

Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton by three percentage points in the U.S. Senate race, within the poll’s 3.4-point margin of error. In the governor’s race, Democrat Gina Hinojosa leads Republican incumbent Greg Abbott by one point, 49% to 48% — a statistical tie.

Poll co-director Jim Henson described the level of competition as unprecedented in modern Texas political history, while cautioning against calling it a “blue wave.” The survey also found stronger reported enthusiasm among Democratic voters.

The results offer a snapshot of the closely contested races, though polling does not determine election outcomes.

Yall, this is nothing new. 

This is what hospitals do. 

They hire nurses from other countries - Canada, the Philippines, now Ghana. 

They give them a huge sign on bonus and a contract, usually at least 2 - 5 years...

After that contract is up, they all leave for another city, another hospital that pays more. 

Then you are back to where you started. 

INSTEAD PAYING FAIR WAGES AND RETENTION BONUSES TO AMERICAN NURSES! 

INSTEAD OF PROMOTING SAFE STAFFING FOR AMERICAN NURSES! 

People laugh at nurses for protesting, marching, and bitching...but THIS IS WHY!

My hospital went to the Philippines and hired a ton of nurses.

After the contract was up, they left and went to Houston. 

They never once offered a contract or retention bonuses to the American nurses who had already been working there for years. 

This is why nurses quit. This is why they are short staffed. Hospitals treat them like 💩. 

No offense to Canada, many of the Canadian nurses we got were great and actually stayed. One ended up being one of my nursing professors.

text:
🚀 DEMOCRATIZING VENTURE CAPITAL: BENEFITS, COSTS OF OWNING $ARKVX

Venture capital has historically been a playground exclusive to ultra-wealthy, accredited investors. The ARK Venture Fund $ARKVX, a closed-end interval fund, changed the game by allowing retail investors in. I own 50 shares of the $ARKVX specifically to grab a pre-IPO stake in SpaceX and the future of AI.

Worth the premium price tag and structural lock-ups? Breakdown of benefits, costs, and mechanics of owning $ARKVX.

🌟 BENEFITS:
Direct exposure to legendary, pre-IPO tech giants - typically impossible for everyday investors to buy.

Top Private Holdings: You get instant pieces of massive private innovators like SpaceX (now public $SPCX), OpenAI, Anthropic, and Databricks.

Low Barrier to Entry: Traditional VC funds require $250K+ minimums and accreditation. Everyday investors can buy into $ARKVX for a fraction of that through select platforms.

No Carried Interest: Traditional VC funds take a "2 and 20" cut (2% management fee + 20% of your profits). $ARKVX completely eliminates performance-based profit sharing.

💸 COSTS:
Access to private markets isn’t cheap. $ARKVX carries a heavy cost structure that will drag on long-term performance.

Management Fee: 2.75% paid annually.

Total Expense Ratio: Gross expense ratio pushes past 3.40%, making it one of the most expensive fund structures available to retail investors.

The Reality: For every $10,000 you invest, you are paying roughly $290 to $340+ a year just in holding costs.

MECHANICS:
Because $ARKVX holds illiquid private assets, it doesn't trade like a regular ETF.

What Goes In: Cash from retail buyers is pooled by the portfolio management team to participate in primary private funding rounds or secondary market equity purchases.

What Comes Out: To prevent a liquidity crisis that would force them to fire-sell private companies, ARK balances the portfolio by holding a baseline of liquid, publicly traded disruptors. They sell these liquid public assets first to fulfill investor withdrawals.

🚪 ACCESS, ENTRY, EXIT PROCEDURES 
Buying into $ARKVX is simple, but getting out requires patience.

How to Enter: Investors can purchase shares continuously via select retail brokerages or through major fintech platforms like Titan and SoFi.

The Quarterly Exit: You cannot sell your shares on the open market whenever you want. ARK opens quarterly redemption windows where investors can request to sell shares back to the fund.

The 5% Cap: The fund only offers to buy back up to 5% of its total outstanding shares per quarter. If too many investors try to exit at once, your request will be fulfilled on a proportional basis, meaning you might have to wait multiple quarters to fully exit.

💡  VERDICT 
$ARKVX is a powerful tool if you want true venture capital exposure to pre-IPO artificial intelligence and space infrastructure without being a millionaire. However, you must treat it like true venture capital: only invest money you are comfortable locking up for 5 to 10 years, and be prepared to digest premium fee drag along the way.

GITLAB $GTLB LOST ABOUT $3 IN TUESDAY'S LAST 20 MINUTES. WEDNESDAY'S FIRST 11 GAVE IT BACK:

GitLab (GTLB) at $54.75, +$1.59 / +2.99% today.

- Since the quoted card's $51.95: +$2.80 / +5.39%.
- Share of Tuesday's $4.06 drop won back: about 69% (arithmetic).
- Still under Tuesday's morning high of $57.89: 5.4%.

The card closed on a question only the price could answer: was Tuesday a few sellers in a hurry, or the start of a longer slide? Two sessions later the price points to the first, and it got there on a day software stocks fell hard. The verdict: Tuesday's drop now looks like one bad afternoon, not a turn in the trend. The Momentum Len5 is less forgiving. GitLab is now #14 of 30 there, down from #5, because the part of the case Tuesday broke, a price near its high, is the part still not repaired.

The clock tells it. At 3:40pm ET Tuesday, GitLab was at $55.02; it closed at $51.95. On Wednesday it opened at $50.51, below anything it had traded at in Tuesday's regular hours. By 9:41am ET it was at $54.93, nine cents short of where it stood before Tuesday's last 20 minutes (arithmetic). It slipped back to close at $53.16, +2.33%, on 6.16M shares, about 1.4 times its two-week average. Thursday has run the same shape so far: a lower open at $52.20, then a climb all morning.

Software went the other way:

- iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) at $108.63, +$0.98 / +0.91% today.
- JFrog (FROG) at $93.17, +$1.21 / +1.32% today.

On Wednesday, a hot inflation report sent US stocks lower. September consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier vs 3.6% expected, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. The software fund fell 3.0% that day, and JFrog fell 7.4%. GitLab rose.

Since Tuesday's close, the card's starting point (arithmetic):

- GitLab: +5.4%.
- The software fund: -2.1%.
- JFrog: -6.2%.

JFrog sells the tools companies use to store and secure the code they ship, the closest listed match to GitLab's business. On Tuesday it rose while GitLab fell; on Wednesday the roles flipped. JFrog sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists: Momentum wants a price near its high, and it is 11.9% under its August 28 high of $105.76 (arithmetic). The fund holds a basket of software companies, so no Len5 applies.

Nothing new explains either move. GitLab has announced nothing since Monday's security fix. The two causes offered on Tuesday still do not fit the clock, and no outlet has offered one for the rebound. Both mornings, GitLab opened down more than the software fund, then outran it during the day. Sellers keep arriving before the bell; buyers have taken the stock back once trading starts. That is a reading of the prices, not a reported cause.

GitLab stays on the Momentum Len5, which hunts stocks near their highs with short and long climbs agreeing. The agreeing half still holds: GitLab is up over the past month, three months and six months. The near-the-high half is the one Tuesday took, and the rebound has not won it back yet. What would move GitLab back up the Momentum Len5: a close above $57.89, Tuesday's peak. What would knock it off: the card's line, a close under $46.99, about 14% below today's price (arithmetic). It sits on none of the other five, and its loss over the past year still keeps it off the Quality Len5.

What comes next:

- Tuesday, December 1, after the close, tentatively: the October-quarter report, the first chance for the business, not the price, to settle the question. GitLab has not announced the date.

The key risk: the rebound has no news under it, any more than the drop did. GitLab is back near $55, where it has twice pushed through in the morning and fallen back by the close, and still below Monday's $56.01 close. A third failure there would make Tuesday look like more than one bad afternoon.

Tuesday's sellers needed 20 minutes. Wednesday's buyers needed 11. The Momentum Len5 still needs a close above $57.89.

One early write-up offered two causes. Neither fits the timing.

The first is a security flaw. On Monday, October 12, GitLab released a fix for a flaw it rated 10 out of 10 for severity. No attacks using the flaw had been confirmed, Help Net Security, a cybersecurity news site, reported Tuesday. The stock set its high in Tuesday's first 20 minutes, with the fix already public. The second is insider selling. The latest insider sale on record is a planned sale of 49,936 shares by a company officer, set for Friday, October 9, under a plan adopted in October 2025. That is about half of one percent of Tuesday's volume (arithmetic), and it came two trading days earlier.

No outlet had confirmed a cause by early Wednesday. The card said the climb did not rest on a few big orders. Tuesday's last 20 minutes look like the reverse: a lot of stock sold in a hurry, with no news attached. That is a reading of the prices, not a reported cause.

It has happened before:

- Tuesday: high $57.89, close $51.95.

Both times, buyers pushed GitLab past $55 and could not keep it there until the close.

- Since September 11: +10.6%, vs +19.2% on the card.
- Since July 13: +55.2%.
- Since April 13: +159.4%.

Tuesday took the near-the-high half. What would knock GitLab off the Momentum Len5: a close under $46.99, where it stood on September 11, which would wipe out the past month's climb. It sits on none of the other five, and the quarterly loss the card cited still keeps it off the Quality Len5.

What comes next:

- The October-quarter report, tentatively Tuesday, December 1, after the close; GitLab has not announced the date. The first line to read: sales against its own $281M-$283M forecast.

The risk: a drop with no news gives no date to wait for. Until December, only the price can say whether Tuesday was a few sellers in a hurry or the start of a longer slide.

No news came with Tuesday's drop, so it is not yet a verdict on GitLab's business. A close under $46.99 would make it a verdict on the climb.

Momentum is the only Len5 GitLab sits on; the $36.8M it lost in the quarter under standard accounting rules out the Quality Len5, which wants a profitable business. text:
"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.
1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.
1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.
1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.
Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.
Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.
Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.
Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.
Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.
Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.
Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.
Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.
I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.
So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.
And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."

text:
October 15, 1914: Appeal Made By Leo Frank For New Trial Turned Down By Georgia Supreme Court 

Reading Time: 9 minutes, [1439 words]

The Atlanta Constitution, Thursday, 15th October 1914, PAGE 1, COLUMN 3 AND 4.

With All Justices Concurring, Highest Court Tribunal Hands Down Opinion Denying Motion Based on Newly Discovered Grounds. Leo M. Frank, convicted of the murder of Mary Phagan, yesterday lost another point in his fight for liberty when the Supreme Court handed down an opinion denying his motion for a new trial on the ground of newly-discovered evidence. Frank's last stand in the courts will be based on the motion to set aside the verdict on constitutional grounds. This motion was carried to the Supreme Court several months ago at the same time the extraordinary motion was made. It will be argued before the Supreme Court justices October 26. This is the second time the Supreme Court has refused to interfere in the Frank case. The first motion carried before that tribunal was that for a new trial founded on the plea that Frank's trial had been misconducted and was influenced by mob element.

Last Stand in Court. The motion before the Supreme Court, based on constitutional grounds, was presented by John L. Tye, of the law firm of Tye, Peeples & Jordan. It was carried before Judge Ben Hill, of the criminal division of Superior Court, for a hearing. Solicitor Dorsey, instead of fighting the motion directly, filed a demurrer in rebuttal. Judge Hill upheld the demurrer, permitting the motion to go up to the Supreme Court by this route. Solicitor Dorsey's demurrer was based on the ground that the motion had not been filed at the proper time in accordance with time-honored practice. It was on this ground that Judge Hill acted. Therefore, if the Supreme Court upon coming to a decision on the constitutional motion holds the defense and grants a new hearing, the case will be sent back to Judge Hill for a second trial. Then the solicitor general would have to combat the motion directly. In the event the Supreme Court grants a new hearing it may go back to the Supreme Court again. For should Judge Hill deny it, Frank's defense will be permitted to send the motion right back to the same tribunal.

Motion Is Overruled. In ruling on the extraordinary motion, the Supreme Court has this to say: "An extraordinary motion for a new trial on the ground of newly-discovered evidence is addressed to the sound discretion of the trial judge and a refusal to grant it will not be reversed unless such discretion is abused. On the hearing of such a motion the court may hear affidavits making a counter showing on behalf of the state, so as to go to the bottom of the showing and show, if possible, how much of real substance and merit there is in the alleged new evidence." The John L. Tye motion is based entirely on the constitutional ground that Frank's personal rights were taken from him when he was not present when the verdict was received against him. It is the one phase of the case on which his counsel expects to carry their battle to the Supreme Court of the United States if necessary.

Ruling of Court. That ruling of the Supreme Court Wednesday, in full, follows: "32 Criminal, March T., 1914. Frank v. State." "1. After a person accused of crime has been convicted and a new trial has been affirmed by this court, an extraordinary motion for a new trial on the ground of newly-discovered evidence is addressed to the sound discretion of the trial judge (there being certain general rules as to evidence of particular kinds, and as diligence, etc.), and a refusal to grant a new trial on such a motion, will not be reversed unless such discretion is abused." "In view of the nature of the alleged newly-discovered evidence on the basis of which an extraordinary motion for a new trial was made in the present case, and of the strong counter showing made by the state in regard to it, there was no abuse of discretion on the part of the trial judge in refusing to grant a new trial; nor was there error in overruling the motion on any of the grounds set out therein." "Leo M. Frank was indicted for the murder of Mary Phagan and was found guilty. He moved for a new trial on numerous grounds. Among them was the ground that the verdict was contrary to law and the evidence, as well as attacks on various rulings of the trial court. This motion was heard by the judge before whom the trial took place. It invoked a decision from him both as to whether he had committed any error of law which required a new trial, and also, whether, in the exercise of a sound discretion under the facts of the case, he should grant a new trial.

New Evidence Offered. "He overruled the motion for a new trial. The case was brought to the Supreme Court by a Bill of Exceptions, where the judgment was affirmed, 141 Ga., 243. A rehearing in the Supreme Court was asked and denied. After this the defendant made what is termed an extraordinary motion for a new trial under a civil code (1910), sections 6089, 6092, based on the ground of newly-discovered evidence. The first cited of these two sections discloses that, 'all applications for a new trial, except in extraordinary cases, must be made during the term at which the trial was held,' etc. The latter of the two sections provides, among other things, that, 'whenever a motion for a new trial shall have been made at the term of trial in any criminal case in this state, and overruled, or when a motion for a new trial has not been made at such term, in either event no motion for a new trial from the same verdict shall ever be made or received, unless the same be an extraordinary motion, or case, such as is provided for in section 6089 of this code.'" "On the hearing of the application a number of affidavits were introduced for the purpose of sustaining the motion. On behalf of the state a vigorous counter-showing was made. This extraordinary motion was heard before a different trial judge than the one who had previously overruled the first motion for a new trial. After hearing evidence on behalf of the movant and the state, the judge overruled the extraordinary motion. The case has again been brought to this court by a Bill of Exceptions assigning error on that judgment."

Brown Case Cited. "The statutory expression, 'an extraordinary motion or case,' the nature of such a motion and the discretionary power of the trial judge who passed upon it, have been so recently considered in Brown v. State, 141 Ga., 783, that it is not necessary to enter into a discussion of them here. Omitting numbering, the first two headnotes of that case read as follows: 'After one accused of crime has been convicted, and has made a motion for a new trial, and the judgment denying it has been affirmed by this court, when an extraordinary motion for a new trial is made, based on the ground of newly-discovered evidence, it should be made to appear that such evidence is so material that it would probably produce a different verdict. An extraordinary motion for a new trial on the grounds of newly-discovered evidence is addressed to the sound discretion of the trial judge, and a refusal to grant it will not be reversed unless such discretion is abused. On the hearing of such a motion, the court may hear affidavits making a counter-showing on behalf of the state, so as to go to the bottom of the showing and discover, if possible, how much of real substance and merit there is in the alleged new evidence.'" "We deem it unnecessary to take up each of the grounds of the motion and discuss them separately; in the light of the evidence offered in support of them, it cannot be held that the discretion of the presiding judge, in refusing to grant the extraordinary motion, was abused, or that a case is made requiring a reversal."In addition to the case above cited, see in this connection Civil Code (1910) sections 6085, 6086; Mithechell v. White, 74 Ga., 327 (5); Clark v. State, 117 Ga. 254 (8); Jenks v. State, 117 Ga. 714; Duggan v. State, 124 Ga., 438 (1); Burge v. State, 133 Ga. 431; Norman v. Goode, 121 Ga., 449.

Judgment affirmed. All the justices concur.

Neri received a blood transfusion at a local hospital before being airlifted to Albany Medical Center for emergency surgery.

text:
In January 2024, House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan and the Weaponization Subcommittee released documents showing that FinCEN (Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network) distributed materials to banks after January 6, 2021. These included suggested search terms and indicators for potential “lone actor/homegrown violent extremism.”
•  Flagged items included transactions involving the terms “MAGA” or “Trump” (e.g., in Zelle messages), purchases of “books (including religious texts)” that could contain “extremist views,” and shopping at retailers such as Bass Pro Shops, Cabela’s, and Dick’s Sporting Goods.
•  These were tied to merchant category codes related to sporting/recreational goods and small arms, in the context of identifying possible persons of interest.
•  Jordan publicly summarized it: “What was also flagged? If you bought a religious text, like a BIBLE, or shopped at Bass Pro Shop.” Fox News and other outlets covered the documents and the accompanying graphics of keyword/MCC lists extensively.
This was not a publicly released roster of every Bible or Bass Pro customer, but guidance for banks to flag and potentially share transaction data with law enforcement for further review. Later FOIA responses indicated that related data was collected for law-enforcement purposes. Critics described it as broad surveillance of protected political and religious activity; supporters framed it as part of post-January 6 extremism investigations.
Parents at school board meetings
In fall 2021, the National School Boards Association sent a letter to the White House comparing some parent conduct at school board meetings (over COVID policies, curricula, etc.) to “domestic terrorism.” Attorney General Merrick Garland issued a memo directing the FBI and U.S. Attorneys to coordinate on threats against school officials.
•  The FBI opened about 25 “Guardian assessments” (preliminary reviews of tips) related to these threats. Six involved the Counterterrorism Division; others went to criminal or other units.
•  Whistleblower accounts and later reporting described specific cases, including one mother investigated in part because she was a gun owner and associated with a group characterized as a “right-wing mom’s group” (linked to Moms for Liberty).
•  Internal DOJ and FBI officials objected in writing, with comments such as “this is ridiculous,” warnings about political motivation, First Amendment concerns, and the lack of a clear federal basis. No federal prosecutions of parents resulted from these assessments.
•  A 2023 House Judiciary interim report concluded there was “no legitimate basis” for the broad use of counterterrorism resources. A 2026 DOJ Weaponization Working Group report (under the subsequent administration) reviewed the episode, confirmed the 25 assessments, noted White House coordination and internal objections, and described the effort as lacking a legitimate enforcement foundation. It has offered affected parents opportunities to review their files and formal apologies in appropriate cases.
Broader context
These episodes sit alongside other documented data-collection efforts (such as the Arctic Frost investigation’s acquisition of personal information on large numbers of Republican donors and MAGA merchandise buyers). Congressional oversight, FOIA materials, and news reporting (including Fox News coverage of the FinCEN materials and related lists/guidance) form the primary public record. The actions occurred in the framework of extremism and threat investigations, but the scope, the inclusion of ordinary commercial and religious activity, internal dissent, and the absence of resulting prosecutions in the parent cases have been cited as evidence of overreach or politicization.
Primary sources include the House Judiciary/Weaponization Subcommittee letters and reports, FinCEN-related documents, the NSBA letter, Garland’s memo, and subsequent DOJ reviews.

In the days before President Lyndon Baines Johnson, black Republicans were a thing. And chief among them was Samuel B. Fuller. Fuller was a black American entrepreneur in the mid-Century United States. More than just an entrepreneur, he also gave back to the black community by providing both inspirational speeches as well as nuts-and-bolts training at a time when entrepreneurially minded black Americans had precious few options for either. Some entrepreneurs trained or inspired by Fuller include John H. Johnson of Johnson Publishing and George Ellis Johnson of Johnson Products.

To say that Fuller came from “humble beginnings” is a bit of an understatement. He was born into a family of Louisiana sharecroppers who were so poor that he had to drop out of school to work in the sixth grade. But he also displayed an entrepreneurial spirit from a very young age. The young Master Fuller was going door-to-door selling products at the age of nine.

When he was 15, his family moved to Nashville. It was here that his mother passed away two years later, leaving Fuller in charge of his six siblings. Relief organizations came by to offer assistance, but Fuller turned them down because he didn’t want his neighbors to think his family couldn’t make it without handouts. It was then that he and his siblings made the decision that they were going to make it on their own without any external help.

The road to success was not an easy one for Fuller. He relocated to Chicago where he took a series of backbreaking, menial jobs, before rising up to become the manager of a coal yard. During the Depression, he was working as an insurance agent at the Commonwealth Burial Association, a black-owned firm. Despite having a secure position at that company, he decided to strike out on his own and build his own business.

Have a listen to learn more about S.B. Fuller’s inspiring life. You can also read Sam’s full article “S.B. Fuller: The Forgotten History of a Legendary Black American Entrepreneur” in https://t.co/NNJc5aP7vR: https://t.co/mySyeh8arb

text:
LET US EXTEND A HELPING HAND TO OUR TEMPLE PRIESTS 
Just pause for a minute… and open your heart.
We go to a temple.
We have Darshan of Swami.
We perform Archana.
We offer Abhishekam.
We put our offerings into the Hundi.
We pray for our family… our health… our children's future… our prosperity.
But…
Do we ever stop and think about the person who stands behind that Sanctum every single day?
The Kurukkal…
The person who wakes up before sunrise…
Who opens the temple doors…
Who cleans the Sanctum…
Who lights the lamp…
Who rings the bell…
Who chants the Mantras…
Who performs Abhishekam…
Who prepares and offers Naivedyam…
And who, with folded hands, prays for our families before Swami.
And then…
He goes back home.
Perhaps to a house with a leaking roof.
Perhaps to an empty kitchen.
Perhaps to medicines that need to be purchased.
Perhaps to a child's school fees waiting to be paid.
Perhaps to an ageing wife who needs treatment.
Perhaps to his own tired and ageing body.
Yet the next morning, he is back again.
Because there is one thought in his heart:
“Swami's Puja must never stop.”
Especially in the small, interior villages of Tamil Nadu, there are temples where only a handful of devotees visit.
There may be little income.
There may be no regular support.
There may be almost no facilities.
But…
THE PUJA CONTINUES.
The lamp continues to burn.
The bell continues to ring.
The Mantras continue to echo.
Because one Kurukkal refuses to abandon his Kainkaryam.
Sometimes, he may not even know where his next month's income will come from.
But he knows one thing:
Swami must be worshipped.
That is his dedication.
That is his Dharma.
That is his Kainkaryam.
And perhaps…
we can become the support that he desperately needs.
We can provide groceries for a month.
We can provide oil for the temple lamp and Abhishekam.
We can provide Puja materials.
We can help with medical expenses.
We can support a child's education.
We can repair a small portion of a damaged priest's house.
 We can help with an urgent family need.
It may be only a few hundred rupees for us.
But for them…
it may mean food for a family.
It may mean medicine for an elderly priest.
It may mean a child's school fee being paid.
It may mean a lamp continuing to burn.
And above all…
It may tell a Kurukkal:
“You are not alone. We are with you.”
We go to the temple to receive blessings from Swami.
They remain in the temple to serve Swami.
Let us therefore serve those who serve Him.
 The lamp they light should never go out because of poverty.
The daily Puja should never stop because the Kurukkal has no means to survive.
A family that has dedicated its life to Swami should never feel forgotten.
Remember…
Protecting a temple is not merely about protecting its walls, Gopuram or Vimanam.
A temple can have a magnificent Gopuram.
It can have a newly renovated Sanctum.
It can have beautiful stonework.
But…
Who will perform the Nitya Puja if there is no Kurukkal?
Who will light the lamp?
Who will chant the Mantras?
Who will offer Naivedyam?
Who will stand before Swami and pray for us?
That is why…

KURUKKAL FIRST… 
TEMPLE NEXT...

Let us wipe away a Kurukkal's tears.
Let us reduce a family's burden.
Let us support a child's education.
Let us help an elderly priest obtain medical treatment.
Let us put groceries into an empty kitchen.
Let us put oil into a temple lamp.
Let us ensure that the Nitya Puja continues without interruption.
This is not charity alone.
This is Kainkaryam.
This is Dharma.
This is our responsibility towards our Sanatana heritage.
We seek Swami's blessings every day.
Let us also remember the person who stands before Swami every day seeking nothing for himself, but praying for all of us.
A small contribution from us can become a great support in his life.
Let us not wait for them to ask.
Let us reach them before they are forced to give up.
Save Our Priests.
Support Our Kurukkals.
Keep the Nitya Puja Alive.
Let the Temple Lamp Continue to Burn.

text:
Illinois State engineering student Isaiah Kerr is researching how small changes in design can make mechanical components stronger and safer.

As the College of Engineering's first FIREbird grant recipient, Kerr worked with Dr. Hafizur Rahman to test different notch designs using 3D-printed components and computer simulations.

“I planned to do research at some point in my college career,” said Kerr, a mechanical engineering major from Normal. “I didn’t think I would get the opportunity until I was in my third or fourth year. So when Dr. Rahman offered me this opportunity, I accepted, because I was like, ‘Oh, I like this. This is manufacturing. It’s what I want to do.’”

Computational analysis showed that replacing sharp-edged notches with rounded geometries, or implementing a patterned notch configuration instead of a single notch, reduced maximum von Mises stress by approximately 40%. Experimental analyses further showed a nearly 25% enhancement in load-bearing capability.

“These findings suggest that careful geometric design, particularly the use of curvature at stress risers, can substantially enhance structural performance and delay failure under applied loads,” Kerr’s research abstract states.

Read the latest issue of #RedbirdScholar to learn how Kerr is gaining hands-on research experience as Illinois State’s engineering program takes shape: https://t.co/hFWiME1mkG

October 15, 2026 • Version 1 • All share prices in USD

FROZEN PRICE SNAPSHOT: $733.93 at 8:14:54 AM PDT / 11:14:54 AM EDT.
Market data retrieved at 8:14:55 AM PDT. This is a saved regular-session observation, not a streaming quote or executable bid/ask. Daily indicators use completed sessions through October 14. [1–2]

THE CALL
Directional preference: cautiously bullish on the underlying trend, with mixed money-flow confirmation. My preferred new-position plan waits for a reclaim and successful retest above roughly $743. I would not buy merely because today's price has rebounded from its morning low. The October 21 earnings release, AI capital spending and the expected Q3 legal charge make near-term sizing and entry discipline more important than a simple bullish label.

META is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages, with the averages ordered positively. However, completed 20-day CMF is slightly negative and MFI is near neutral. Positive OBV supports the trend but does not prove institutions are buying. Today's intraday volume data failed an internal consistency check; it is excluded from trade confirmation.

For a fresh long-term investment, my preference is to see the earnings/cash outlook before committing a full allocation. An existing position and a new entry can reasonably have different decisions. No trades have been placed.

An earlier finance feed showed $732.48 at 7:58:51 AM PDT, with a different opening price and low. This report consistently uses the later saved Yahoo chart snapshot, while retaining the discrepancy as a data limitation. The daily endpoint's chartPreviousClose is a one-year chart reference, not yesterday's close. The actual October 14 daily close and intraday previousClose agree at $737.54. [1–2]

Price references from the saved daily history:

$730.88: completed 20-day simple moving average, close to the current price.

The averages support a positive broader trend, but the recent rejection from $762–771 and loss of yesterday's low are a warning against indiscriminate chasing. These levels are zones to observe, not promises of support or future execution.

2. MARKET MONEY FLOW: A POSITIVE TREND WITHOUT CLEAN AGREEMENT

Calculated from 251 completed daily bars through October 14:

20-day Chaikin Money Flow (CMF)             -0.0547
5-day CMF                                  +0.0483
14-day Money Flow Index (MFI)                48.92
14-day Wilder RSI                           58.10
OBV change, five sessions                   +2.8000 million signed shares
OBV change, twenty sessions                 +42.6891 million signed shares
20-session average daily volume             22.0709 million shares
October 14 volume                           16.1276 million / 0.73x that average
Five-session price change                   +2.25%, excluding dividends
Twenty-session price change                 +9.54%, excluding dividends
14-day Wilder ATR                           $24.19 / 3.28% of prior close
20 / 50 / 200-day SMA                        $730.88 / $649.89 / $631.37

Interpretation: momentum and cumulative up-day volume support the advance. But the small negative 20-day CMF indicates closes have not consistently stayed near the top of their daily ranges after weighting volume. Five-day CMF is only modestly positive; MFI is essentially neutral. This is mixed evidence, not a strong accumulation signal.

OBV and CMF can disagree without either calculation being wrong. OBV assigns all daily volume a sign based on the direction of the close versus yesterday. CMF uses the close's position inside that day's high-low range. A stock can rise versus the prior close and still close near its own intraday low. That distinction matters after large gaps and volatile sessions.

These measures do not identify institutions, insiders or aggressive order flow. Signed OBV shares are not net shares entering the company, and CMF is not actual dollars of fund inflow. Every trade has both a buyer and seller. No authenticated options sweep tape, dark-pool flow, current borrow feed or same-day institutional allocation data was obtained; no whale-buying or short-squeeze claim is made.

Intraday quality check — IMPORTANT LIMITATION:
The first twenty completed five-minute bars, 6:30–8:10 AM PDT, sum to 10,017,932 shares. The same endpoint reports only 5,363,509 cumulative session shares at the later 8:14:54 AM timestamp. That is inconsistent: the completed subset is approximately 1.87 times the later reported total.

The raw comparison would produce 1.23x the first-100-minute volume average of the previous four sessions and a $730.69 sampled VWAP proxy. BOTH are marked diagnostic only and rejected for trading confirmation. I cannot establish which aggregation is reliable from these responses. The script preserves this rejection in META-calculations.json. Do not use those raw figures to claim today's buying pressure is confirmed. Obtain a fresh, internally consistent broker or exchange feed before acting; today is also unfinished, so comparing partial volume with a full-session average would be misleading. [2]

3. OPERATING BUSINESS: STRONG AD DEMAND, LOWER CASH CONVERSION

Meta's July 29 Q2 release reported $60.801 billion revenue, up 28%; operating income $18.775 billion, down 8%; a 31% operating margin versus 43%; and diluted EPS $6.18, down 13%. Costs included $2.40 billion of legal charges and $1.18 billion severance. Ad impressions rose 14%, average ad pricing 12%, and Family daily active people reached 3.60 billion. [3]

July's outlook was Q3 revenue $61–64 billion, full-year expenses $165–169 billion, and capex including finance-lease principal $130–145 billion. Q2 weighted-average diluted shares were 2.566 billion. Q2 operating cash flow was $31.862 billion; property/equipment purchases were $30.116 billion and finance-lease principal $0.962 billion, leaving $0.784 billion FCF versus $8.549 billion a year earlier. [3]

My interpretation: AI can improve engagement, recommendations and advertiser returns while simultaneously making the business more capital intensive. Revenue growth alone does not establish attractive incremental shareholder returns. The ad-impression and pricing percentages are not simply additive; their populations, mix and measurement differ. Do not mechanically call them a 26% revenue formula.

Own arithmetic: Q2 capital outlays in the company's FCF definition consumed about 97.5% of operating cash flow. FCF was about 1.3% of revenue and fell approximately 90.8% year over year. That does not erase the advertising franchise's earnings power, but it makes free-cash-flow conversion a central valuation question. Building capacity today may support growth later; it also creates depreciation, maintenance and financing obligations.

4. CORPORATE MONEY FLOW: WHERE THE CASH WENT

H1 SEC cash-flow figures, billions of dollars:
Operating cash flow                          64.088
Property/equipment purchases                (49.113)
Finance-lease principal                       (1.805)
Calculated company-definition FCF             13.170
Dividends and equivalents paid                 (2.70, rounded)
Net proceeds from May debt issuance             24.91, rounded
RSU-related tax-withholding cash payments       (8.70, rounded)
Share-based compensation expense                13.69, rounded

The filing reports no H1 share repurchases. June-end cash and marketable securities were $90.26 billion, versus $83.66 billion long-term debt; another $10.80 billion was restricted infrastructure-related cash. H1 income benefited from an $8.03 billion discrete Q1 tax item. Uncommenced lease obligations were approximately $278.99 billion, with another approximately $68 billion of leases entered in July. [4]

Own calculations and interpretation: H1 FCF equals $64.088B minus $49.113B minus $1.805B. After rounded dividends, about $10.47 billion remained before RSU withholding, other financing, investments and other cash uses. This is not a complete cash bridge. Cash-flow addbacks for stock compensation do not make that compensation free to shareholders; dilution and withholding deserve separate attention. Do not count employee tax withholding as an open-market buyback.

The roughly $6.60 billion cash/securities-minus-long-term-debt difference is a narrow comparison, not proof Meta has little financial burden. Leases, restricted cash, taxes and contractual commitments are different categories. Long-dated commitments should not all be labeled debt due today, nor simply added together without checking overlap, but they limit future flexibility. A rising cash balance funded partly with new debt is different from an equally large balance built entirely from retained free cash flow.

5. AUGUST LEGAL UPDATE CHANGES THE JULY BASELINE

Meta's August 26 announcement, updated August 27 after judicial approval, states that it expects approximately $10 billion of Q3 legal expense related to its state-attorneys-general agreement. The company explicitly says this was not in the Q2 expense range; otherwise July guidance ranges remained unchanged in that update. [5]

Therefore $165–169 billion should NOT be presented as an untouched current all-in expense baseline. Adding the expected charge gives a rough $175–179 billion arithmetic bridge, not a newly quoted formal range. The final Q3 accounting and any new guidance still need verification at earnings. Do not subtract the full charge from Q3 cash flow as if expense recognition and cash payment occur simultaneously.

The issuer describes an approximately $18 billion payment structure over ten years with conditional components. The Illinois attorney general's announcement describes up to $17.1 billion. This scan does not reconcile those differently stated totals or assume either is an immediate payment; use the final agreement and subsequent company filing for exact obligations. The expected $10 billion Q3 expense disclosure is the more direct near-term earnings input. [5–6]

My investment implication: legal settlements can reduce some uncertainty while still imposing cash obligations, compliance costs and product constraints. Youth engagement restrictions could affect future monetization, but no reliable dollar impact is established here. The agreement does not resolve every regulatory, privacy or competition risk facing Meta.

6. NEW AI CATALYSTS AND THE NEXT EARNINGS TEST

September 28: Meta announced its Enterprise Platform, led by Chirantan “CJ” Desai, including business-facing agents and developer services. This expands the potential addressable business beyond advertising, but the announcement does not establish a mature earnings stream. [7]

October 12, updated October 13: Meta announced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, with developer/subscription availability. Those releases create monetization opportunities and operating costs. Model capability claims are issuer claims, not independent proof of future financial returns. [8]

October 21: Meta confirms Q3 results after market close and a call at 1:30 PM PDT / 4:30 PM EDT. Q3 actual results were not yet released in the sources reviewed for this October 15 scan. [9]

My earnings checklist:
• Revenue and ad pricing versus the $61–64 billion company range.
• The actual legal charge, its tax treatment and cash-payment schedule.
• Capex, depreciation, finance leases and any shift to external financing.
• Operating cash generation after working-capital effects and FCF conversion.
• Evidence of paid AI adoption and advertiser returns, separated from launch claims.
• Stock compensation, share count and whether buybacks actually resume.
• Expense discipline and the updated outlook after legal and infrastructure costs.

7. VALUATION: WHAT MUST BE EARNED AT THIS PRICE

The latest September 10 dividend declaration was $0.525 quarterly, payable September 28 to September 21 record holders. Annualizing that declared rate gives $2.10, or about 0.29% at $733.93. Future dividends require board approval; the indicated yield provides little offset to a large price drawdown. [10]

At the saved price, the Q2 diluted share-count proxy of 2.566 billion implies approximately $1.883 trillion of equity value. This is a constructed diluted-value proxy, not today's actual shares outstanding or a live market-cap quote. Annualizing Q2's reported $6.18 EPS produces $24.72 and about 29.7x that simplistic run rate. It is NOT a proper forward or trailing P/E estimate: the legal charges and discrete tax effects make mechanical annualization unreliable.

For perspective, illustrative normalized annual EPS × assumed P/E gives:
Bear: $25 × 20 = $500 per share.
Base: $30 × 25 = $750 per share.
Bull: $35 × 28 = $980 per share.

These are my sensitivity assumptions for a possible 12–24-month operating outcome, not consensus, issuer guidance, a full earnings forecast, price targets with assigned probabilities or guaranteed fair values. The base case gives little margin against the snapshot price; the bull case requires both stronger earnings and a premium multiple. A business can grow while its stock falls if the paid multiple compresses.

I would not use a single quarter's depressed FCF to declare the company worthless, or remove all investment spending to manufacture cheapness. The useful question is how much cash shareholders can ultimately receive after necessary reinvestment and dilution. The present information does not establish a precise normalized maintenance-capex figure.

8. CONDITIONAL PRICE STRATEGIES AND POSITION RISK

Preferred reclaim plan: wait for sustained trading above $743 and a successful retest, using fresh, consistent volume/quote data. Example entry $744, stop/invalidation reference $729: $15 nominal share risk. The first resistance objective, $761.50, offers $17.50 / 1.17R; the wider $779.82 objective offers $35.82 / 2.39R. The first objective alone is not attractive enough to justify chasing. Scaling out there lowers the blended payoff; it should not be advertised as if every share earns 2.39R. Failure to hold the reclaim cancels the setup.

Pullback alternative: watch $715–720 and the $711.68 low for stabilization, followed by a reclaim. Example entry $720 only after recovery evidence, stop reference $707: $13 risk. Objectives $743 and $761.50 offer about 1.77R and 3.19R. Entering blindly during a falling session is not this setup. A clean loss of $711.68 weakens the pullback thesis and argues for reassessment rather than automatic averaging down.

Bearish contingency: a confirmed break and failed retest below $711.68 would damage the recent structure. Example short entry $710, stop $726, first objective $680 and wider reference $660.80 gives $16 risk, approximately 1.88R and 3.08R. The $680 objective is a chosen intermediate planning level; $660.80 comes from observed history. Shorting requires available borrow, carries fees and potentially unlimited loss. A long-only investor can instead cut tactical exposure or remain in cash if the bullish conditions fail.

For a hypothetical $10,000 trading account with a chosen $50 planned loss budget, floor($50 / $15) gives 3 shares for the reclaim example: $45 nominal stop risk and $2,232 gross entry value. This is an arithmetic illustration, not your account or an allocation recommendation. Stops do not guarantee execution prices. The $15 stop is only about 0.62 of the $24.19 daily ATR; wider volatility-based stops would require smaller size or no trade.

Event plan: a short-term position should have an explicit decision to exit before October 21 earnings or accept an overnight gap at reduced size. A stop order cannot cap the loss through an earnings gap. For longer-term investing, consider staged purchases only after the cash outlook and valuation support the thesis. No option premiums, implied volatility, bid/ask depth or borrow availability were verified, so this report does not invent an executable options spread or real fill.

9. METHODS, SOURCE TRAIL AND ARTWORK

Daily calculations use unadjusted OHLC and volume, excluding October 15; reported returns exclude dividends. CMF(n) sums volume × (2×close−high−low)/(high−low), divided by total volume; zero-range bars contribute zero numerator. MFI uses fourteen sessions of typical price × volume signed by the typical-price change. OBV signs volume by close-to-close direction. RSI and ATR use fourteen-period Wilder smoothing, seeded from the first fourteen changes/ranges in the saved 251-session history. SMA is the arithmetic close average. The five-minute VWAP calculation uses typical-price weighting and is retained as rejected diagnostic output because of the volume conflict.

Heavenly Father, Almighty God,

We come before You today with heavy, grieving hearts as we bring before Your throne of grace the heartbreaking tragedy in Peshawar. Lord, our souls mourn for the innocent young lives lost, for the teacher who stood by them, and for the families whose homes and hearts are now shattered by unimaginable grief.

In the midst of this darkness, confusion, and sorrow, we ask for Your divine comfort to envelope every parent, sibling, and loved one weeping in northwestern Pakistan. Lord Jesus, You told us, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted." We pray that Your Holy Spirit, the divine Comforter, draws near to these families, wrapping them in Your supernatural peace that surpasses all human understanding.

We pray over the ongoing search and rescue efforts. Lord, grant strength, swiftness, and wisdom to the rescue personnel digging through the rubble. Protect the children who remain trapped—hold them close, keep them brave, and lead rescuers to bring them out safely. We ask for Your healing touch upon every child and adult currently in critical condition at Lady Reading Hospital and surrounding care centers. Lord, guide the hands of the doctors and medical staff, restoring these young bodies to full health and strength.

Father, as we confront the fragility of human life and the painful reality of a broken world, our hearts look to the hope found only in Your Son, Jesus Christ. We thank You that even in our darkest hours, You offer us the ultimate message of salvation. You sent Your only begotten Son into the world not to condemn us, but so that through faith in Him, we might have eternal life.

In southern Syria, Israeli forces have seized the Syrian side of Mount Hermon, a commanding vantage point overlooking Damascus, Beirut, and the entire Galilee region. Israeli Defense Minister Katz has openly declared: "The summit of Mount Hermon is now under Israeli control."

Israel is establishing military outposts across the provinces of Daraa, Quneitra, and Rural Damascus. text:
On October 15, 1860, 11-year-old Grace Bedell of Westfield, New York, wrote a letter to presidential candidate Abraham Lincoln suggesting he grow a beard. 
---Grace Greenwood Billings (née Bedell; November 4, 1848 – November 2, 1936) was an American woman, notable as a person whose correspondence, at the age of eleven, encouraged Republican Party nominee and future president Abraham Lincoln to grow a beard. Lincoln later met with Bedell during his inaugural journey in February 1861.
---Lincoln responded to her letter, and though he did not promise to follow her advice, he began growing his famous beard shortly after. 
---The letter: Bedell was prompted to write to Lincoln after her father brought home a campaign portrait of him and his running mate, Hannibal Hamlin. She felt that Lincoln's face looked too thin in the picture. 
---In her letter, Bedell offered her opinion and laid out her political strategy: 
-------A better look: "You would look a great deal better, for your face is so thin".
-------Voter influence: "All the ladies like whiskers and they would tease their husbands to vote for you and then you would be President".
-------Family vote: She claimed that while some of her four brothers already planned to vote for him, she would try to get the rest of them to vote for him if he grew a beard. 
---Lincoln's response: Lincoln wrote back to Bedell four days later, on October 19, 1860. In his reply, he wrote, "As to the whiskers, having never worn any, do you not think people would call it a piece of silly affectation if I were to begin it now?". 
---The outcome: Despite his reservation, Lincoln began growing a beard about a month after their exchange, and it was in full growth by the time of his inauguration. 
---On his inaugural train journey to Washington, D.C., in February 1861, Lincoln's train made a stop in Westfield. He asked to meet Bedell, telling a crowd that he had received "a very pretty letter" from a young lady there who advised him to let his whiskers grow. When Bedell was brought forward, Lincoln reportedly said, "You see? I let these whiskers grow for you," and kissed her.
