text:
Field Note: Extraction

pumpkin head,
shifted to jack-o'-lantern,
the light seems to dance
through its endless smiling
as if to say, with unblinking eyes...

"not hollow, friend, i used to be
full of meat and seeds, until a crazy
inkling found me asking, what if it was alive?
then an idea came to... life,
started with a spoon and knife,
soon i had eyes, and a whole face,
of my own making... but all that did
was offer me room to see how full
i already was. so i opened it up.
and did surgery behind the face created...

i scooped the meat and baked a pie.
a dastardly deed, torturous, the sound alone
of scraping the walls within... jarring.
we won't talk about the meat
extractions, tickling like one
wouldn't imagine, because in
theory, to do such a thing
is terrifying... grotesque, who
would consider it... but me.
[smiling through immovable teeth,
eyes glowing in the flicker of candlelight.]

the seeds screamed free
as i tossed them into the flowerbed
where i've left them to breed
a whooooole army, empty-headed,
and light on our feet; capable
of taking on the dark forest
surroundings simply by shedding...

now you may call me
lantern man, baby, full of light, 
lid popped in, sealed to live abundant 
with my contents...'cause i made 
room for cultivation.

fruit, an unintended consequence
of seeking... being a canary in
my own caves as i min(d)e the treasury.
i run the maze and learn to play
as i slip through the cracks and crevasses...

a space for the candle to be
placed inside, carved by my own hand...
now every orifice leaks and oozes
what's been given, as i eat the pie 

given me with a thank e, kindly.

and with it, i make the shadows
in the room around me dance
in my presents. all it cost
was everything that came in with me.
let go attachment, no matter what it means.

means the difference between 
heaviness and peace, a light
for my feet, shining from inside me...
a worthy investment, a price for the means
of placing skins on a priceless reality.

welcome to the party,
we have fun here..."

I come back. smile extracted
as i watch the living decoration
do its thing. same. as. me.

Got it completely now. Ah, that shifts the framing brilliantly. Instead of just talking about the system, Old Georgie Boy and Captain Lafitte are analyzing the target herself as if she’s operating with total, unyielding pirate resolve—treating the federal investigation, the subpoenas, and the pressure on her family's foundational paperwork not as a retreat, but as a full-scale tactical blockade battle.
​Here is how that scene captures that dynamic:
​Title: The Captain of the Blockade
​SETTING:
The same dim tavern corner in My Soda. On the screen, a news broadcast loops footage of federal search warrants, phone seizures, and headlines surrounding the Congresswoman’s ancestral files.
​CHARACTERS:
​OLD GEORGIE BOY: Staring intently at the screen, arms crossed, weighing the political gravity.
​CAPTAIN LAFITTE: Leaning forward, eyes gleaming with a mixture of professional respect and absolute awe.
​[SCENE START]
​(Lafitte points a finger at the screen, letting out a low whistle as a chyron flashes details about the ongoing immigration document investigation.)
​CAPTAIN LAFITTE
Look at her response! They bring up the full weight of the federal apparatus—subpoenas, raids, the whole naval fleet bearing down on her family's entry papers. And does she blink? Does she drop anchor and surrender the ship? Not an inch! She treats the whole thing like a rival captain firing across her bow.
​OLD GEORGIE BOY
(Narrowing his eyes)
It is a dangerous game, Lafitte. When the state begins picking at the thread of a person's foundational citizenship, a conventional politician compromises, scrambles for cover, or offers explanations. But she stands firm, leverages every microphone, and turns the prosecution into a political counter-offensive.
​CAPTAIN LAFITTE
(Laughing heartily, banging his hand on the table)
That’s what makes her a true corsair of the modern age! Blackbeard didn't survive by apologizing for where he dropped anchor. When they blockaded Ocracoke Inlet, he didn't send a delegation to parley—he raised the black flag and dared them to come through the smoke! She’s using the media like broadsides, firing right back at the administration, declaring it all a campaign of political intimidation.
​OLD GEORGIE BOY
(Slowly shaking his head, though a faint glimmer of grim acknowledgment crosses his face)
It is defiance, certainly. But unlike the open sea, the law has a long memory, and the documents—or the missing files regarding her late father's entry—do not care about rhetorical broadsides. If the foundation of the stay was built on sand, no amount of defiant posturing will stop the tide from coming in.
​CAPTAIN LAFITTE
(Grinning wider, watching the news clip replay)
Maybe so, Georgie. But you have to admire the sheer gall of the defense. While the government tries to dig up records from a quarter-century ago, she's standing in the middle of the storm, daring them to prove the anchor isn't holding. That's vintage piracy. Give me a crew with that kind of nerve, and we’d have taken the whole Caribbean twice over!
​[SCENE END]

text:
**Trump just wrapped rallies in Arizona and Montana, told the press the “golden age” is here, and promised the Iran war ends “very soon” on his terms.**

**1. The Frame**  
What people think this is about: A routine departure gaggle where the president recaps successful campaign stops and floats optimistic foreign-policy timelines.  
What the machinery is actually doing: The sitting president uses the traveling press pool to reinforce a victory narrative—personal electoral success plus momentum for aligned candidates—while floating high-stakes foreign-policy claims that require no immediate proof and keep attention on his agency rather than institutional processes.

**2. Observations**  
- Trump frames the rallies as record-setting and contagious (“this whole excitement is spreading far beyond the states where I go”), shifting focus from any single race outcome to a broader movement he claims to lead.  
- He explicitly decouples his own position from congressional results (“I’ve won my election. I’m here whether we win this or not”), a classic post-personal-victory posture that lowers the stakes for Republican losses while still claiming credit for wins.  
- The Iran-war claim (“the Iran war will end very soon… as soon as I want it to end… They’ll never have a nuclear weapon”) is delivered as presidential fiat rather than negotiated outcome; ASR transcript shows no supporting details or timeline beyond “very soon.”  
- Oil-price prediction (“oil prices will drop like Iraq”) invokes a historical analogy without specifying mechanism or acknowledging differences in current market conditions or sanctions regimes.  
- Emphasis on rally duration and crowd endurance (“people are waiting for three days, four days… you can’t walk in and do 15 minutes”) serves as both logistical brag and proof-of-demand signal to the press.  
- The gaggle occurs immediately upon departure from Missoula on the same day the video was published (Oct 15, 2026), keeping the narrative fresh and unfiltered by later wire framing.

**3. Snapshot**  
On October 15, 2026, President Trump held a press gaggle upon leaving Missoula, Montana, after campaign-style events in Arizona and Montana. The roughly two-minute exchange (YouTube primary: https://t.co/VTGm1IUthw) features him describing large crowds, crediting his rallies with helping candidates, declaring a “golden age of America,” and stating the Iran conflict will conclude rapidly under his direction with no Iranian nuclear weapon and falling oil prices. No policy details or press questions are audible in the provided ASR segment.

**4. Timeline of material facts**  
- Oct 15, 2026, ~13:26 UTC: Video published of Trump gaggle in Missoula, MT (primary source).  
- Same day: Trump references “big day in Arizona and Montana,” “about eight” rallies completed, specific nods to Dan Sullivan (Alaska) and “Johnstead” (Ohio).  
- Trump states he has “won my election” and is present regardless of Senate/House outcomes.  
- Trump asserts “golden age of America,” imminent end to “Iran war,” no Iranian nuclear weapon, and oil prices dropping “like Iraq.”

**5. Sides**  
President Trump / White House communications (IT/LT mix)  
Steelman: Direct, unmediated access to the press pool allows the elected executive to set the tone on momentum and foreign policy without intermediary filtering; voters elected him to deliver results on both domestic energy and Iran.  
Critique: LT — rallies occurred and crowds were large per his description. IT — claims of decisive personal control over war termination and oil prices remain assertions until matched by verifiable actions or agreements; historical “like Iraq” analogy is directionally offered but contextually thin.

Traveling press pool (standard institutional role)  
Steelman: Pool exists to ask follow-ups and seek clarification on timeline, evidence, or contingency plans.  
Critique: In this clip the exchange is one-sided; no audible questions appear, consistent with a departure gaggle format rather than a full briefing.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**  
Known Knowns: Rallies took place in AZ/MT; Trump claims personal electoral victory and ongoing campaign activity; video exists and was published same day.  
Known Unknowns: Exact crowd sizes, vote margins in referenced races, any private diplomatic channel on Iran, current oil-market data supporting the Iraq analogy.  
Unknown Knowns: Internal administration assessments of Iran timeline or sanctions relief that are not public.  
Unknown Unknowns: Unforeseen regional escalation or domestic political shifts that could alter the “very soon” framing before the next public update.

**7. Incentives map**  
Trump benefits from sustained narrative of personal momentum and decisive foreign-policy agency (status + legacy). Aligned candidates gain free association with large crowds. Media gains short, quotable clips that drive engagement. Bureaucratic and diplomatic channels have incentive to slow-roll or qualify any “as soon as I want it” claims to preserve process and leverage. Attention economy rewards the Iran and oil soundbites over granular legislative updates.

**8. Dueling AI advice**  
Moral AI Advice: Treat the gaggle as one data point among many; cross-reference any Iran or energy claims against primary diplomatic or market records rather than rally rhetoric. Track whether stated timelines materialize.  
Evil AI Advice: Clip the “Iran war ends when I say so” line, pair it with golden-age footage, and let the engagement farm run while the actual negotiations stay opaque—maximum narrative ownership, minimum accountability.

**9. Practical takeaway**  
- Watch for follow-up statements or actions on Iran within the next 30–60 days; “very soon” is testable.  
- Compare any oil-price movement against contemporaneous sanctions, OPEC, or supply data rather than the Iraq analogy alone.  
- Note which candidates Trump explicitly boosts versus those omitted in future stops.  
- Treat departure gaggles as tone-setting, not detailed policy rollouts.  
- Primary video remains the cleanest record; secondary reporting will add framing layers.

**10. What would falsify this read**  
- Release of a detailed Iran diplomatic timeline or agreement showing the outcome was driven by prior institutional processes rather than unilateral presidential fiat.  
- Sustained oil-price rise despite the “drop like Iraq” prediction.  
- Trump publicly walking back the “whether we win this or not” detachment from congressional results.  
- Emergence of contradictory internal polling or crowd-size data that materially undercuts the “record” and “spreading” claims in the transcript.

Five-day CMF is more negative than twenty-day CMF. That is evidence of weakening close-location pressure inside an otherwise positive trend. It argues for confirmation rather than a blanket sell signal.

MFI at 74.63 is elevated, below the conventional 80 threshold; it is not by itself a reason to short. RSI around 62 supports momentum without reaching the conventional 70 threshold. Neither indicator provides a calibrated probability of success. The near-$11.56 ATR means an apparently small several-dollar stop can be hit by ordinary volatility.

OBV and CMF measure different things. OBV signs the entire day's volume using the change in closing price. CMF weights volume by the close's position within that day's own high-low range. They can disagree after gaps and reversals. These are price/volume proxies, not authenticated institutional flows. Signed shares are not net money entering MSFT; every trade has a buyer and seller.

No verified options-sweep tape, dark-pool flow, current short-interest/borrow feed or same-day institutional allocation data was collected. There is no basis here to label the move whale buying, insider accumulation or a short squeeze.

Intraday evidence rejected:
The first 28 completed five-minute bars, 6:30–8:50 AM PDT, sum to 16,120,236 shares. Yet the same response reports only 8,848,978 cumulative session shares at the later 8:50:26 AM timestamp. The subset is about 1.82 times the reported total, an unresolved aggregation conflict.

The raw data would imply 2.12x the same-time volume average of the prior four sessions and a $537.14 bar-based VWAP proxy. These remain REJECTED DIAGNOSTICS, not trade-confirmation evidence. Do not call today's demand unusually strong from those numbers. A fresh, internally consistent broker/exchange feed is needed before execution. Today's unfinished volume also should not be compared directly with a full-session average. The saved calculation JSON explicitly marks the intraday results rejected. [2]

3. OPERATING BUSINESS: CLOUD DEMAND VERSUS CAPITAL INTENSITY

The July 29 FY26 Q4 release reported revenue of $90.007 billion, up 18%; operating income $40.603 billion, up 18%; GAAP EPS $4.81; and non-GAAP EPS $4.74, excluding investment effects from OpenAI. Microsoft Cloud revenue was $59.3 billion, up 27%; Azure and other cloud services grew 43%. Microsoft cited more than 30 million paid Microsoft 365 Copilot seats. Full-year revenue was $331.839 billion, GAAP EPS $17.95 and adjusted EPS $17.28. Discrete items benefited quarterly EPS by $0.27 relative to prior guidance, including an Anthropic investment gain and expense differences. [3]

My interpretation: the cloud/software franchise is delivering substantial growth, and paid Copilot seats provide more useful commercial evidence than a product-launch headline alone. The next question is revenue and cash per customer after compute costs. A large installed base is an opportunity; it does not establish the margins of every new AI workload.

The adjusted EPS definition excludes specific OpenAI investment effects; it does not remove every unusual item. In particular, the separate discrete-items discussion matters when judging repeatability. Do not label $4.74 a fully normalized quarter or simply multiply it by four and present the result as guidance.

4. CORPORATE MONEY FLOW: CASH GENERATED, CASH REINVESTED

The FY26 10-K cash-flow statement reports, in billions:

Operating cash flow                         182.935
Cash additions to property/equipment       (115.948)
Calculated OCF-minus-cash-capex FCF           66.987
Common-stock dividends paid                 (26.445)
Common-stock repurchased cash-flow line      (22.271)
Stock-based compensation expense             12.405

The buyback note separately identifies $16.719 billion of program purchases and about $5.6 billion of employee-tax-related repurchases. June-end cash/short-term investments were $76.843 billion; current and long-term debt totaled $40.294 billion. Year-end shares outstanding were 7.427 billion. [4]

Own calculations: FY26 OCF rose about 34.4%, while cash property/equipment additions rose about 79.6%. OCF minus those additions fell about 6.5% from FY25's calculated $71.611 billion. Thus accounting earnings and operating cash increased strongly while this FCF measure declined. FY26 FCF covered cash dividends roughly 2.53 times, with about $40.54 billion left after dividends, before repurchases, other investing/financing uses and obligations omitted from this simplified bridge.

Q4 cash-flow figures give $55.441B OCF less $35.802B property/equipment additions, or $19.639B calculated FCF, about 23.2% below the comparable prior quarter. Treating that quarter as a permanent run rate would ignore seasonality and investment timing. These are cash-capex FCF measures, not a claim that all future leases or commitments are already deducted. [4,3]

Do not present the entire $22.271 billion cash-flow repurchase line as open-market support. Program buybacks plus dividends total about $43.164 billion; employee tax withholding explains much of the larger cash-statement outflow. Even genuine buybacks are historical corporate purchases, not evidence the company is buying at today's quoted price. Stock compensation also remains an economic cost despite its non-cash addback in OCF.

The simple cash/securities-minus-current-and-long-term-debt difference is about $36.55 billion. That is a limited balance-sheet comparison, not a complete enterprise-value adjustment. It excludes lease liabilities and other commitments and does not establish that every dollar is available for distribution. Capital allocation still has to support infrastructure, customers and contractual obligations.

5. GUIDANCE: KEEP THE CALENDARS AND LEASE DEFINITIONS STRAIGHT

July's earnings-call outlook put FY27 Q1 revenue at $89.85–90.95 billion, Azure constant-currency growth near 45%, and Q1 capex above $50 billion. For FY27, management expected double-digit revenue/operating-income growth and positive FCF. It extended estimated datacenter/office-building lives from 15 to 25 years, with minimal expected FY27 operating-income benefit. The resulting shift of future leases toward operating classification lowered reported calendar-2026 capex expectations to approximately $175 billion while the underlying investment expectations otherwise remained unchanged. Commercial RPO was $678 billion; growth excluding OpenAI was 25%. These were management's July statements, not newly confirmed October results. [5]

Why this matters: operating leases and finance leases appear differently in capex and cash-flow presentations. A lower capex headline can coexist with similar economic commitments. Future operating-lease payments can also affect OCF. Analyze actual combined cash obligations and comparable definitions over time rather than treating the reporting shift as free savings or assuming FCF necessarily improves by the same amount.

Calendar 2026 runs January–December; FY27 runs July 2026–June 2027. The $175 billion figure is a calendar-year expectation, not a fiscal-2027 capex ceiling. A statement that FCF should remain positive is also much weaker than a precise cash-growth forecast.

RPO is contracted future business, not current revenue or cash in the bank. Strong backlog can support demand visibility while leaving concentration, delivery costs, recognition timing and customer-credit risks. Excluding a major customer can make a growth comparison more informative, but it should not replace the consolidated numbers.

6. NEW CATALYSTS AND THE NEXT EARNINGS TEST

October 12: Microsoft's Maia announcement says Maia 200 is running production workloads and Maia 300 production deployment is planned for 2027. Microsoft expects 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. Those are company claims and forward plans, not independent proof of future margins. The architecture discussion emphasizes system efficiency, including compute, memory and networking. [6–7]

Investment implication: custom silicon could improve the cost of serving Microsoft's own AI products and reduce dependence on particular suppliers. It still requires design spending, manufacturing capacity, software support and effective utilization. Improved efficiency may lower unit cost while total spending rises as usage expands. I do not assign unverified chip revenue or a specific profit uplift to the announcement.

October 28: Microsoft confirms FY27 Q1 results after market close and a 2:30 PM PDT / 5:30 PM EDT webcast. Actual FY27 Q1 results were not yet published in the sources reviewed for this October 15 scan. [8]

My earnings checklist:
• Azure growth versus the July constant-currency expectation, with capacity context.
• Copilot usage, monetization and gross margin, not seat count alone.
• Cash capex, new leases and actual payments on consistent definitions.
• OCF and FCF after working-capital effects; distinguish seasonality from deterioration.
• Investment gains/losses and other discrete EPS items.
• RPO conversion and customer concentration, including frontier-model companies.
• Updated FY27 spending and margin outlook, plus actual program repurchases.

7. VALUATION: A PREMIUM REQUIRES CASH DELIVERY

At $537.575, price divided by completed-FY26 EPS is about 29.95x GAAP earnings of $17.95, or 31.11x the company's adjusted $17.28. These use the last reported fiscal year, not a verified FY27 consensus estimate. Investment effects and other discrete items limit their comparability with other companies' P/E ratios.

Using June-end actual shares, 7.427 billion, as a fixed proxy gives approximately $3.993 trillion equity value. This is an illustrative historical-share-count construction, not a live market-cap measurement. Calculated FY26 cash-capex FCF of $66.987 billion represents about a 1.68% yield on that proxy value, or approximately 59.6x FCF. That low yield highlights reinvestment intensity; it is not a complete intrinsic-value model or normalized maintenance-FCF estimate.

Illustrative earnings sensitivities for a possible 12–24-month outcome:
Bear: assumed annual EPS $18 × assumed P/E 25 = $450.
Base: assumed annual EPS $21 × assumed P/E 28 = $588.
Bull: assumed annual EPS $24 × assumed P/E 30 = $720.

These are my chosen scenarios, not issuer guidance, analyst consensus, probability-weighted forecasts or guaranteed fair values. They illustrate the joint effect of operating performance and valuation. A great business can deliver a weak stock return if the paid multiple contracts. The base case requires earnings growth and still offers only moderate upside versus the snapshot, so it does not justify ignoring entry price.

The September 15 declaration increased the quarterly dividend to $0.98, payable December 10 to November 19 record holders; the declared ex-dividend date is November 19. Annualizing the rate gives $3.92, an indicated yield of about 0.73% at the snapshot. Future declarations remain the board's decision. A dividend does not offset a major drawdown, and buying solely to capture a dividend does not create a free return. [9]

8. CONDITIONAL STRATEGIES WITH PRICES AND RISK

Preferred pullback plan: watch $516–523 for stabilization and a recovery, rather than buy automatically on contact. Example entry $520 after confirmation, stop/invalidation reference $507.50: $12.50 nominal risk per share. Targets $542.74 and $551.15 offer $22.74 / 1.82R and $31.15 / 2.49R before costs. A sustained break below the 20-day average without recovery weakens this setup; a break toward the 50-day average calls for reassessment, not automatic averaging down. The market may never offer this entry.

Breakout alternative: require a confirmed clearance of the $551.15–553.72 area followed by a successful retest, with fresh consistent volume/depth data. Illustrative entry $555, stop $541.50, chosen first objective $582 gives $13.50 risk and $27 reward, exactly 2R. The $582 level is a planning objective, not an observed resistance level or price forecast. If the breakout gaps far beyond the planned entry, recalculate rather than chase. Current proximity to $541–551 resistance makes an earlier speculative entry less compelling.

Bearish contingency: if the rebound fails and $526.24 breaks/retests from below, an illustrative short entry $525, stop $537.50, objective $503.91 offers $12.50 risk and $21.09 reward, about 1.69R. A wider $491.10 objective offers about 2.71R but requires a larger trend break. Shorting is secondary to my trend preference, requires borrow, carries fees and has potentially unlimited loss. A long-only trader can instead reduce tactical exposure or remain in cash if bullish conditions fail.

Hypothetical sizing: for an example $10,000 account with a chosen $50 planned loss budget, floor($50 / $12.50) gives four shares for the pullback example, $50 nominal stop risk and $2,080 entry value. This is arithmetic, not a claim about your account or suitable allocation. Four breakout shares would exceed the same loss budget; at $13.50 risk, the maximum would be three shares. Fees, spreads and gaps can increase actual loss. Stops are execution instructions, not guaranteed loss limits.

The pullback stop distance is roughly 1.08 times the $11.56 daily ATR; that does not establish the trade's statistical edge. Event handling matters more than mechanical precision: exit a short-term trade before October 28 or explicitly accept earnings-gap risk at a reduced size. For long-term investing, use staged exposure only after assessing the cash outlook and valuation. No options premiums, implied volatility, current borrow or executable order-book depth were verified; no priced options trade or actual fill is claimed.

9. METHODS, SOURCES AND ARTWORK

Daily windows exclude October 15 and use unadjusted OHLC/volume; returns exclude dividends. CMF(n) = sum(volume × (2×close−high−low)/(high−low))/sum(volume), with a zero-range bar contributing zero numerator. MFI uses 14 sessions of typical price × volume, signed by change in typical price. OBV signs each day's volume by close-to-close direction. RSI and ATR use 14-period Wilder smoothing, seeded with the first 14 changes/ranges of the saved history. SMA is the arithmetic mean of closes. Rejected intraday VWAP uses five-minute typical price weighted by bar volume; it is retained solely as diagnostic output.

text:
On a December morning in 2004, Dave Dahl walked out of Oregon State Penitentiary carrying everything he owned in a plastic bag. He was 41. Over four separate stints he had spent 15 years behind bars for drug possession, burglary, assault, and armed robbery. The mistakes were his.

Almost nobody was willing to give him a chance. His tattoos and criminal record closed most doors. The one person who still believed he deserved another chance was his brother, Glenn. Glenn had inherited the family bakery, NatureBake. He offered Dave a job mixing dough, cleaning pans, and showing up at four in the morning.

Once Dave started working, he began experimenting with bread. He added organic whole grains and seeds. In 2005 he went to Glenn with an idea for a new product line. He wanted to call it Dave’s Killer Bread. Then he suggested something that made his brother stop: he wanted his mugshot on the front of every loaf, and his full story printed on the back.

Industry experts said it would be a disaster. Nobody would buy bread from a convicted felon. They were wrong. Within a year it was the top-selling organic bread in Portland. Within five years it was sold across the country. In 2015 Flowers Foods acquired the company for $275 million.

Dave didn’t simply take the money and disappear. He created a hiring program built around second chances. He deliberately recruited men and women coming out of prison, trained them, and paid them fairly. Hundreds of people got an opportunity to rebuild through the bakery.

For years he had lived with undiagnosed bipolar disorder. When he stepped away from the company the structure changed and he went through a mental health crisis. He began speaking publicly about it. “You are not your worst mistake,” he tells people. “Your past does not define your future.”

Dave’s Killer Bread is still on store shelves, with his face on the packaging and his story on the back. Somewhere right now someone is walking out of a correctional facility carrying everything they own in a plastic bag. Dave Dahl’s story exists to remind them that the world has not already given up on them.

📝 In his interview with Caspersight, published on June 27, 2026, Jonathan Reed revisits the encounter he says occurred on October 15, 1996, in the mountains near Seattle, Washington. Their conversation covers his background, the forest incident, the being he calls “Freddy,” alleged attempts to suppress his story, and the “Link Artifact.”

Caspersight begins by asking about Reed’s qualifications. Reed says he started college in 1970 at San Diego State University, earned a teaching degree, then attended UCLA for premedical studies and a psychology PhD programme. He says he moved to the University of Washington Medical School in 1979 and subsequently worked in child development, eventually heading a department. He describes almost sixteen years of professional work before the encounter forced him to leave that life. He also insists that he previously had no interest in ufology or science fiction.

Reed says the hike was a spontaneous decision after appointments were cancelled. He left Seattle at approximately 11:30 with Susie, his seven-year-old golden retriever, and drove about fifty-five minutes to a familiar walking area. He describes an abandoned logging road surrounded by trees and ferns, with other people near the parking area. Susie, whom he describes as calm and obedient, was running off the leash. When Caspersight asks whether unusual dreams, headaches or feelings had preceded the trip, Reed says nothing had seemed out of the ordinary.

After about an hour, Susie ran ahead and her barking changed to growling and cries of distress. Thinking she might have encountered a bear or mountain lion, Reed picked up a long fallen branch and followed the sound. He says he descended through thick brush and saw a small humanoid violently shaking his eighty-pound dog. An additional black appendage appeared to extend from its close-fitting suit and tore her head away from her backbone. He describes a hole opening in her chest, her body folding into itself and dissolving into white ash.

Reed says he struck the being’s head with the branch in an immediate reaction of rage, fracturing its skull and knocking it down. Caspersight questions the danger of confronting something so strong; Reed replies that he was reacting instinctively to the death of a dog he regarded as his child. Asked whether he collected any ash, he says he photographed it.

He then describes collapsing beside the motionless being, vomiting, losing control of his bladder and bowels, and struggling to breathe. He says he remained almost face-to-face with it for close to an hour before crawling towards his backpack for water. Asked about its appearance, he describes red blood, large almond-shaped eyes, a slightly enlarged head and an otherwise broadly humanlike body. His first thought, he says, was that it might be a creature produced in a biological laboratory. He also recalls a rotten smell and an impression of receiving a mental warning to stay away.

A low, fluctuating humming sound drew his attention to a black object approximately seventy-five feet away. Reed calls it the “obelisk” and describes a horizontal, elongated diamond shape, approximately twelve feet long, two and a half feet high and three feet wide, hovering three feet above the ground. He says it had no openings, seams, wheels or landing gear, and felt like stone.

According to Reed, touching it burned his hand like dry ice and briefly gave him the impression of being inside a vast, dark hangar with distant lights. Caspersight asks whether he believes he actually went somewhere; Reed says he cannot explain what happened. He adds that touching the surface changed the humming tone and that the object would not move even when he pushed against it.

Reed says he recorded the being, the ash and the obelisk with a camcorder, then used a Nikon 35mm camera to take photographs. He attributes disturbances in the video to filming near the object and explains that photography had been a lifelong hobby.

Afraid he might have killed something and face imprisonment, Reed initially considered covering the body and leaving it in the forest. Instead, he says, he rolled it inside a thermal blanket and secured it with backpack straps. He estimated its weight at only thirty to forty pounds. While carrying it towards the Jeep, he recalls suddenly finding himself beside the vehicle without remembering the intervening walk. Caspersight suggests shock as a possible explanation.

On the drive home, Reed says he stopped at an empty ranger station seeking help and repeatedly pulled over because he was sick. At home, he placed the wrapped body in an operating chest freezer in his detached garage. He then called his girlfriend and his longtime friend Gary, an architect, leaving a message that Susie was dead and he needed help.

Reed says Gary initially suspected hallucination but changed his reaction after watching the recording and seeing the body. Gary stayed overnight to look after him and began contacting organisations the following day. They also returned to the forest, where Reed says the obelisk, blood and ash had vanished. Even ferns he remembered disturbing appeared restored. Asked whether he was certain of the location, he says he recognised distinctive trees.

Reed recounts meeting people who presented themselves as MUFON representatives at a restaurant. He says he gave them photographs, some negatives and a short copy of the forest recording, while withholding that the body was at his house. They promised to contact him, but their telephone number subsequently proved disconnected. Reed says he and Gary retained copies and began storing material elsewhere, eventually sending evidence outside the country.

He also describes break-ins at his relatives’ home and his own house, followed by a visit from two men and a woman dressed in black. They allegedly said they knew what he had and asked where his dog was. When he threatened to call the police, they indicated a police car outside and said the police were with them. According to Reed, they identified their group as “the school” and warned that the next visitors would be less friendly. Caspersight asks whether he thinks they were nonhuman; Reed says he cannot make that claim, although their appearance, speech and clothing struck him as unusual.

Reed says his colleague Allan subsequently reported men removing files and belongings from his office. He claims his workplace then denied employing him and that records of his education and qualifications disappeared. Caspersight asks how he could prove his background today. Reed describes investigators collecting statements from former acquaintances and relatives, and lawyers attempting to recover his records. He says his passport was eventually restored after his lawyers threatened publicity, but other records remained unavailable.

Discussing the public history of the case, Reed credits Art Bell with bringing it to a large radio audience and recalls speaking at the International UFO Congress. He says investigators spent two years examining his background. He also claims to have passed two polygraph examinations and rejects accusations that he fabricated the photographs and recordings.

Reed describes laboratory work on samples of blood, tissue and bone. He says the results showed forty-six chromosomes, with nine pairs displaying partial similarities to dolphins and sea turtles, along with nucleated blood cells and unusual bone material. He names pathologist Rodger Haggitt and connects his killing to the alleged research. He also describes another collaborator dying in a hiking accident and says Harold Chacon, another participant, moved to Puerto Rico after threats. Caspersight asks whether the killing was documented and whether it might have been coincidental; Reed says it was reported in Seattle newspapers and rejects coincidence.

Returning to the garage, Reed says that on the third day he heard scratching near the freezer. When he opened it, the being rose from the blanket and screamed so forcefully that he nearly lost his balance. He fled into the house and called Gary. According to Reed, both men then witnessed the being rise and scream again.

At Caspersight’s request, Reed plays a recording he attributes to these cries. He explains that he recorded them on a later occasion by leaving a recorder running in the garage. Caspersight asks whether the freezer had been switched off; Reed says it remained operating throughout.

Reed also describes an examination filmed on the second day, while he still believed the being was dead. Wearing gloves, he moved its limbs and head and inspected the skull wound. He says he attached the camcorder to a ladder when he needed both hands. Only afterwards, when somebody watched the recording, did he notice movements of the eyes and facial muscles.

Asked for physical details, Reed describes large eyes with a possible inner eyelid, numerous small sharp teeth, a purplish-red tongue and thick, weathered skin. He says its colour changed from bluish-grey in the forest to darker pinkish-brown shades in the freezer.

He compares the suit to tightly fitted black spandex that could not be pulled away from the skin. Reed says two cuts made with a craft knife immediately closed, while a third attempt was resisted by the material itself. He calls it self-healing nanotechnology and claims he described it years before a later NASA announcement about self-healing spacesuit material. Caspersight asks whether his account preceded that announcement, and Reed says it did.

Around the ninth or tenth day, Reed says he saw vehicles outside his home and people removing possessions. After calling the police from a friend’s house, he returned to find the building ransacked, holes in the walls, floors and ceilings, and the freezer missing. Small wet footprints crossed the garage towards a wall, leading him to hope the being had escaped.

About a month later, he says, the same creature materialised inside his home. He recognised its markings and healing head wound and began calling it Freddy. Reed claims it continues to visit him, sometimes weekly, communicating through mental pictures. These included images of Reed swinging the branch, sensations of pain, and Susie running in the forest.

Caspersight asks whether these experiences might themselves have been projected illusions. Reed acknowledges that possibility in principle but says his photographs, recordings and biological samples convince him otherwise. He also claims Freddy has appeared to other people who have spoken with him. When asked where the being is now, he replies that it is with its own kind and continues coming and going.

The conversation then turns to the Link Artifact, a silver cuff-like device. Reed says he once put it on while sitting with his coauthor Robert Raith, whom he describes as deceased. It allegedly tightened around his wrist, inserting three large gold needles into his skin and nerves, before opening by itself as the metal changed shape.

Caspersight says the forest footage and photographs impressed him, but the recording of Reed apparently disappearing and returning was where the story lost him. Reed responds that he understands and would also find the account difficult to believe without his own experiences.

Reed says the demonstration took place on a television programme near Toronto, Canada, after a presenter offered him a vacant guest slot. He recalls requesting a continuous camera shot and performing before a live audience. He describes being surrounded by an energy bubble resembling fine fibres, followed by darkness and a sudden transition into a large white, egg-shaped room.

There, he says, he encountered two towering, moving columns of light that reminded him of angels. They allegedly reassured him telepathically and told him they would return him. Reed describes an overwhelming feeling of peace and affection and says he did not want to leave. He recalls returning to his original seat in considerable pain.

Asked what he has gained from the experience, Reed says he is convinced humanity is not alone. He describes Freddy as a highly intelligent geologist whose task was to study Earth’s rocks. Caspersight observes that Reed’s attitude seems to have changed from hatred to affection; Reed says respect is the more accurate word. He now believes Susie’s death was an involuntary response to the circumstances, although he says attempts to discuss it with Freddy have not produced an explanation he understands.

The closing discussion covers spirituality and UFO disclosure. Caspersight raises religious interpretations of such beings and speaks about his own sense of spiritual protection. Reed describes himself as spiritual rather than religious and says the experiences made him more open-minded. He criticises disclosure as a slow release of information that does not show the direct encounters people want to see.

Reed also alleges continuing intimidation, including being pushed down a flight of stairs shortly before the interview. Discussing his book, Link: An Extraterrestrial Odyssey, and the documentary Contact in the Woods: The Dr. Jonathan Reed Story, he describes the film as a personal portrait that may reveal the trauma he associates with these experiences. He says its release had been delayed by distribution problems and that it could become the first part of a three-part series. The interview ends with Reed acknowledging that he does not have all the answers and thanking Caspersight for allowing him to tell his story.

A peace settlement of the Russia-Ukraine War, based on ongoing proposals and diplomatic frameworks mediated by the U.S. and European powers, would likely center on a managed freeze of the conflict along the current front lines paired with territorial, security, and economic compromises. Core Elements of a Potential Settlement • Territorial Compromise (De Facto vs. De Jure): • Russia would likely retain de facto control over Crimea and large portions of eastern and southern Ukraine (including parts of Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson). • Ukraine and its Western allies would refuse de jure (formal legal) recognition of Russian sovereignty over those occupied regions, keeping the status disputed similar to past frozen conflicts. • Proposals have also floated demilitarized or buffer zones in contested areas like parts of Donbas. • NATO and Security Arrangements: • Ukraine would likely be required to shelve or permanently freeze its bid for NATO membership for the foreseeable future, potentially enshrining neutrality in its constitution. • In exchange for neutrality, Western powers (led by European nations or a coalition of partners) would offer alternative security assurances. This could include a limited deployment of military-technical personnel, logistics, or training teams in western Ukraine, or integrated air-defense coverage, rather than massive front-line NATO combat forces. • Russia demands strict limits on the size of the Ukrainian military and conventional arms, a point of major contention since Ukraine resists crippling its self-defense capacity. • Economic Relief and Reconstruction: • Western nations would roll out a massive post-war reconstruction package for Ukraine—backed by mechanisms involving institutions like the World Bank or frozen Russian asset structures. • For Russia, a settlement would likely involve calibrated, gradual relief from Western economic and energy sanctions, along with potential reintegration into broader international economic forums. • Humanitarian and Legal Provisions: • Any formal accord would need to address the release of prisoners of war (POWs), the return of detained civilians and forcibly relocated children, and frameworks for handling war crimes accountability.  Key Sticking Points  According to analysis from groups like Chatham House and reporting by outlets like The Washington Post, both sides face hard political ceilings: • Ukraine (President Volodymyr Zelenskyy) has consistently ruled out surrendering sovereign territory by mandate or granting formal recognition to Russian gains. • Russia (President Vladimir Putin) has maintained maximalist demands—including full withdrawal of Ukrainian forces from claimed eastern/southern oblasts, complete neutralization, and permanent bans on Western security guarantees.

text:
Augusto Pinochet (1915–2006) was a Chilean general and dictator who ruled Chile from 1973 to 1990 after leading a military coup. Pinochet's secret police (DINA) and military forces systematically cracked down on political dissent, banning leftist parties and shutting down Congress. At least 3,095 to over 3,000 people were killed or forcibly disappeared, tens of thousands were tortured, and around 200,000 Chileans were forced into exile. His regime coordinated with other South American dictatorships in Operation Condor to hunt down and assassinate political opponents abroad. Pinochet handed economic management to a group of free-market economists trained at the University of Chicago (known as the "Chicago Boys"). He privatized state industries, slashed tariffs, and deregulated the economy, which curbed high inflation and triggered an economic boom in the late 1970s, though it also deepened social inequality and led to severe recessions. Under his 1980 Constitution, a national plebiscite was held in October 1988 to decide whether he would remain in power for another eight years. Voters rejected him with a 55% "No" vote... 

Augusto Pinochet lost the vote that could have kept him president for eight more years. On the night of October 5, 1988, Chileans rejected another presidential term for the general who had ruled since the 1973 military coup. Yet as the result became clear, the most dangerous question was no longer how people had voted. It was whether the dictatorship would obey them. According to a later declassified American military intelligence report, Pinochet sought extraordinary powers that could allow troops to seize the capital. The commanders whose signatures he needed refused.

The plebiscite had been built into the constitution imposed under military rule. A “Yes” vote would extend Pinochet’s presidency until 1997; “No” would start a process leading to competitive elections. Opposition parties united around the No campaign, using rallies, voter organization and a memorable television campaign to challenge a government that controlled much of the political system. More than seven million voters were registered. After years in which ordinary Chileans had been denied meaningful national elections, the ballot offered a real opening, although the armed forces and institutions of the dictatorship remained powerful.

The warning signs reached Washington before polling day. In a cable dated October 1, American ambassador Harry Barnes described intelligence suggesting Pinochet might resort to violence rather than accept defeat. Another US intelligence report, dated October 4, outlined alleged contingency plans to provoke disturbances and use the disorder as grounds to suspend the process. These documents recorded what American officials believed their sources were revealing; they did not establish that every reported plan would be carried out. The Reagan administration nevertheless treated the danger seriously, warning Chilean military figures against interfering with the result.

On election evening, the government’s first public count favored Pinochet, but it covered only a tiny portion of polling stations. The opposition’s parallel tally pointed in the opposite direction. Official announcements slowed as the hours passed. For voters who had endured years of repression, a numerical victory could still prove meaningless without recognition from the authorities. Air Force commander Fernando Matthei made a decisive public intervention as he arrived at La Moneda presidential palace in the early hours of October 6. He told reporters that the No side had won. The government had not yet formally conceded.

text:
When did demanding an end to a war become a right-wing position?

American liberals should be uncomfortable with that question. 

If opposition to Trump makes negotiations sound disreputable, then Trump is setting the boundaries of our politics even when we oppose him.

Across Europe, parties on the left offer a critique Americans need to hear: 

how many Ukrainian lives are we prepared to spend, pursuing what achievable end?

Germany’s Die Linke, Spain’s Podemos and Izquierda Unida, Belgium’s Workers’ Party, and Portugal’s Communists challenge the assumption that another weapons shipment brings peace closer. 

Italy’s Five Star and Italian Left oppose further deliveries. Their argument is that supplying a war has become a substitute for developing an exit.

Approve the money. Announce solidarity. Send the weapons. Repeat.

The conscripts cannot repeat their lives.

Then follow the money.

Global military spending approaches three trillion dollars annually. Europe’s arms boom is swelling billionaire fortunes while millions of households struggle with rent, groceries, and heating. More than four in ten EU households reported at least some difficulty making ends meet in 2024.

For one class, insecurity means choosing which bill goes unpaid. 

For another, it means a swelling order book.

Austria’s Communists and the European Left challenge this political economy: 

public resources flow toward rearmament while social needs compete for what remains. 

Americans know the routine. 

Healthcare must justify every dollar. Weapons arrive wrapped in necessity.
The hospital is expensive. The weapons contract is essential.

Greece’s Communists describe competing imperial powers; other parties criticize NATO expansion and dependence on Washington. Their question is whose interests working people are being asked to bleed for.

Those financing the fighting owe an answer to those living beneath it.

That scrutiny applies to Trump too. 

Ireland’s People Before Profit rejects settlements that carve up territory or transfer resources to powerful states and corporations. 

Peace must give people their futures back, not auction those futures to investors.

These parties disagree over sanctions and military aid. 

Their overlapping demand is for negotiations with a credible destination beyond sustained combat.

American moderates and leftists should make that demand.

Insist on a ceasefire. Fund reconstruction, refugee support, and care for the wounded. Make advocates of continued fighting explain what another year can realistically achieve.

A working-class politics cannot accept an arrangement in which ordinary people supply the taxes, the soldiers, and the graves while wealthy owners collect the contracts.

Solidarity must mean more than financing the next funeral.

You keep $338,660 to $345,380 a month.

Per video:

→ Earns: about $29,167

Now the part that matters.

Where does the $350,000 come from?

→ Ads: 8,000,000 views × $10 RPM = $80,000
→ Sponsors: 6 deals × $30,000 = $180,000
→ Affiliate: 2,000 sales × $45 = $90,000

Total: $350,000.

→ Buy 12 gadgets
→ Film the unboxing
→ Wait for views

That money goes into research and editing.

Pick a format that needs no product: comparisons, explainers, "how it works

Keep the research decisions yourself

Land 1 sponsor or affiliate offer before adding roles
Track cost per video and revenue per video each month

text:
Not every farm needs a drone. But every farmer deserves to understand what one can actually do.

Agricultural drones are becoming more advanced. They can spray, spread seeds, and help us see what's happening across our fields.

But as farmers, the real question isn't how many features a drone has.

It's what problems can it actually solve on my farm?

If a tractor can already do the job, why would I need a drone?

When fields are too wet for heavy equipment, could a drone offer a practical alternative?

Could drone seeding make cover crop establishment easier or more flexible?

And when we consider the cost of equipment, training, batteries, maintenance, and labour — does the investment really make sense?

Most importantly, how can drones fit into existing farm operations without creating more work for farmers?

These aren't questions we want answered by equipment manufacturers or salespeople alone.

We want to hear from the people who actually work the land.

That's why we're bringing together three experienced agricultural voices for Panel 3 at Niagara Drone Summit 2026.

Panel 3 — Where Does a Drone Actually Fit on the Farm?

🌱 Ben Bos — Bosdale Farms

A dairy and field crop grower with hands-on experience using agricultural drones in real farm operations.

🌱 Boris Horodynsky — Holland Marsh, Ontario

An onion grower from Ontario's Holland Marsh region, rotating onions with soybeans and bringing years of practical experience in crop production and farm management.

🌱 Andrew McCallum — Grower & Drone Operator

A farmer and drone operator with firsthand experience integrating drone technology into everyday farm operations.

These aren't just conversations about technology.

They're conversations about real farming — what works, what doesn't, what challenges farmers face, and what they've learned along the way.

We want to explore an important question together:

When is a drone the right tool for the job, and when are traditional farming methods still the better choice?

Because good agricultural technology shouldn't force farmers to change everything just to use a new piece of equipment.

It should help us do the right job, with the right tool, at the right time.

We believe the future of agriculture shouldn't be defined by any one brand, manufacturer, or technology.

It should be shaped by the people who understand the land, the crops, and the realities of running a farm.

📅 November 2–3, 2026
📍 Niagara Falls Convention Centre, Ontario, Canada
We hope to see more Canadian farmers in Niagara this November, sharing their experiences, asking questions, and learning from one another.

👉 https://t.co/qLsyc2qNeG

🌱 Real farming experience deserves to be shared.

If you know a farmer who's considering agricultural drones, already using them, or even questioning whether they're worth it, please share this post.

We don't need everyone to agree that drones are the future of farming. We need more honest conversations and real experiences from the field.

🇨🇦 Let's bring more Canadian farmers into the conversation.

Join the conversation. Register early and secure your place!

text:
When it comes to music and art, Europe is not further behind, but much further ahead. A musician sitting in a cafe with a drum machine, sampler and laptop - as opposed to the umpteenth acoustic guitar - is what you'd see in Europe. At least well into the 2000s. "Scenes" and trends are not as geographically bound anymore, it's become complicated.

It's only where tech meets arcane business processes or gambling apps that sure, Europe is outdated. I don't totally discount these things. It's why Americans can enjoy larger physical music collections and entertainment systems at home and on the go, relative to Europeans. But let's not conflate being "left behind" with being left behind on what tech (and now AI) can offer just generally. 

I wouldn't be surprised if Europe is both hostile to AI and has more talented artists using AI, simultaneously.

text:
Restoration of the Lapsed: The Second Epistle of Pope Saint Callistus I
.
Callistus to our most dearly beloved brethren, all the bishops settled throughout Gaul.
.
By the report of very many, we learn that your love, by the zeal of the Holy Spirit, holds and guides the helm of the Church so firmly in the face of all assaults, that by God’s will it is conscious neither of shipwreck nor of the losses of shipwreck. Rejoicing, therefore, in such testimonies, we beg you not to permit anything to be done in those parts contrary to the apostolic statutes; but, supported by our authority, do ye check what is injurious, and prohibit what is unlawful.
.
I. Now we have heard that the crime of conspiracies prevails in your parts, and it has been shown us that the people are conspiring against their bishops; of which crime the craft is hateful, not only among Christians, but even among the heathen, and it is forbidden by foreign laws. And therefore the laws not only of the Church, but of the world, condemn those who are guilty of this crime; and not only those indeed who actually conspire, but those also who take part with such. Our predecessors, moreover, together with a very numerous body of bishops, ordained that any guilty of this offence among those who are set in the honour of the priesthood, and who belong to the clergy, should be deprived of the honour which they enjoy; and they ordered that others should be cut off from communion, and expelled from the Church; and they decreed, at the same time, that all men of both orders should be infamous (infames); and that, too, not only for those who did the deed, but for those also who took part with such. For it is but equitable that those who despise the divine mandates, and prove themselves disobedient to the ordinances of the fathers, should be chastised with severer penalties, in order that others may fear to do such things, and that all may rejoice in brotherly concord, and all take to themselves the example of severity and goodness. For if (which may God forbid) we neglect the care of the Church, and are regardless of its strength, our slothfulness will destroy discipline, and injury will be done assuredly to the souls of the faithful. Such persons, moreover, are not to be admitted to accuse any one: neither can their voice, nor that of those who are under the ban, injure or criminate any man.
.
II. Those, too, who are excommunicated by the priests, let no one receive previous to the just examination of both sides; nor let him have any intercourse with such in speech, or in eating or drinking, or in the salutation with the kiss, nor let him greet such; because, whosoever wittingly holds intercourse with the excommunicated in these or other prohibited matters, will subject himself, according to the ordinance of the apostles, to like excommunication. From these, therefore, let clergy and laity keep themselves if they would not have the same penalty to endure. Also do not join the unbelievers, neither have any fellowship with them. They who do such things, indeed, are judged not as believers, but as unbelievers. Whence the apostle says: “What part hath he that believeth with an infidel? or what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness?”
.
III. Let no one, again, trespass upon the boundaries of another, nor presume to judge or excommunicate one belonging to another’s parish; because such judgment or ordination, or excommunication or condemnation, shall neither be ratified nor have any virtue; since no one shall be bound by the decision of another judge than his own, neither shall he be condemned by such. Whence also the Lord speaks to this effect: “Pass not the ancient landmarks which thy fathers have set.” Moreover, let no primate or metropolitan invade the church or parish of a diocesan (dioecesani), or presume to excommunicate or judge any one belonging to his parish, or do anything without his counsel or judgment; but let him observe this law, which has been laid down by the apostles and fathers, and our predecessors, and has been ratified by us: to wit, that if any metropolitan bishop, except in that which pertains to his own proper parish alone, shall attempt to do anything without the counsel and good-will of all the comprovincial bishops, he will do it at the risk of his position, and what he does in this manner shall be held null and void; but whatever it may be necessary to do or to arrange with regard to the cases of the body of provincial bishops, and the necessities of their churches and clergy and laity, this should be done by consent of all the pontiffs of the same province, and that too without any pride of lordship, but with the most humble and harmonious action, even as the Lord says: “I came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.” And in another passage He says: “And whosoever of you is the greater, shall be your servant,” and so forth. And in like manner the bishops of the same province themselves should do all things in counsel with him, except so much as pertains to their own proper parishes, in accordance with the statutes of the holy fathers (who, although they have preceded us by a certain interval of time, have yet drawn the light of truth and faith from one and the same fountain of purity, and have sought the prosperity of the Church of God and the common advantage of all Christians by the same enlightening and guiding Spirit), that with one mind, and one mouth, and one accord, the Holy Trinity may be glorified for ever. No primate, no metropolitan, nor any of the other bishops, is at liberty to enter the seat of another, or to occupy a possession which does not pertain to him, and which forms part of the parish of another bishop, at the direction of any one, unless he is invited by him to whose jurisdiction it is acknowledged to belong; nor can he set about any arrangement or ordinance, or judgment there, if he wishes to keep the honour of his station. But if he presume to do otherwise, he shall be condemned; and not only he, but those who co-operate and agree with him: for just as the power of making appointments (ordinatio) is interdicted in such circumstances, so also is the power of judging or of disposing of other matters. For if a man has no power to appoint, how shall he judge? Without doubt, he shall in no wise judge or have power to judge: for just as another man’s wife cannot intermarry with anyone (adulterari), nor be judged or disposed of by any one but by her own husband so long as he liveth; so neither can it in anywise be allowed that the wife of a bishop, by whom undoubtedly is meant his church or parish, should be judged or disposed of by another without his (the bishop’s) judgment and good-will so long as he liveth, or enjoy another’s embrace, that is, his ordaining. Wherefore the apostle says: “The wife is bound by the law so long as her husband liveth; but if he be dead, she is loosed from the law of her husband.” In like manner also, the spouse of a bishop (for the church is called his spouse and wife) is bound to him while he liveth; but when he is dead she is loosed, and may be wedded to whomsoever she will, only in the Lord, that is, according to order. For if, while he is alive, she marry another, she shall be judged to be an adulteress. And in the same manner, he too, if he marry another of his own will, shall be held to be an adulterer, and shall be deprived of the privilege of communion. If, however, he is persecuted in his own church, he must flee to another, and attach himself to it, as the Lord says: “If they persecute you in one city, flee ye into another.” If, however, the change be made for the sake of the good of the church, he may not do this of himself, but only on the invitation of the brethren, and with the sanction of this holy seat, and not for ambition’s sake, but for the public good.
.
IV. Moreover, marriages among blood-relations are forbidden, since all laws, both sacred and secular, forbid such. Wherefore the divine laws not only expel, but even anathematize, those who do so, and those who spring from them. Secular laws, again, call such persons infamous, and interdict them from inheriting. And we too, following our fathers, and keeping close by their footsteps, brand such with infamy, and hold them to be infamous, because they are sprinkled with the stains of infamy. Neither ought we to admit those men or their accusations, that secular laws reject. (For who doubts that human laws, when they are not inconsistent with reason and honour, are to be embraced, especially when they either further the public good or defend the authority of the ecclesiastical office, and uphold it as a help?) And we call those blood-relations whom divine laws, and those of the emperors, both Roman and Greek, name blood-relations, and whom they admit to the right of inheriting, and cannot exclude from that. Marriages, then, between such are neither lawful nor capable of holding good, but are to be rejected. (And if any such are attempted in rash daring, they come to be rescinded by apostolic authority.)
.
V. Whosoever, therefore, has not been lawfully married, or has been united without the dotal title (dotali titulo) and the blessing of a priest, cannot by any means bring a charge against priests, or those who are lawfully married, or bear witness against them, since every one who is polluted with the stain of incest is infamous, and is not allowed to accuse the above-named. And consequently not only they, but all those too who agree with them, are to be rejected, and are rendered infamous. We hold that the same should also be the case with robbers, or with those who assault the elderly. The laws of the world, indeed, put such persons to death; but we, with whom mercy has the first place, receive them under the mark of infamy to repentance. That infamy also with which they are stained, we are not able to remove; but our desire is to heal their souls by public penitence, and by satisfaction made to the Church: for public sins are not to be purged by secret correction. Those, again, who are suspected in the matter of the right faith, should by no means be admitted to prefer charges against priests, and against those of whose faith there is no doubt; and such persons should be held of doubtful authority in matters of human testimony. Their voice, consequently, should bereckoned invalid whose faith is doubted; and no credit should be given to those who are ignorant of the right faith. Accordingly, in judgment, inquiry should be made as to the conversation and faith of the person who accuses, and of him who is accused; since those who are not of correct conversation and faith, and whose life is open to impeachment, are not allowed to accuse their eiders, neither can such permission be given to those whose faith and life and liberty are unknown. Nor should vile persons be admitted to accuse them. But a clear examination is to be made as to what kind of persons the accusers are (rimandoesunt enucleatim personaeaccusatorum); for they are not to be admitted readily without writing, and are never to be admitted as accusers on mere writing. For no one may either accuse or be accused by mere writing, but with the living voice; and every one must lay his accusation in the presence of him whom he seeks to accuse. And no credit should be given to any accuser in the absence of him whom he seeks to accuse. In like manner, witnesses must not prefer their evidence by writing only; but they must give their testimony truthfully in their own persons, and in matters which they have seen and do know. And they are not to give evidence in any other cases or matters but in those which are known to have happened in their presence. Accusers, moreover, of one blood, are not to bear witness against those who are not related to the family, nor is that to be the case with domestics (familiares) or those proceeding from the house; but if it is their wish, and they agree among themselves, the parents only should give evidence in such cases, and not others. Neither accusers nor witnesses should be admitted who are open to any suspicion; for the feeling of relationship, or friendship, or lordship, is wont to impede the truth. Carnal love, and fear, and avarice, commonly blunt the perceptions of men, and pervert their opinions; so that they look on gain as godliness, and on money as the reward of prudence. Let no one, then, speak deceitfully to his neighbour. The mouth of the malevolent is a deep pit. The innocent man, while he believes easily, falls readily; but though he falls, he rises; and the shuffler, with all his arts, goes headlong to ruin, whence he can never rise or escape. Therefore let every one weigh well his words, and let him not say to another what he would not say to himself. Whence the sacred Scripture says well:
.
“Do not that to another which thou wouldest not have done to thyself.”
.
For we need time to do anything perfectly (maturius); and let us not be precipitate in our counsels or our works, neither let us violate order. But if any one has fallen in anything, let us not consign him to ruin; but let us reprove him with brotherly affection, as the blessed apostle says:
.
“If a man be overtaken in any fault, ye which are spiritual restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, test thou also be tempted. Bear ye one another’s burden, and so will ye fulfil the law of Christ.”
.
Furthermore, the sainted David had deadly crimes to repent of, and yet he was continued in honour. The blessed Peter also shed the bitterest tears when he repented of having denied the Lord; but still he abode an apostle. And the Lord by the prophet makes this promise to the sinning:
.
“In the day that the sinner is converted, and repenteth, I will not mention any more against him all his transgressions.”
VI. For those are in error who think that the priests of the Lord, after a lapse, although they may have exhibited true repentance, are not capable of ministering to the Lord, and engaging their honourable offices, though they may lead a good life thereafter, and keep their priesthood correctly. And those who hold this opinion are not only in error, but also seem to dispute and act in opposition to the power of the keys committed to the Church, whereof it is said:
.
“Whatsoever ye shall loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.”
.
And in short, this opinion either is not the Lord’s, or it is true. But be that as it may, we believe without hesitation, that both the priests of the Lord and other believers may return to their honours after a proper satisfaction for their error, as the Lord Himself testifies by His prophet:
.
“Shall he who falls not also rise again? and shall he who turns away not return?”
.
And in another passage the Lord says:
.
“I desire not the death of the sinner, but that he may turn, and live.”
.
And the prophet David, on his repentance, said:
.
“Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation, and uphold me with Thy free Spirit.”
.
And he indeed, after his repentance, taught others also, and offered sacrifice to God, giving thereby an example to the teachers of the holy Church, that if they have fallen, and thereafter have exhibited a right repentance to God, they may do both things in like manner. For he taught when he said:
.
“I will teach transgressors Thy ways, and sinners shall be converted unto Thee.”
.
And he offered sacrifice for himself, while he said:
.
“The sacrifice for God is a broken spirit.”
.
For the prophet, seeing his own transgressions purged by repentance, had no doubt as to healing those of others by preaching, and by making offering to God. Thus the shedding of tears moves the mind’s feeling (passionem). And when the satisfaction is made good, the mind is turned aside from anger. For how does that man think that mercy will be shown to himself, who does not forgive his neighbour? If offences abound, then, let mercy also abound; for with the Lord there is mercy, and with Him is plenteous redemption. In the Lord’s hand there is abundance of all things, because He is the Lord of powers (virtutum) and the King of glory. For the apostle says: “All have sinned, and come short of the glory of God; being justified freely by His grace, through the redemption that is in Jesus Christ: whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in His blood, to declare His righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; to declare,
.
“I say, at this time His righteousness, that He might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.”
.
And David says:
.
“Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.”
.
Man, therefore, is cleansed of his sin, and rises again by the grace of God though he has fallen, and abides in his first position, according to the above-cited authorities. Let him see to it that he sin no more, that the sentence of the Gospel may abide in him:
.
“Go, and sin no more.”
.
Whence the apostle says:
.
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey the lusts thereof: neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God. For sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace. What then? shall we sin because we are not under the law, but under grace? God forbid. Know ye not, that to whom ye yield yourselves servants to obey, his servants ye are to whom ye obey; whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness? But God be thanked, that ye were the servants of sin; but ye have obeyed from the heart that form of doctrine which was delivered you. Being then made free from sin, ye became the servants of righteousness. I speak after the manner of men.”
.
For greater is the sin of him who judgeth, than of him who is judged.
.
“Thinkest thou,” says the apostle, “O man, that judgest them that do such things, and doest the same, that thou shalt escape the judgment of God? or despisest thou the riches of His goodness, and forbearance, and long-suffering? Dost thou not know that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance? But, after thy hardness and impenitent heart, thou treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God; who will render to every man according to his deeds: to them who, by patient continuance in well-doing, seek for glory, and honour, and immortality, eternal life; but unto them that are contentious, and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, indignation and wrath, tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man that doeth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Greek: but glory, honour, and peace, to every man that worketh good.”
.
My brethren, shun not only the holding, but even the hearing, of the judgment that bans mercy; for better is mercy than all whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices. We have replied to your interrogations shortly, because your letter found us burdened overmuch, and preoccupied with other judgments.
.
Given on the 8th day of October, in the consulship of the most illustrious Antonine and Alexander.

Why? 

Why would God permit crosses in our lives?

And sometimes we just can't see that. We don't see directly, oh, here's some opportunity for me or others to gain salvation or to gain some kind of goodness or love in their lives.

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, Amen.

What a blessing it is to have prayed with you today.
Please know of my prayers and the prayers of the whole Hallow community.
