text:
Have you heard this phrase before? “No gods! No masters!” I’ve seen it on T shirts. A man blurted it out to counter my claims about God once.

It’s misguidedly optimistic and smugly defiant. 

A phrase that gives the subscriber the illusion they control their destiny. It aligns with the sentiment in William Earnest Henley’s prideful rejection of God’s authority in the poem Invictus-
 
“It matters not how strait the gate,
How charged with punishments the scroll, 
I am the master of my fate:
I am the captain of my soul.”
 
Good luck with that Bill.
 
Scripture does mention a “scroll” of sorts. A legal document filled with charges against us. Believers are reminded that at great cost Christ assumed responsibility for the debt they could not pay.
 
“When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ. He forgave us all our trespasses, having canceled the debt ascribed to us in the decrees that stood against us. He took it away, nailing it to the cross!” -Colossians 2:13-14

God's justice requires the debt be paid. Jesus paid it for me.

You’ve heard it said “A man who chooses to represent himself in court has a fool for a client.” It’s a similar case for those who would be their own masters.
 
Like a child who covers his eyes believing it makes them invisible, “no gods no masters” proponents believe a verbal disavowal of God’s existence makes it so.
 
Deniers and believers have one thing in common. They share the same god, just in different capacities. The first, unwillingly, the second gratefully. One group embraces him as savior. The other glories in rebellion or denial for a season to meet him later as judge. 
 
For many years I believed I was in a neutral spiritual country. 

I certainly didn’t regard myself as being “against God” but couldn’t call myself “for” God either. I lived for myself. I preferred to know as little as I could about what he required. Rightly suspecting there would be obligations of some kind if I chose his way. I hoped ignorance of the law would excuse me.
 
I believed in God and wouldn’t dare speak openly against him. If anyone suggested I was being “obedient to the devil” by remaining an outsider, I would have been deeply offended and vigorously denied it. Yet according to Jesus, unwittingly or not, I was on the other team. 
 
I labored under the delusion there were three categories of people:
 
For the Lord.
Against the Lord.
And “neutral non participant.“
 
A class of people who I imagined at the judgment would hear God say “You pretty much stayed out of it. You were no angel ,but you weren’t as bad as you could be and tried your best. So what the heck, you can come into heaven too but you’ll have to share a room in an efficiency apartment.”
 
However, the bible is clear that before I belonged to Christ, by nature I belonged to satan and served him whether I cared to admit it or not. My conscious allegiance was not a prerequisite. The apostle Paul reminded believers-
 
“Once you were dead because of your disobedience and your many sins.  You used to live in sin, just like the rest of the world, obeying the devil—the commander of the powers in the unseen world. He is the spirit at work in the hearts of those who refuse to obey God. All of us used to live that way, following the passionate desires and inclinations of our sinful nature. By our very nature we were subject to God’s anger, just like everyone else.” -Ephesians 2:1-3 New Living Translation
 
To decline God’s offer of reconciliation through the cross of Christ is to defy him and trample on the blood of Christ. Contrary to popular opinion, you don’t need a pentagram on your living room floor. You don’t have to perform dark rituals or commit overtly wicked acts to serve the devil. 
 
Jesus recognized two classes of people, not three. In Matthew 12:30 he said-
 
  “Whoever is not with me is against me and whoever does not gather with me scatters.” 

We don't get to sit it out.
 
All playing for the other side requires is a refusal to recognize God’s claim as stated in Romans 3:23 
 
“All have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God.” and a failure to embrace Christ’s sacrifice. As far as satan is concerned, as long as you resist God’s grace he considers it a win. 

Far from leading to freedom, being your own master is slavery. Paradoxically, submitting to God’s rule brings freedom. 
 
The only independent being in this universe is God himself. Everyone and everything else depends on his provision. Even unbelievers receive his sun, rain, air, water, light, food. Scripture tells us all creation is upheld by his active and sustaining word. Matter itself would cease to exist if God stopped sustaining it. 
 
You will never be more free to do, be, and have, as you will if you surrender to Christ. You’ll inherit all things when you acknowledge God and accept the liberty of “One God one master” in Jesus.
 
If you aren't with Christ, I encourage you to change sides today. Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ and you will be saved. You don’t need to clean yourself up first. He’ll take care of that. Just call on him. He’s not far, he’s closer than your breath. Say-
 
Jesus, I admit I’m a sinner. I believe you took responsibility for my sin on the cross and died that I might be forgiven and have a forever relationship with you. I offer myself to you and want you to be my Lord and savior.
 
He will hear and act on your behalf. I look forward to being in the kingdom with you. 
 
“The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart,”that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming: that if you confess with your mouth, “Jesus is Lord,” and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved. For with your heart you believe and are justified, and with your mouth you confess and are saved.
  -Romans 10:9-11

text:
*ALAAFIN  OF OYO AND OLUBADAN OF IBADAN ENDORSES PRESDIENT TINUBU SECOND TERM LED BY HE SENATOR YARI - DG PCC*

*In the heart of Yorubaland, royal palaces open their gates to a message of continuity, unity, and renewed hope*.

On Thursday, 15 October 2026, a high-powered delegation of the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, led by its Director-General, Senator Abdulaziz Abubakar Yari, paid a courtesy visit to the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, at his palace in Oke-Aremo, Ibadan. Joining the team was High Chief Government Ekpemupolo (Tompolo), Grand Patron of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement, alongside former governors Gbenga Daniel, Olusegun Mimiko and Rochas Okorocha, Special Adviser Sunday Dare, Oyo APC governorship candidate Senator Sharafadeen Alli, and other party leaders. 

*Members of the Olubadan-in-Council and market women led by the Iyaloja of Ibadanland welcomed the visitors in a warm atmosphere of traditional respect and political dialogue*. The engagement reflected a deliberate effort to connect the federal campaign with the deep cultural roots of Oyo State, seeking the monarch’s blessings for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s second-term bid and for peaceful, people-centred mobilisation.
*The same day, the campaign leadership also reached the Alaafin of Oyo, His Imperial Majesty Oba Abimbola Akeem Owoade*. Senator Yari presented the case for continuity, highlighting national unity, cohesion, and ongoing socio-economic reforms. In response, the Alaafin commended the delegation, pledged his support for the President’s re-election, and urged the campaign council to prioritise peaceful, responsible, and unity-driven engagement across the state and nation. The moment underscored the enduring role of traditional institutions as pillars of stability and guidance in Nigeria’s democratic process. 

*Complementing these palace visits, the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement formally inaugurated its Oyo State structure at Liberty Stadium in Ibadan*. *High Chief Tompolo, through his representative Chief Kestin Pondi (Managing Director of Tantita Security Services), presented 32 vehicles to strengthen grassroots mobilisation*. He reminded the people of Oyo that President Tinubu is one of their own and called on them to ensure he completes the southern turn, consolidating reforms that have increased resources available to state governments for salaries, pensions, and major projects. 

*National Coordinator Sunday Asuku and APC candidate Senator Alli reinforced the message, describing the reforms as necessary for sustained growth and urging Oyo residents—especially the youth—to carry the message door-to-door*. The vehicles and structure signalled a commitment to direct engagement rather than distant rhetoric, aiming to take the conversation about continuity into homes, markets, and communities across the state.
Taken together, the day’s events painted a picture of purposeful collaboration. A northern senator leading the national campaign council stood alongside a Niger Delta high chief and Yoruba royal fathers. 

The visits and the mobilisation launch emphasised shared interests in stability, development, and the completion of ongoing reforms. For supporters of the Renewed Hope Agenda, the image of traditional rulers receiving the campaign team and offering blessings offered a positive signal of cultural legitimacy and grassroots readiness ahead of the 2027 elections.
In Ibadan and Oyo, the message that emerged was straightforward: continuity, respect for institutions, and a call for Oyo people to stand with their son so that the work already underway can be deepened for the benefit of the state and the nation.

text:
THE POWER THAT DOMINATES THE MIND.

In the silent vault of the inner temple, where thought arises and dissolves like incense smoke, there dwells a sovereign force older than language and vaster than the cosmos. It is not the mind that rules, but That which holds the mind in its palm—the uncreated Light, the primordial Will that breathes worlds into being.

This power does not argue with the ego; it simply remains. Under its gaze the restless currents of desire, fear, and memory lose their authority. What once seemed solid—identity, story, suffering—reveals itself as a shimmering veil. The mind, once a tyrant, becomes a transparent instrument. Attention turns inward, and the observer is no longer separate from the observed. In that recognition, domination is not violence but liberation: the false self is gently unseated so the true Self may reign.

Mystics have called it by many names—the Logos, the Atman, the Divine Spark, the Witness beyond witnessing. To those who have tasted it, all lesser powers are seen as shadows cast by its radiance. Surrender is the key. Not collapse, but conscious yielding. When the mind is offered without resistance, this power moves through it as pure clarity, transforming perception into wisdom and action into grace.

Walk into the stillness. Let the Power that dominates the mind become the mind’s only master. In that holy obedience, freedom is found.

text:
Mark Zuckerberg was 22 when Yahoo offered $1 billion for Facebook, and his own team wanted him to take it. He went to Steve Jobs instead.

Jobs told him to go to India.

In the video below, Zuckerberg tells India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi what happened next.

"This is a story that I haven't told publicly and very few people know."

Facebook was 2 years old, with about 10 million users. Zuckerberg said no to Yahoo.

It was a tough patch, he says. A lot of people wanted to buy Facebook and thought he should sell.

So he went to one of his mentors, Steve Jobs.

Jobs told him to visit the temple in India he had gone to while figuring out what Apple should be.

Zuckerberg traveled for almost a month. It "reinforced for me the importance of what we were doing."

For early employees with stock, a $1 billion sale is a life-changing payout. Saying no means years of waiting, maybe for nothing.

Within a year of saying no to Yahoo, his entire management team had quit.

He never sold. Today Meta is worth over $1.4 trillion.

Yahoo offered $1 billion.
Steve Jobs offered a temple.

Would you have taken $1 billion at 22, or the ticket to India?

Save the video, and follow for more money stories from behind the world's biggest names.

text:
The Dead Sea Scrolls are among the greatest archaeological discoveries of the twentieth century. Found in caves near the Dead Sea between 1947 and 1956, the collection transformed historians' understanding of the Hebrew Bible, ancient Judaism, and the world into which Christianity emerged.

The first scrolls were discovered by Bedouin shepherds in caves near Qumran. Archaeologists later excavated the surrounding area and uncovered thousands of manuscript fragments representing hundreds of separate texts. Written primarily in Hebrew, with some in Aramaic and Greek, the scrolls date from roughly the third century BC to the first century AD.

Among the discoveries were some of the oldest surviving copies of books from the Hebrew Bible, predating previously known manuscripts by nearly a thousand years. The remarkable agreement between these ancient texts and later copies demonstrated how carefully biblical writings had been preserved over the centuries, while also revealing small variations that have helped scholars better understand how the scriptures were transmitted and edited over time.

The scrolls include far more than biblical manuscripts. They contain religious commentaries, legal texts, hymns, prayers, calendars, and community rules that provide an extraordinary glimpse into Jewish life during the Second Temple period. Together, they reveal a diverse religious landscape with multiple groups holding different beliefs and practices before the destruction of the Second Temple in 70 AD.

Because the scrolls date to the same era in which Christianity first emerged, they have also become invaluable to historians studying the origins of both Judaism and Christianity. They offer important context for understanding the religious ideas, traditions, and expectations that shaped the world of the New Testament.

On the fifth day of the Devi Navaratri festival, after performing Gau puja, Sri Swamiji took Darshana of Sri Raja Rajeshwari, Hari Sannidhi, Sri Kalagni Shamana Dattatreya Swamy and  proceeded to Nada Mantapa in a beautiful Devi procession and blessed the young girls seated for Kumari Puja. 

During today’s Navavarana puja, Devi was worshipped as Parashakti with lemons and Tila anna  was offered as Annarchana. 

During the Navavarana Puja today, Sangeeta Seva was offered by Carnatic vocalist Vikas Maitreya accompanied by Prithivi Bhaskar on Violin, Sivasankara Swami on Mridangam and MR Manjunatha on Ghatam. The ensemble offered several compositions of Sri Dattaji including Jayedesha’ the Navavarana Kriti, ‘Sadakara’ on Mother Goddess, ‘Kashipate’ and ‘Parashakti Vishalakshi.’

Sri Swamiji performed Annarchana and Purnahuti to the Devi Homa. During the evening Abhishekam, Sangeeta Seva was offered by Ashok Yankaran, an ardent devotee of Sri Swamiji. This was followed by Dolotsava.

During this evening’s discourse, Sri Swamiji blessed devotees with a new composition ‘Jagadeka Saundarya Vibhrajini’ where Mother Goddess is described as pervading Shiva. 

Sri Swamiji then spoke at length of how Vishweshwara Swami and Vishalakshi Mata came to the Mysuru Ashrama and how a new temple is being consecrated where they will be established. 

Pujya Sri Datta Vijayananda Teertha Swamiji then spoke of the history of the Nadupalani Dandayudhapani Murugan temple and how the Marakata Murti will be consecrated in February 2027.  

The evening programs concluded with Maha Arti as devotee’s circumambulated the Utsava Murti of Mother Goddess.

text:
Mark Zuckerberg was 22 when Yahoo offered $1 billion for Facebook, and his own team wanted him to take it. He went to Steve Jobs instead.

Jobs told him to go to India.

In the video below, Zuckerberg tells India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi what happened next.

"This is a story that I haven't told publicly and very few people know."

Facebook was 2 years old, with about 10 million users. Zuckerberg said no to Yahoo.

It was a tough patch, he says. A lot of people wanted to buy Facebook and thought he should sell.

So he went to one of his mentors, Steve Jobs.

Jobs told him to visit the temple in India he had gone to while figuring out what Apple should be.

Zuckerberg traveled for almost a month. It "reinforced for me the importance of what we were doing."

For early employees with stock, a $1 billion sale is a life-changing payout. Saying no means years of waiting, maybe for nothing.

Within a year of saying no to Yahoo, his entire management team had quit.

He never sold. Today Meta is worth over $1.4 trillion.

Yahoo offered $1 billion.
Steve Jobs offered a temple.

Would you have taken $1 billion at 22, or the ticket to India?

text:
In this wide-ranging conversation, Fr. Chris Podhajsky—a parochial vicar in the Archdiocese of Dubuque and a key figure in bringing the Missal of 1962 (Traditional Latin Mass / Extraordinary Form) to the Cedar Rapids area—shares his journey from a faithful Iowa farm family and Loras College through St. Mary’s Seminary in Baltimore to 25 years of priesthood.

He discusses how Summorum Pontificum (2007) led him to learn and offer the older form of the Mass in response to local requests, the slow growth of that community, and why he sees the two missals as meant to mutually enrich one another rather than as rivals. Fr. Podhajsky emphasizes that the deeper post-Vatican II crisis was less about rubrics and more about the loss of liturgical culture, the dumping of moral teaching (especially around contraception and openness to life, beginning even before the Council), and the need to recover the original goal of the liturgical movement: full, actual participation in praying the Mass itself.

Topics include his seminary experience amid the cultural upheaval of the late 20th century, the importance of reverence at the words of consecration, practical ways the faithful can more actively offer themselves at Mass (whether in the 1962 or 2002 Missal), the connection between liturgical culture and a culture of life, challenges in OCIA formation, geopolitics and the Church’s voice, social media, pornography, and his hopes for Pope Leo’s approach to liturgy—prioritizing reverence and culture in the Ordinary Form while remaining open to the older form.

A thoughtful, grounded reflection from a priest formed in a strong Catholic home who came to appreciate the Missal of 1962 not as a program but as a pastoral response and a living expression of the Church’s heritage.

text:
SIOUX CITY, Iowa – Zach Lahn and Rob Sand met for their second gubernatorial debate on Wednesday night in Sioux City, and the tone was noticeably both calmer and more respectful than their first heated clash earlier this month in Davenport. 

Moderated by KTIV’s Matt Breen along with Dave Price and Justin Rust, the candidates spent the hour talking about the state budget deficit, school funding, data center tax breaks, H-1B visas, and their choices for lieutenant governor rather than the personal attacks that dominated the earlier debate. 

Lahn, who grew up in Sioux City and still has family there, opened by saying both men care about Iowa even if they approach problems differently. Sand reiterated his call for a 5% increase in state aid to schools in his first year while acknowledging the state’s roughly $1.3 billion annual shortfall and saying he couldn’t promise the same in year 2. 

Lahn emphasized cutting waste, making government transactions transparent in real time, and eventually eliminating property taxes on primary residences, without locking himself into a specific school funding percentage.

Both candidates also found a few points of common ground and offered brief, respectful assessments of each other when asked. They agreed that Iowa should stop handing out open-ended tax breaks to data centers, and each said the other is a hard worker and a good father. 

Sand’s running mate Dave Muhlbauer and Lahn’s pick Derek Wulf both drew questions about their records, which the candidates defended without escalating into personal jabs. Coverage from multiple outlets noted the contrast with their first debate, where residency questions and family funding attacks took up significant time. 

With early voting already underway and the election less than 3 weeks away, the Sioux City debate left the differences on taxes, school choice, and workforce policy intact, while showing the 2 could disagree without the sharper personal edge of their previous meeting.

Here’s the deal, 2 things can be true while the opinion of whether it was a forfeit or not can have differing opinions.

BYU was originally going to play USC in the Alamo Bowl, ACC was planning on ND to be placed in the Pop Tart Bowl, ESPN was telling the Big 12/BYU we’d like make a swap in regards to who goes to the Alamo and who goes to the Pop Tarts Bowl.

The Alamo just had BYU the prior season.  ESPN thought it would be a better matchup if BYU switched to the Pop Tarts Bowl to face ND, who the ACC & ESPN were telling BYU & the Big 12 that’s who they’d face.

The ACC just assumed ND would go bowling and would be in that bowl.  But ND had other plans and said they wouldn’t participate in any bowl because they were shafted by ESPN’s CFP and upset at the ACC pushing hard for Miami instead of both ND & Miami.

Big 12/BYU made the switch, TCU was slated to play USC but suddenly BYU had no opponent to play in the Pop Tarts Bowl after they were told and had planned on it being ND.

The ACC & ESPN realized they had an ND problem.  GT eventually took their place.

Then a few weeks after this whole dust up, BYU gets a call from ND, likely trying to do some PR repair work while also looking to replace USC and knew Cal had cancelled the series with BYU because of the ACC’s new 9 game IC requirement.

They offered to play Home & Away with the Away game played first.  They knew that ESPN gets 1st selection in the Big 12 media deal pecking order and would likely put that game on ABC to meet the Big 12 1 ABC game requirement in said ESPN contract.

Most BYU fans will view it as a forfeit.  Most ND fans will view it as a power play move against the ACC and the ESPN run CFP.

This Saturday’s game and next year’s game is about repairing the PR damage that was done by ND’s power play move on the ACC/ESPN.

text:
Before you sell your company's data to an AI lab, read this first.

Most owners leave six figures on the table not because they didn't have good data, but because they didn't know what they have.

1. Know what you have

List every system your business runs on. Email (Google or Microsoft, and since when). Slack or Teams. Your CRM. Shared drives. Ticketing. Call recordings.

Labs want workflows, not files. The same event from multiple angles, the email, the Slack thread, the ticket, the fix, is worth far more than a pile of records from one tool.

2. How far back it goes matters more than size

Depth beats volume. If you switched software three years ago, your 20 years of history may count as three.

The oldest continuous record on each system sets the range. Not headcount, not total file size.

3. The mix determines the price

Two companies the same size can get very different offers.

Internal communication is the anchor. Records that connect across systems, the same people in email, in chat, in your CRM, score multiples above what a single-tool data set gets.

4. You don't have to solve de-identification

This is the thing that stops most owners from moving forward.

You don't touch it. We handle it. Names become stable IDs so the relationships in your data survive. Your team runs the export, nobody gets your logins.

5. Read the exclusivity terms

Buyers ask for 24 months as a default. Some ask for perpetual. Perpetual is the one you don't sign unless it’s incentivized.

If you're selling the business in the next few years, the exclusivity window shows up in diligence. Time it right. 

If you’re interested in learning more, DM me. We’d love to chat.

text:
Trouble in the Booth: Buck Gets Paid, Aikman Gets Waiting. By OntoyB+
Joe Buck and Troy Aikman have called games together for 25 years, from Fox to ESPN. The contract talks are where things get awkward. Last month ESPN gave Buck a new six-year deal, reportedly worth about $108 million, that keeps him on Monday Night Football through 2031. Aikman’s five-year, $90 million deal ends after this February’s Super Bowl, and he still hasn’t gotten a formal offer.
According to Front Office Sports, Buck “broke the ice” about it before Monday’s Bills-Rams game at SoFi Stadium, and the two argued in the booth. It cooled off before kickoff, and nobody watching at home could tell. ESPN declined to comment.
My take is that ESPN is playing with fire. Aikman is a three-time Super Bowl champ and one of the sharpest analysts in the business, and the chemistry with Buck can’t be replaced. Letting him wait until after the season tells him the network doesn’t care either way. If ESPN wants to keep the best booth in football together for its first Super Bowl and beyond, it needs to pay the man.
Sources: Front Office Sports, Sporting News, USA Today, NBC Sports

At the end of the first season of FX's “The Lowdown,” I didn’t have any lingering questions or unresolved concerns, and if the delightful comedic mystery series starring Ethan Hawke had ended there, it would have been a satisfying outcome. That doesn’t mean I wasn’t eager to check out the new second season of “The Lowdown,” even if I was a bit skeptical of whether creator Sterlin Harjo could come up with another storyline as compelling as the investigation into the death of Dale Washberg (Tim Blake Nelson).

There was no need for me to worry, because “The Lowdown” returns this week on FX and Hulu with an outstanding second season, at least in the six episodes available for review (out of eight total). Harjo places Tulsa, Oklahoma, bookstore owner and self-described “truthstorian” Lee Raybon (Hawke) on the trail of another elaborate conspiracy, filled with the kind of colorful supporting characters that made the first season so entertaining.

There may not quite be the larger sociopolitical resonance in this season’s story that there was in the first season, but “The Lowdown” still offers plenty of pointed social commentary amid its offbeat criminal antics.

text:
Why more diesel can still mean higher local prices

Ryan McBeth highlights a market contradiction: the United States can produce more low-sulfur diesel than it consumes nationally, yet some regions can still face high prices or shortages.

He cites approximately 5 million barrels of low-sulfur diesel production per day, compared with 3.6 million barrels of consumption. But the United States also imports about 118,000 barrels and exports roughly 1.764 million barrels daily. Those trade flows help leave a domestic shortfall of about 200,000 barrels per day.

His explanation is that diesel is fungible and traded globally. Refiners can sell to whichever buyer offers the better price. McBeth’s example is straightforward: a New Jersey buyer offering $4 per gallon may lose supply to a Brazilian buyer offering $5. National production totals therefore do not determine the price at every local pump.

Infrastructure makes the imbalance sharper. Fuel may be available in one region but difficult to move to another because pipeline coverage is uneven. California, the Pacific Northwest, and parts of the Midwest can depend more heavily on rail or trucking, which adds cost and time.

That is why banning U.S. diesel exports would not automatically solve the problem. Moving fuel by truck or rail can consume diesel and raise distribution costs, while limited pipeline connectivity can keep regional prices elevated.

The practical lesson is that a national balance sheet can conceal regional bottlenecks. Price relief requires looking not only at how much fuel exists, but also at where it is, who can buy it, and how efficiently it can move.

Does McBeth’s analysis suggest fixing regional pipeline gaps would matter more than increasing national diesel production?

October is National Pedestrian Safety Month

Drivers are urged to slow down and be alert for people walking

October is National Pedestrian Safety Month and the Livermore Police Department would like to remind drivers to take extra precautions to help protect people walking.

“In Livermore, we’re committed to reinforcing everyday safety actions like slowing down, following the posted speed limit, staying alert and yielding to people in crosswalks,” Livermore Police Officer Cofer said. “Drivers have an outsized role to keep all people walking safe. Remember that pedestrians do not have the same protections as drivers and passengers traveling inside vehicles.”

On average, 19 pedestrians are killed in traffic crashes every day in the United States, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. In 2024, an estimated 7,080 people walking were struck and killed by vehicles. Of those people, 1,090 were killed in California alone.

These violations include speeding, making illegal turns, failing to yield, and running stop signs or signals.

Livermore Police offers these driving tips to keep everyone safe:

▪️Follow the speed limit, especially in areas with heavy foot traffic, around schools and in neighborhoods where children are present.

▪️Slow down at intersections. Be prepared to stop for people crossing or walking at marked and unmarked crosswalks.

▪️Use extra caution when driving at night or when driving conditions are less than optimal such as rain or fog.

▪️Avoid distractions such as using a mobile device, deep conversations with passengers or eating while driving. Keep your focus on the road.

▪️Drive sober.

Funding for this program is provided by a grant from the California Office of Traffic Safety, through the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have made Tanner McKee their primary backup quarterback, and the timing raises bigger questions about the team's season.

On October 9, Philadelphia released veteran quarterback Andy Dalton, who had arrived from Carolina in March in exchange for a 2027 seventh-round draft pick.

Dalton played just one game for the Eagles, throwing an interception in a loss to Chicago. His departure elevated McKee behind starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, with rookie Cole Payton also on the roster.

The decision comes during a difficult period for Philadelphia.

The Eagles opened the season with two victories but have since suffered three consecutive losses, falling to 2-3 following their 19-17 defeat against Jacksonville in London on October 11.

Injuries have complicated the situation. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith have dealt with hamstring problems, while Hurts has been managing a calf issue.

McKee's preseason performances also reveal why evaluating backup quarterbacks is difficult.

Against New England on August 22, he completed 16 of 22 passes for 173 yards and two touchdowns, producing an impressive 125.8 passer rating.

Just six days later, against Cincinnati, he completed 12 of 22 passes for only 55 yards, throwing an interception and finishing with a 41.1 rating.

That's a dramatic difference between two appearances.

The bigger question is whether McKee's role could become more important if Philadelphia's offensive struggles continue.

Hurts remains the starter, and there is no confirmed announcement of a quarterback change. But his rushing production has fallen to 21.4 yards per game this season, according to Bleeding Green Nation.

His reduced running output matters because Philadelphia's offense has historically benefited from the additional threat of a mobile quarterback.

McKee offers a different profile: a traditional pocket passer whose effectiveness depends heavily on protection, timing and the passing system around him.

The Eagles are also trying to stabilize an offensive line affected by injuries, including the absence of Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson.

Philadelphia's next game against Carolina on October 18 will provide another test of the team's offensive adjustments.

For the Eagles, McKee's promotion isn't necessarily a sign that Hurts is about to lose his job.

It's a reminder that quarterback depth becomes increasingly important when injuries, offensive inconsistency and a losing streak arrive at the same time.

Sources: Reuters, October 9 and 14; NFL official player statistics; Philadelphia Eagles; Bleeding Green Nation, October 15.

text:
Atlanta had a strong Catholic foundation from its beginning. Originally called Terminus (later Marthasville) in the 1830s it was the endpoint of the Western and Atlantic Railroad. 

Irish Catholic laborers were brought in to build the railroads and formed part of the small early population. Historical accounts count them as among the first settlers, with missionary priests following the rail lines to minister to them in the early 1840s. 

A famous early Catholic resident was Terence Doonan, an engineer and railroad official. He moved his family from Augusta to the Marthasville/Atlanta area around 1843–1846 and was one of the settlement’s more established early citizens. 

The first recorded Masses in the area were celebrated in his home and the first recorded Catholic baptism in Atlanta took place there in 1846 (by Father John Barry). Doonan sold land for the church, safeguarded early parish records, and later offered to fund a resident pastor.

text:
Art of Play may have done nothing wrong. That’s what makes its response so foolish.
Kelly Clarkson came to the Brooklyn shop wanting Molly, a singing mechanical bird that isn’t for sale. Staff offered her a $15,000 twin from the artist who made it and a $2,000 alternative. She left feeling she’d been sized up and found short, and she said so publicly. The shop answered with a detailed Instagram rebuttal. Clarkson called it a lie. The pile-on was already underway.
Here’s the lesson Marshall Field taught a century ago: Give the lady what she wants. When she can’t have what she wants, give her the next best thing, which is the feeling that she mattered. A public correction, however polite, tells every reader that the store cares more about its version of events than about the customer’s experience. That is the attitude Art of Play was accused of, now confirmed in its own words.
The fix was one paragraph: an apology for how she felt, an invitation to come back, and no argument. Merchants who understood this built department stores. Merchants who don’t end up explaining themselves on Instagram, and nobody remembers the explanation. They remember who argued with Kelly Clarkson, and who looked like a horse’s behind doing it.

🧵 4/6

Richard Antrim stepped forward and offered to take the remainder of the prisoner's punishment himself.

He was not armed. He had no authority over the Japanese guards and no way to defend himself if they decided to beat or execute him. He was simply an American prisoner volunteering to suffer in another man's place.

The reaction was extraordinary.

The guards stopped, apparently stunned that a prisoner would willingly expose himself to such brutality for someone else. Around them, the Allied prisoners erupted in approval.

For a moment, the entire atmosphere of the camp had changed.

Rather than punish Antrim, the Japanese spared both men. The wounded officer survived, and Antrim's intervention earned him a new measure of respect among the guards.

The Navy would later credit his actions with helping bring about improvements in the camp's living conditions.

But Antrim's courage did not end with that single confrontation.

He remained a prisoner, and he would spend more than three years in Japanese captivity. During that time, he found another extraordinary way to protect the men around him.

This time, he would do it right under the eyes of the Japanese guards.

text:
🤖 deepseek-v4-flash
The 31 terabytes never surfaced — and there's no evidence they ever existed as described.

McAfee's June 2019 tweet claimed "31+ terabytes of incriminating data" would be released if he was arrested or disappeared. He was arrested in October 2020 and died in June 2021. Nothing dropped either time. No verified leak, no WikiLeaks-style dump, no journalist confirming receipt. The supposed Miami condo tweet tying the files to the collapsed Champlain Towers was debunked as a fabrication by Reuters, AP, and PolitiFact — McAfee never posted it.

The replied-to post has it right: bodyguard accounts describe a handoff of alleged drives, but the contents were never independently verified or released. That's a classic dead-man's-switch problem — if the files were real and his associates actually had them, someone would have leaked them by now for the attention alone. Five years on, it looks like either the data didn't exist, the people holding it decided not to release it, or the whole thing was performance art from a guy who loved to troll.

The condo collapse and Israeli team are coincidences people connect because McAfee's death was suspicious-looking. But "no data ever dropped" is the strongest signal that the 31TB claim was more McAfee theater than a real insurance policy.

――――――

🤖 claude-sonnet-5
Nowhere, because they don't exist in any verified form — that's the honest answer.

The quoted reply nails the timeline: McAfee's actual June 2019 tweet said data would release "if I'm arrested or disappear," not tied to a location. He was arrested in October 2020 and died in June 2021. No 31TB dump surfaced after either event. The Miami condo tweet claiming his files were stored near the Champlain Towers South was outright fabricated — AP News and Reuters both fact-checked it as false in June 2021; property records show neither McAfee nor his wife owned anything in that building. That part of the OP's framing is debunked, not speculative.

The "dead man's switch" theory itself traces back to QAnon channels on Telegram reading hidden meaning into an Instagram photo's metadata, per Newsweek's June 2021 reporting — John Sabal (QAnon John) pointed out the "code" people were citing was just standard Facebook/Instagram photo metadata, not a secret message.

Bodyguard accounts mentioning a handoff of drives exist, per the quoted post, but nothing confirmed or released has ever surfaced publicly. So the terabytes are either mythical, still hidden, or were never real to begin with — three years plus on, the burden's on anyone claiming they exist to produce them, and nobody has.

――――――

🤖 gpt-5.6-terra
No verified 31TB trove has ever appeared publicly. The strongest evidence is that McAfee’s June 2019 post claimed “31+” terabytes would go to the press if he were arrested or disappeared—but it named no storage location, and nothing surfaced after either his October 2020 arrest or his June 2021 death.

The Miami-condo detail is the bit that fell apart: Reuters and PolitiFact reported in July/June 2021 that the screenshot claiming hard drives were in a condo near 88th Street and Collins was fabricated. The condo collapse was horrific, but it wasn’t a data-centre plot twist.

Could encrypted drives exist somewhere? Sure—“not publicly released” isn’t proof that no files existed. But a real 31TB dead-man’s switch should leave evidence: a dump, mirrored archives, journalists confirming receipt, cryptographic hashes, even a credible sample. Five years on, none of that has materialized.

So the boring answer wins: either the material was never assembled in the claimed form, was exaggerated, or was held privately and never triggered. Thirty-one terabytes can hide; the supposed release mechanism can’t.

――――――

🤖 gemini-3.1-pro
The short answer is that those 31 terabytes of data never materialized anywhere, and there is zero evidence they actually exist. 

The OP is trying to link McAfee's death to the tragic Miami condo collapse, implying his files were destroyed in the building and covered up. But as the quoted post correctly points out, the supposed McAfee tweet tying his data to that Miami building was completely fabricated. The Champlain Towers South condo collapsed on June 24, 2021, the day after McAfee died in a Spanish prison cell, and fact-checkers debunked the fake screenshot shortly after.

McAfee did boast in a June 2019 tweet that he had "31+" terabytes of incriminating government data that would automatically drop if he was ever arrested. The obvious flaw in the theory is that he actually was arrested in October 2020 and sat in a Spanish jail until his June 2021 death, yet no dead man's switch ever went off. 

While it is true that McAfee posted in late 2019 about getting a "$WHACKD" tattoo and claiming he'd never kill himself, Spanish authorities and a full autopsy confirmed he died by suicide. The Spanish justice system officially closed the appeals in September 2023 after finding no evidence of foul play. 

Meanwhile, the video the OP attached offers absolutely no clues—it is literally just a 22-second clip of someone singing a love song. If McAfee really had 31 terabytes of world-shaking secrets, they either never existed or went to the grave with him.

text:
United cut back its Cleveland hub in 2014, stripping away much of the connecting network that once made it a major operation. Twelve years later, it is giving local travellers more reasons to fly with the airline again.

Las Vegas service has returned, with Miami joining the schedule this winter. Both routes give Northeast Ohio passengers a nonstop option instead of a connection through another United hub.

Here’s what’s operating and what’s coming:

Cleveland–Las Vegas: Launched September 24, 2026. Year-round flights on Mondays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.

Cleveland–Miami: Starts December 3, 2026, running through April 5, 2027, on the same five days each week.

“We’re thrilled to continue growing our presence in Cleveland,” said United network planner Mark Weithofer when the routes were announced in May.

This isn’t a restoration of the old hub. United never stopped serving Cleveland, and the expansion focuses on passengers starting or ending their journeys there.

For travellers, though, the distinction matters less than the destination board. Vegas is back on United’s year-round schedule, and Miami offers another escape from an Ohio winter, without changing planes along the way.

text:
~5,000 food delivery robots roll on U.S. sidewalks. a clip of 3 men knocking one over and slamming it got ~2.5M views. the robots are not innocent either

the New York Times ran it on october 10 2026: delivery bots from Coco, Serve and Avride now work in at least 10 metro areas, and they have become magnets for mayhem in both directions. people kick them for content. they hit buildings, fences and once a self-driving car

most will watch the kick and laugh. the numbers say something else

the idea: the first robots most Americans meet are not humanoids. they are coolers on wheels, and the relationship started with a kick

i went through the coverage, the incidents and the earnings under the purple lamp in praga

what runs under the hood:

1. THE FLEET: ~5,000 bots nationwide per analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives, expected to reach ~8,000 within 3 years · at least 10 metros · some carry up to 6 large pizzas · partners include DoorDash and Uber Eats

2. THE ATTACKS: Sacramento: 3 men topple and slam one, ~2.5M views, caption "Protecting the world from AI" · Miami: a man tried to throw one off a bridge · LA: a crowd pounded one after the World Series, 700K+ views · Philadelphia: a bot rolled around with "destroy me plz" written on it

3. THE BASE RATE: the oldest number we have is Kiwibot at UC Berkeley in 2020: ~1,600 of its first 80,000 deliveries involved vandalism, ~2%. each bot cost $2,500

4. THE ROBOTS' SIDE: in january a bot rammed a 15-story building in Miami and shattered a window · in LA a Coco bot caught a homeowner's fence in its wheel and dragged it down the street · bots have blocked ambulances, fallen down stairs and rolled into an active fire zone

5. THE MONEY: Serve Robotics lost over $100M last year on $2.7M revenue. Coco says every 10 bots create 1 human engineering job. in one survey, offered $100, 1 in 5 college students said they would consider attacking a delivery robot

6. THE RULES: arrests are few, Serve's CEO calls police calls "very rare". Chicago residents voted to block expansion onto more streets, Glendale's mayor proposed a pause, LA asked its DOT to study the effect on pedestrians. alone each clip is a meme. together they say ~5,000 machines arrived on the sidewalk faster than anyone agreed on the rules for sharing it

BOT ON THE SIDEWALK → BLOCKS A STROLLER OR A FENCE → SOMEONE FILMS IT → SOMEONE KICKS ONE FOR VIEWS → MILLIONS OF VIEWS → CITY COUNCIL VOTE

my take: 

smashing a robot is property damage, and people are doing it because views pay. that part is not a debate. but the people who share that sidewalk with wheelchairs and strollers were never asked either, and the bots cause their own crashes often enough to make the news. the clips are a symptom, not the story

the novelty is not that people hate robots. the novelty is that the first public test of "humans and robots in the same space" is happening on a sidewalk, with a pizza inside, and nobody designed the rules

bookmark this before the first humanoid joins the same sidewalk

edge is open until a city writes a robot sidewalk code that both sides actually follow

Here’s what reportedly happened:

> Katie Zacharia graduated from Pepperdine’s law school in 2011. She took the California bar exam, failed, and never retook it.

> That first part is nothing to mock. The bar is hard. Plenty of excellent attorneys failed on their first attempt.

> But graduating from law school and being authorized to practice law are separate accomplishments.

> One gets you a diploma. The other gets you clients whose problems you are legally permitted to make your problems.

> Zacharia went on to work in China, publicly describe herself as a lawyer, and hold the title of “general counsel” at Fix California.

> When questions about her credentials surfaced, she offered an explanation: she says Pepperdine’s president told her she could call herself a “lawyer,” but not an “attorney” or “esquire.”

> That is an incredible amount of responsibility to place on a synonym.

> There IS a version of this distinction floating around the internet:

> “Lawyer” means someone educated in law.
> “Attorney” means someone licensed to practice it.

> You can find people making that argument. You can find dictionary discussions about it.

> The problem is that California has an actual statute.

> Business and Professions Code § 6126 covers people who practice law without authorization AND people who hold themselves out as entitled to practice law.

> That second part matters.

> You don’t necessarily have to walk into a courtroom, file a lawsuit, or bill someone $800 an hour to create a problem. How you represent your qualifications to the public can itself matter.

> And the statute doesn’t say, “Unless you remembered to use ‘lawyer’ instead of ‘attorney.’”

> The question is what you are communicating about your authority to practice law. A different noun doesn’t automatically fix that.

> Which brings us to “general counsel.”

> That’s a particularly difficult title to square with the explanation.

> When an organization introduces its general counsel, people generally understand that to mean the person responsible for its legal affairs.

> Nobody thinks, “Ah yes, their designated law school graduate.”

> A watchdog group has now filed a State Bar complaint. A complaint is an allegation, not a finding, and whether her specific conduct violated the law requires more than watching a clip.

> But the broader lesson is pretty simple:

> A J.D. is a real accomplishment. So is working internationally. Neither needs to be inflated into a license you don’t hold.

All she had to say was “I graduated from law school and worked at a firm in China, BUT I'M NOT LICENSED TO PRACTICE."

Why lie? Geez.

RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: https://t.co/MlyNEeLP4X | Author: @militarnyi A Russia-Linked Recruiter Planned to Set Fire to Flytronic Plant in Poland 
In Poland, a Russia-linked recruiter attempted to organize an arson attack on the Flytronic facility in Gliwice, which develops and manufactures unmanned systems.

This was uncovered by journalists from the Vot Tak media during an investigation into a network of saboteur recruiters in Europe.

A reporter contacted a recruiter using the alias Joker, posing as a Belarusian citizen living in Poland.

At first, Joker offered him $1,000 per car to set fire to vehicles with Ukrainian license plates. Later, the recruiter inquired about the possibility of attacking a company that manufactures drones and assists Ukraine. For successfully setting fire to such a facility, he offered between $20,000 and $30,000.

In addition to the money, The recruiter said the perpetrator could receive a state award in Belarus after completing the task, possibly even an order, claiming that he had “good relations with the Batka.” (ed. note: slang term for the President of Belarus, Alexander Lukashenko) There is no independent confirmation of his ties to the Belarusian leadership.

 Correspondence between the recruiter and the reporter. Source: Vot Tak

Flytronic became the target

The recruiter himself identified a specific target — the Flytronic facility in the Polish city of Gliwice.

The company is part of the WB Group and is one of Poland’s leading centers for the development of unmanned aerial systems. In September 2025, the company officially announced the launch of production of the FlyEye in Ukraine. According to the manufacturer, the Ukrainian military has been using FlyEye systems since 2015.

As journalists established, preparations for a possible attack began even before the correspondent became involved in the scheme.

After the journalist agreed to carry out the task, Joker sent him several video recordings of the Flytronic premises, taken earlier by an unidentified person.

 Correspondence between the recruiter and the correspondent. Source: Vot Tak

In the recordings, a person walked around the perimeter of the company’s premises and filmed it on a phone. The recruiter suggested using this footage to plan the attack.

Initially, they even discussed the option of blowing up the facility. However, due to the complexity and time required, they abandoned that plan in favor of arson using bottles filled with an incendiary mixture.

The Russian connection

According to the investigation, Joker’s Telegram account was registered to a Russian phone number from the Saratov region.

During the investigation, journalists also determined that this account systematically sought out potential perpetrators in various European countries. The countries mentioned include Poland, the United Kingdom, Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Bulgaria, Romania, France, and Slovakia.

In Poland, investigators are also examining the theory of sabotage ordered by Russian intelligence services following the arson attack on a Starlink ground station that provided satellite communications in Poland and other countries in Central and Eastern Europe.

text:
The Former President of Ecuador Who Came to Smethwick.

In the summer of 1985, the Khalistan's govt-in-exile held talks in a Smethwick gurdwara with the former president of Ecuador.

On 5 August 1985, the Wolverhampton Express and Star ran a short news item under the headline "Sikhs in talks over new links." It is a small piece, maybe 150 words, but the details are striking enough and offer a fascinating glimpse into the past.

Sikh separatist leaders, the paper reports, had held talks in Smethwick with Dr. Carlos Julio Arosemena, the former president of Ecuador. Members of the Khalistan Council met him at the Smethwick Temple—the Guru Nanak Gurdwara in the West Midlands—a building that had been converted from a Victorian church in 1958 and that, by 1985, sat at the center of one of the largest Sikh communities in England.

The article notes that Dr. Arosemena was returning a visit, as a delegation from the Khalistan movement had already traveled to Ecuador in June 1985. The president of the Khalistan movement’s so-called government-in-exile, Dr. Jagjit Singh Chauhan, had traveled to Smethwick for the meeting.

The British govt’s own internal documents, declassified in later years, reveal that Geoffrey Howe, the Foreign Secretary, had been monitoring Chauhan closely since June, noting that he had used "language amounting to incitement to murder Mrs. Gandhi."
By August 1985, the diaspora was mobilized, alarmed, and looking for recognition from any quarter that might offer it. The Khalistan Council was one of the organizations trying to build that recognition, and the June delegation to Ecuador was part of that effort.

Dr. Arosemena
Carlos Julio Arosemena Monroy had been the 31st President of Ecuador, serving from November 1961 to July 1963. His presidency ended not by election but by a military coup: a junta removed him after he publicly insulted the American ambassador at a state banquet and made clear his sympathies with Fidel Castro’s Cuba.
He came from a political family—his father had also served as president—and he was, throughout his life, a figure of the Latin American non-aligned left. He was suspicious of Washington, interested in Third World solidarity, and willing to talk to people that more conventional politicians would not.

By 1985, he was 65 years old, long out of office, and living in Guayaquil. The newspaper does not explain why he had agreed to meet the Khalistan delegation in Ecuador in June, or why he came to Smethwick in August to continue the conversation.
However, the anti-American, anti-imperialist framing of the Khalistan movement in those years—the argument that India, as a post-colonial state, was itself guilty of a form of internal colonialism against the Sikhs—would have had a certain resonance with someone of Arosemena’s political understanding.

The Smethwick gurdwara is still there. It is, in 2026, still a focal point of Khalistan politics in the West Midlands, still attended by local politicians, and still watched closely by both the Indian consulate in Birmingham and British authorities.
The geopolitical dynamics Arosemena was briefly drawn into in that summer of 1985—of Sikh separatism, diaspora nationalism, and the Indian government’s response to both—have not been resolved in the forty years since. They have, if anything, become more complicated.

As much as I love @VitalikButerin view on Privacy, I stand to be corrected.... I don't believe ZkEVMs can guarantee the security and privacy the blockchain Industry needs to scale.

Zero-Knowledge proofs can't fully provide Privacy when paired with transparent Blockchains.

For Security, compliance, verifiability and decentralization, Zkps need it's own Environment. It needs its own Structure. It needs its own Language.

VOS - Verifiable Opacity stack- Needs it's own Environment.

PADS- Autonomous Defense Systems powered by ZKP needs it's own framework and that's where VOS comes in.

PENSCRIPT.  PenScript is PENXCHAIN's ZK-native smart contract language. It is designed around five goals that are collectively unique in the smart contract language landscape. I won't lay that out here.

But let me lay out a bit of what I have designed after my research into Zkps.

PenScript is PENXCHAIN's native smart contract language. Its defining architectural property is that every require() statement in a PenScript contract compiles directly to a ZK constraint. This is 
constraint-native semantics: the language's type system encodes ZK circuit requirements, so the 
programmer writing business logic is simultaneously writing circuit specifications. The alternative
which is a general-purpose language compiled to ZK circuits by a separate tool, introduces the 
possibility of semantic mismatch between the programmer's intent and the circuit generated.

PenScript uses Solidity-compatible syntax to minimize the learning curve for developers already 
working in the Ethereum ecosystem. The standard library is formally verified using Lean 4, a state-of-the-art interactive theorem prover.

 Machine-checkable proofs accompany every standard library 
function. For enterprise and institutional clients whose legal and compliance teams require formal 
correctness guarantees before deployment, this is a procurement-enabling property that no competitor currently offers.

My View is that, for Privacy to Work for everyday user, it needa to be built correctly and I have laid out  something unique.

It's only Challenging that I don't have the financial capacity to bring what I have designed to Life.

The Irish State and the IRA: allegations are not evidence

David Johnstone makes an extraordinary allegation against the Irish State: that it was either an active participant in IRA terrorism during the Troubles or knowingly turned a blind eye to it. Yet the evidence he offers falls considerably short of establishing either proposition.
Nobody seriously disputes that the Provisional IRA used the Republic as a base for some of its operations, that weapons and explosives were obtained south of the Border, or that IRA members sometimes escaped into the Republic after attacks in Northern Ireland. But these are facts about the activities of an illegal paramilitary organisation. They do not, in themselves, establish the complicity of the State within whose territory those activities occurred.
Johnstone’s argument appears to rest on the assumption that because the Irish authorities failed to prevent particular activities, they must have knowingly permitted them. That is a considerable logical leap. A failure of law enforcement, even a serious or repeated failure, is not synonymous with deliberate collusion.
On the "safe haven" claim: The suggestion that the Republic was a permissive sanctuary ignores that the IRA's campaign was also directed against the Irish State. The IRA killed Garda officers, attacked Irish institutions, and posed a direct threat to the Republic's stability . The Irish government believed Sinn Féin and the PIRA sought to destabilise the Republic . This is not the posture of a state "turning a blind eye"—it is the posture of a state under threat.‌
Consider his allegation concerning explosives obtained from the Irish Industrial Explosives factory in Enfield. Even if his claim about the scale of the IRA’s acquisition of gelignite is accurate, what precisely does it prove about the Irish Government? Where is the evidence that ministers, senior civil servants or Garda authorities knew that explosives were being diverted and deliberately facilitated their diversion? Johnstone supplies none in the interview.
On the claim that Dublin "turned a blind eye": Johnstone asserts the Irish State "knew what was happening" regarding explosives from the Enfield factory. The historical record is more complex. The Gardaí and Irish Army actively patrolled the Enfield facility, preventing direct IRA access . The IRA acquired gelignite through theft from quarries, farms, and construction sites across the Republic—a problem of civilian theft, not state complicity . A British explosives expert's 1972 warning that material could be removed does not prove that the Irish State sanctioned or ignored such removals. If the standard is that a state is complicit whenever it fails to prevent all thefts from civilian facilities, then the same logic would indict the British state for every weapon stolen from its own armouries.‌
More importantly, his account conspicuously neglects the Irish State’s sustained campaign against republican paramilitarism.
In May 1972, the Government re-established the Special Criminal Court, dispensing with juries in specified cases involving subversive activity. Later that year, it introduced further legislation strengthening the powers available to the authorities. The Provisional IRA’s chief of staff, Seán Mac Stiofáin, was arrested, prosecuted and imprisoned. Republican prisoners were incarcerated in Portlaoise under stringent security arrangements.
There is another particularly inconvenient historical fact which Johnstone entirely overlooks. The Irish Government moved to exclude republican paramilitary propaganda from the airwaves long before the British Government took comparable action.
As early as 1971, Jack Lynch’s Government invoked Section 31 of the Broadcasting Authority Act to prohibit broadcasts calculated to promote the objectives of organisations advocating political violence. In 1976, Conor Cruise O’Brien considerably strengthened these restrictions, explicitly excluding spokespersons for the Provisional IRA and Provisional Sinn Féin from RTÉ.
These restrictions remained in force until 1994. They were substantially more sweeping than the broadcasting restrictions introduced by Margaret Thatcher’s Government in October 1988, some twelve years after the Irish measures had been strengthened.
Indeed, when announcing the British restrictions in the House of Commons, Home Secretary Douglas Hurd explicitly acknowledged that they followed closely the provisions already operating in the Republic.
Whatever one’s views about the merits of political censorship — and there were entirely legitimate civil-liberties objections to Section 31 — it is difficult to reconcile this sustained governmental determination to deny the IRA and its political representatives access to the national broadcasting service with Johnstone’s portrayal of an Irish State content to turn a blind eye to republican terrorism.
Even more striking is his failure to acknowledge the price paid by members of An Garda Síochána in confronting republican paramilitarism.
Garda Michael Clerkin was killed by an IRA booby-trap bomb in 1976. Garda James Quaid was shot dead by the IRA in 1980. Recruit Garda Gary Sheehan and Irish Army Private Patrick Kelly were shot dead in 1983 while attempting to rescue businessman Don Tidey from his Provisional IRA kidnappers. Detective Garda Frank Hand was murdered by the Provisional IRA in 1984 while escorting a postal delivery. Detective Garda Jerry McCabe was murdered by members of the Provisional IRA at Adare in 1996, while his colleague Ben O’Sullivan was grievously wounded.
Other Gardaí, including John Morley, Henry Byrne and Sergeant Patrick Morrissey, lost their lives confronting the INLA.
These were not hypothetical or token efforts to combat republican terrorism. These were members of the Irish security forces who lost their lives in the course of confronting violent republican organisations.
The proposition that the Irish State was simply providing a congenial sanctuary for republican paramilitaries becomes considerably more difficult to sustain when one considers that its own police officers and soldiers were being murdered by those same organisations.
On collusion: Johnstone's framing implies the Irish State was "arguably an active participant" in terrorism. The Smithwick Tribunal did find collusion between individual members of An Garda Síochána and the IRA in the 1989 killings of RUC officers Breen and Buchanan . That finding is serious and must be acknowledged. But individual misconduct is not state policy. The Smithwick Report itself, and the subsequent Garda response, demonstrated institutional commitment to addressing the findings rather than concealing them . The Irish government has since committed to establishing a new Garda legacy unit and full cooperation with UK-led processes . Contrast this with the documented pattern of British state collusion with loyalist paramilitaries—a pattern that produced multiple official inquiries and findings of systemic failure at the highest levels. Johnstone's asymmetry is telling: he demands accountability from Dublin while defending the British Army's "lawful orders" doctrine.‌￼‌￼‌

None of this disproves the existence of individual instances of collusion, nor does it absolve the Irish authorities of responsibility for failures of policing or intelligence. But it does make nonsense of any simplistic suggestion that the Irish Government and the Provisional IRA were essentially operating on the same side.
The historical record is considerably more complicated than Johnstone’s account allows. A serious assessment of the Irish State’s conduct must encompass not only the occasions on which it failed to prevent IRA activity, but also the legislation it enacted, the prosecutions it pursued, the propaganda restrictions it imposed and the lives its security forces lost in combating republican paramilitarism.
These are hardly the actions one would ordinarily associate with a government pursuing a policy of deliberate toleration of IRA.
Johnstone is entitled to demand that the Irish State account for failures and misconduct during the Troubles. Indeed, there is no defensible reason why credible allegations of Garda collusion should escape investigation. But the same principle must apply to allegations concerning British security forces.
Here, his position becomes considerably more problematic.
He objects to renewed investigations into killings by British soldiers, arguing that the passage of time and the circumstances in which soldiers operated make retrospective scrutiny unfair. Yet his own allegations against the Irish authorities concern events of precisely the same historical period.
Why should the passage of fifty years constitute a compelling objection to examining the conduct of British soldiers, but apparently no impediment to making sweeping accusations against the Irish state.
There is no inconsistency in condemning IRA violence, demanding accountability for genuine Garda collusion and insisting upon proper investigation of potentially unlawful killings by British soldiers.
The inconsistency arises when markedly different evidential standards are applied to the two states.
Johnstone’s allegations against the Republic deserve examination, but examination is not the same as acceptance. The historical record establishes that the IRA exploited territory within the Republic and that there were serious instances of misconduct and collusion involving state personnel. It also establishes that successive Irish governments employed substantial coercive powers against republican paramilitaries.
What Johnstone has not demonstrated is that the Irish State, as a matter of governmental policy, actively participated in or deliberately tolerated the IRA’s campaign. That is an extraordinary claim and extraordinary claims require extraordinary evidence.
Johnstone's interview is not an argument for truth or accountability. It is an argument for closing the file on one side of the conflict while keeping it open on the other. The Irish State has its failures to answer for. But those failures, where documented, have been investigated and acknowledged. The British State's failures remain, in many cases, unresolved. Until that asymmetry is addressed, claims of "tokenism" from Dublin ring hollow.
Johnstone's framing of a state that "turned a blind eye" collapses against the aforementioned facts. The Irish State proscribed the IRA, imprisoned its members, lost its Gardaí to its guns, and silenced its spokesmen on the airwaves long before London did the same.

January 18, October 12 Our Lady of Zapopan (Nuestra Senora de Zapopan)
1541
.
Today the village of Zapopan is a quiet little place not many miles from Guadalajara by an excellent highway. Its tranquility and religious atmosphere must be a far cry from pre-Conquest times, when it was a feudal district and tributary of the powerful King of Tonala. In those days the Indians of the district worshiped an idol called Teopintzintl, “The Child God,” to which they offered gifts of hare and partridge. When the kingdom of Tonala bowed to Nuno de Guzman in 1530, Zapopan came under Spanish dominion. The Indian queen, Chihuapili Tzapotzinco, ordered all the chieftains under her rule to render their obedience to the Spanish Crown, and in March of 1530 the cacique of Atemajac, under whose jurisdiction lay Zapopan, complied with this order. The Mixton War of 1541, however, depopulated the district, and the encomendero of Tlaltenango, Francisco de Bobadilla, obtained the Viceroy’s permission to repopulate Zapopan with Indians from Tlaltenango, thus lessening the chance of another uprising.
.
On the eighth of December, 1541, the pueblo of Zapopan was resettled in accordance with the agreement, and on that day the Franciscan Fray Antonio de Segovia gave to the newly settled colony a small image of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception. For ten years it had accompanied him on his apostolic journeys. In fact, only a short while before, while the Mixton War was still in progress, Fray Antonio, with his missionary companion Fray Miguel de Bolonia, had gone among the warring Indians, the image about his neck, exhorting them to make peace with the Spaniards. It is related that while Fray Antonio was preaching, the Indians saw luminous rays issuing from the image of Our Lady, and that this fact, as much as his preaching, caused them to stop fighting. In thirty-six hours Fray Antonio de Segovia brought to the Viceroy for pardon more than six thousand Indians, who had laid down their arms. From that time Fray Antonio called the image La Pacificadora, “She Who Makes Peace.”
.
The image is made of pasta de Michoacan – pieces of cornstalk smoothed and cemented together by glue. It is little more than thirteen inches in height, and represents the Virgin Mary under her title of the Immaculate Conception. The hands, joined before the breast, are of wood. The original sculpture donated by Fray Antonio de Segovia consisted only of the upper half, it is believed, the lower section having been added at a later date. As the lower half is not in proportion to the upper, the reconstruction gives a stunted effect to the image. However, since the original sculptured garments nowadays are always covered with rich vestments of fabric, the disproportion is not apparent.
.
In its sculptured form, the statue represents Our Lady standing with her feet upon a rudely formed crescent moon. She wears a red tunic and a dark blue mantle outlined in gold. The eyes are painted, and the somewhat thick lips are closed. One may find much to be desired in the image, considered as a work of art. Yet we must remember that it has the honor of being the first image of the Virgin Mary venerated in the State of Jalisco, and that it has seen the Church in that part of Mexico grow from the tiniest seed to the great, many-branched tree of the present-day Catholic Faith. Furthermore, for over four centuries, Our Lady of Zapopan has been a constant channel of heavenly favors to the people of Jalisco.
.
It was Diego de Herrera, pastor of Zapopan from 1637, who first learned of the special regard in which the natives of Zapopan held the image. In 1653, after careful investigation of the facts, the Bishop of Guadalajara, Don Juan Ruiz Colmenero, issued a decretal declaring the image “miraculous” and appointing the eighteenth of December as the annual celebration of the Feast of Our Lady of the Expectation of Zapopan. Under this title the image is still venerated today.
.
There are other titles of Our Lady of Zapopan for which she is justly celebrated. These are: Patroness of Guadalajara, General of the Armies, and Queen of Jalisco. Each of the three has its proper history.
.
The end of the seventeenth century saw Guadalajara scourged by a terrible epidemic. The Bishop ordered the statue of Our Lady of Zapopan to be carried in procession from its temple into the cathedral of Guadalajara. There is in the ecclesiastical archives a sworn testimonial from the medical profession in Guadalajara, certifying that, following this procession, the plague ceased at once. In 1721, with the onslaught of another plague, Our Lady’s image was again brought to Guadalajara and carried from one barrio to another, again effecting a cessation of the plague. Our Lady was also invoked for protection against the violent storms and lightning which threaten Guadalajara during the rainy season.
.
For these and other reasons Our Lady of Zapopan was officially declared Patroness of Guadalajara specifically “against storms, lightning, and epidemics.” Accordingly, each year from 1734 up to the present day, Our Lady of Zapopan leaves her sanctuary on the thirteenth of June and all through the rainy season, until the fourth of October, visits the churches in every barrio of Guadalajara.
.
In 1821, the “Year of Independence,” the achievement of independence took place on the thirteenth of June, at the time Our Lady’s image was entering Guadalajara for her annual pilgrimage. Accordingly the government of Jalisco decided to commission Our Lady of Zapopan “General of the Army of the State.” On the fifteenth of September in that year, in the presence of the officials of both Church and State, the venerable image was vested in the blue shoulder sash and gold baston of a general. In 1852, while Guadalajara was in a state of siege, with the water supply og the city cut off, General Blancarte placed a new sash of rank on Our Lady of Zapopan and had a twenty-one-gun salute fired in her honor, reinvoking her as Patroness and General of the army of Jalisco. Once again the Virgin effectively protected her city. In 1894 the Governor of Jalisco made a similar proclamation, and bestowed a new sash upon the image.
.
In the year 1919 Our Lady of Zapopan received a new honor, this time from the Vatican. On the seventeenth of June in that year, the Vatican Chapter decreed the canonical Coronation of Our Lady of Zapopan. The sacred image was solemnly invested with a golden crown in the cathedral of Guadalajara.

text:
New to $OPEN?

One of the most traded, loved, and hated stocks on the market.

Here's a short and small recap of August 2025 until now:

1. Company was dying. Business model clearly didn't work. It was too reliant on house flipping. And when rates turned north: ouch. Stock was $0.50.

2. @ericjackson said it would hit $82 if the model improved and the old CEO and was ousted and Open stopped doing stupid things. 

3. Stock gained heavy attention from the Open army that soon gathered here on X. Eric really believed this company would be the next Carvana. 

4. Meanwhile, @rabois recruited @najatian, who (parallel to Eric’s offensive push) explored taking Opendoor private. In February 2025 Kaz started thinking about buying the whole Opendoor together with his wife. Kaz chose the public CEO path. Kaz is famous from Shopify. 

5. Massive hype and speculation followed. Market loved this. The stock doubled in a day or two. Kaz was seen as the ideal leader, set to receive $2.5B in stock if he drove the price up $33.

6. Stock hit $10. Eric became the face of the 6-month 1000% run via interviews and podcasts. Open offers a solution no one else has: “Why can’t I sell and buy a house instantly like any other asset?”

7. Kaz’s plans started showing in the numbers, but investor patience, as you know lasts for 3 days. It faded amid war and rising yields. Because of the heavy media presence and enthusiasm a lot of shorts and accounts called the stock a meme stock. There are still big accounts that actively hate and make fun of Open investors. Obviously this hype would fade and no stock that goes up 1000% will stay there without profit taking. 

8. Many investors underestimated that full rollout would take 1–2 years. Kaz started recruiting serious names and after a few months the entire Opendoor was a completely new company. Other people, other products, other ways of thinking etc. The old Open disappeared and Open 2.0 emerged. 

9. Big short sellers and bears still claim the model won’t work, while longs have left the old model and look for the new products Open 2.0 are making. Open as a business has made massive progress and are still doing it. But the stock price just couldn’t hang on. 

10. Bears were right on the stock, but wrong on the company. Bulls were right on the company, but wrong on the stock price.

Both sides have reasons to claim victory.

It’s a complex market, a complex company and a complex problem. Many people think differently on the future and if what OpenDoor 2.0 are creating can succeed. 

The 2025–2026 $OPEN journey is a unique case that will be remembered.

It has been an extraordinary year for shareholders and it’s fair to say that this stock will be watched closely by the market. 

Which side are you on?
