text:
Governance and Priority Committee Update
The Governance and Priorities Committee met today, and most of the speakers came for one item: the Annual Funding for Homelessness Response. I want to thank everyone who spoke or wrote in. I respect the passion people brought, and I know this issue weighs on a lot of us. Reconciliation is part of this conversation too, and it was on my mind throughout.
Many of the comments reflected compassion and a desire to help the homeless, but also some misunderstanding of what the City has the authority to do. Health care, mental health treatment, addictions services, rent control, transitional housing, supportive housing, and income supports are provincial responsibilities. We can't fix a system we don't control.
The Fire Chief and the City Manager explained why encampments are taken down, and their reasoning is well established. Their study and experience with centralized encampments show they are unsafe for the people living in them, for the neighbours around them, and for the first responders who attend calls there. They also mentioned gang activity, disease spreading quickly and vermon bites are common in those conditions. Compassion on those calls is a primary responsibility for our crews, and the City's policy and protocols for interacting with people experiencing homelessness are built around dignity and compassion.
At the Avenue K encampment, fire crews described open drug use, tent fires, and residents of the encampment bringing in heating elements and building materials being used in unsafe ways. The fire department shared photos and body cam footage from the site. They showed many discarded needles and other drug paraphernalia, propane tanks hooked up to barbecues as a heat source, a long line of flammable garbage along the back lane, a huge amount of bike parts and tires, and several photos of discarded meth packaging. A nearby elementary school, along with area residents, raised concerns numberous times during the encampment's existence.
According to Administration and Fire, people were not moved along with nowhere to go. The shelters were not full at the time, and the Province confirmed there was space and support for all 120 people at the time when the camp was taken down. The Salvation Army works with the Province to provide space, including hotel rooms if needed. The fire department and the Salvation Army both offer help before cleanups and again on the day itself, and very few people accept it. During the October 7 cleanup, only 2 people accepted support. Another 7 went after the cleanup to the Salvation Army for help, with 3 placed in shelter and 4 in a hotel. Administration also noted that the Saskatoon Tribal Council, Central Urban Métis Federation Inc. (CUMFI) and other partner organizations agree that encampments are unsafe.
As well, the larger police presence during the October 7th cleanup was deemed necessary because of what happened on the first attempt to clean it up on September 24. Only 6 police officers were there in Sept. along with Fire and contractor personnel to do the original cleanup, and they faced roughly 120 people and protesters who illegally took over contractor equipment and climbed all over it while forming a human chain. That established that the situation was unsafe and that some people were willing to break the law. Due to that scenario, a larger police presence was deemed to be necessary for the clean up in Oct.
As to the summer bathroom and shower program which was covered by the report on this item, Administration was asked about security costs. The City pays half, and our portion comes to $216,000 for the 139 days it operated. That covers four peacekeepers for each shift, covering 24 hours a day.
A related report went to the Standing Policy Committee on Environment, Utilities and Corporate Services last week proposing two additional public washroom locations remain open, separate from the summer washroom I mentioned above. Each is open from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m., and security at each location currently costs $276,000. Because these are City public washrooms, the City carries that full cost. Administration estimated that moving to 24 hours a day availability for those bathrooms would cost roughly $500,000 per location.
These items come back during budget next month for final approval.
We also had a historical report of the DEED project and while it was informative, it was an information item only and had no speakers. If you're interested in the history of the project, you can access the agenda for today's meeting online and review it.
There was also a public update on the Muskeg Lake Cree Nation's MOU with the City about what a partnership in the DEED could be. Every aspect is being considered including owner / operator options to reduce the City's contribution. The MOU expires June 2027 and no proposal or further details are available at this time.
Otherwise, we discussed a number of Council appointments for 2027 to the various committees and city boards, which will be reported at Council in the near future.

text:
Trump’s Democracy-for-Diesel Deal Shames Us All

Listen · 5:57 min
15OCT2026 
By Thomas L. Friedman
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/OGkgPRDr08

If President Trump does not understand what will happen to him if he proceeds with his plan to trade away support for Ukraine’s democracy for Russian diesel, let me spell it out: He will enter the history books in the chapter on leaders who sold out their country’s democratic values to appease a dictator.

Donald Trump, meet Neville Chamberlain. When future students search online for “sellout,” “appeaser” or “traitor to his country’s core values,” their two pictures will come up first, side by side. And deservedly so. At least Chamberlain was trying, in what proved to be lethally misguided fashion, to avoid a world war. Trump is trying to avoid losing a few seats in Congress — and is likely to be no more successful in achieving his goal than Chamberlain was in achieving his.

I have never believed that Trump was somehow an agent of Russia’s leader, Vladimir Putin, or in his pay. It is much worse. He simply does not cherish democracy. He cherishes money. And he has no problem selling the first for the second. When he acts in his own commercial interests, that’s his personal business. When he uses the American presidency to make a buck, it is our collective shame.

There is simply no core American value Trump will not sell. Desperate to lower diesel prices, which are hurting Republicans in the midterms, Trump actually made a deal to import diesel fuel from Russia, even though it offers a potential windfall for the Kremlin so it can bomb Ukraine harder — and is unlikely to help lower prices or increase supplies much at all. Worse, his aides then asked Ukraine to refrain from attacks on Russia’s oil refineries, without Trump making the same demand of Putin regarding Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. It makes me sick to my stomach to even type this.

Unique among great powers, “the United States has always made the protection and promotion of liberal values part of its foreign policy because it’s part of the country’s political DNA,” Michael Mandelbaum, the author of the new book “The American Way of Foreign Policy: Ideology, Economics, Democracy,” told me. “Different presidents have given these values different emphases, depending on the circumstances and their own personal predilections.”

But none have “ever abandoned them entirely — let alone repudiated them,” Mandelbaum added. “In that sense Trump really is unique. Of course, all presidents, including him, have operated in a domestic political environment in which those values are widely shared, which means that he will pay a political price for violating them. But in the short term that isn’t likely to help Ukraine.”

This is shocking to Ukrainians, who for nearly five years have been resisting Putin’s attempt to wipe their country off the map. My friend Vitaly Sych, the editor in chief of the Ukrainian news outlet NV, texted me from Kyiv the other day:

“When Donald Trump became president, Ukraine lost an ally.” From his first days in office, Trump “started positioning himself as a ‘negotiator,’ as an ‘intermediary’ between Ukraine and the aggressor — Russia,” Sych added. “That was strange enough. And now he is openly siding with Russia, pushing for Ukraine’s capitulation and calling it a peace deal,” Sych said. “If Ukraine hits an oil refinery in Russia, there is always an outraged post from the U.S. president on Truth Social. Is he now the Kremlin’s spokesperson?”

The United States has long stood for freedom and democracy, Sych said. “Now they are just for diesel. What a change.” Russian missiles and drones kill or wound dozens of civilians, including children, every day, he wrote. “Russians are killing us like in a shooting range. No concern comes out about this from the White House. Only about Russian diesel. It is a mix of intellectual and moral bankruptcy to claim we don’t want peace. Of course we want peace,” he said. “But we don’t want capitulation packaged as peace.”

I have to say, it is hard for me to decide who is more despicable: Trump or tough-guy Republican senators like Tom Cotton, who lambasted President Joe Biden for not sending enough military aid to Ukraine and today sits curled up in a corner of the U.S. Capitol, saying nothing while Trump sells Ukraine to Putin outright.

Here’s the beginning of a story in The Hill from Sept. 16, 2023:

A group of Republican senators sent a letter to President Biden Saturday urging him to “immediately” provide the missiles Ukraine needs to win its war against Russia. Senator Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) shared the letter in a post on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, arguing that not sending the weapons would “only prolong the war and cost lives.” Cotton was joined by Senators Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) in his request. “We … urge you to immediately send MGM-140 Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) to Ukraine,” they wrote. “Additional delay will only further undermine U.S. national security interests and extend this conflict.”

That was then — when Biden was president. This week a bipartisan group of 12 senators (six Republicans and six Democrats) sent a letter to Trump demanding that he rescind the diesel agreement and roll back the Treasury Department’s license allowing it. Cotton, who is the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee, did not sign the letter.

It is hard to tell whether Trump’s democracy-for-diesel idea is his alone or was cooked up with his negotiators, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. If those two are part of it, I hope they understand that they will share Trump’s infamy in the history books. The good work they have done to end the Gaza war will all be forgotten. They should speak up now, because history will have its eyes on them, too.

text:
My neighbor lent her younger brother $38,000 to buy a house.

Three months later, he hired a lawyer to threaten her for telling their family he owed her money.

The reason he gave was that the $38,000 had been a gift.

What made the situation worse was that their mother took his side.

Denise, 42, lives in Columbus, Ohio. She works as a hospital administrator and had spent years rebuilding her finances after her divorce.

Her younger brother, Marcus, was 34 when he found a house listed for $287,000. He had a steady job, but he was short on the down payment and closing costs.

Their mother called Denise and begged her to help.

“You know he’s been struggling. This house could finally give him some stability.”

Denise initially offered $10,000. Marcus called her the following evening and explained that he needed $38,000 to close the deal.

“I’ll pay you back,” he promised. “Give me two years. I just need somebody to believe in me.”

Denise had helped him before. She paid part of his college expenses, covered his rent when he lost his job, and helped him buy his first car.

She believed him.

She transferred the money in three installments and kept the bank receipts. But because he was her brother, she never insisted on signing a formal loan agreement.

For the first two months, Marcus treated her like a hero.

He invited her over to see the house, thanked her repeatedly, and told relatives that without his sister, he would still be renting.

Then, at a family gathering, their aunt congratulated him on becoming a homeowner.

Denise smiled and said, “I’m just waiting for my $38,000 back.”

Everybody laughed.

Marcus didn’t.

The following morning, her phone rang.

“Why are you telling people I owe you money?” he demanded.

Denise thought he was joking.

Until he said, “You gave me that money. You can’t start changing the story now.”

text:
In years gone past this is the time of year I'd be heading to the USA for the winter.

For context, my whole life I wanted to go to the USA. My whole caddie life I wanted to go and caddie there.

Never thought I'd achieve either. I had kids and a wife and a life.

But in 2017 the opportunity came. My mate Andy, a Carnoustie lad, was going back out to caddie at Secession in South Carolina. And I should go.

I got my caddie master Ailsa Roy to write me a letter of recommendation, and I also got former Ryder Cup player David Gilford to write for me as well.

I got word back from the caddie master Greg Crum. RIP.

I was finally, in my mid 30s, going to the USA.

But let me tell you how I got there. Because the journey is the story.

As I said, wife, kids, and at the time money was tight. I needed the cheapest possible route.

Six hour Megabus from Dundee to Manchester. Fifteen pounds. Cramped and uncomfortable.

Three hour wait in Manchester.

Flight to Lisbon. Fifteen hours to wait in Lisbon for my connection.

Flight to JFK. Two hours in immigration.

Eight hour wait at JFK.

A couple of hours to Savannah.

Hour Uber from Savannah to Beaufort.

54 straight hours of travelling to get there.

I arrived at the Super 8 motel at around midnight with a few hundred dollars in my hand.

I had to ask the staff if I could pay night by night.

I had not slept in two days. My back was destroying me. And I was praying for work fast, because if it didn't come I was homeless.

So I decided to walk to the course. No idea how far it was.

First time in America. South Carolina in early October. I was dying in the heat. A mile and a half, mostly no pavements, over a big bridge. Walking along roads genuinely worried a snake or an alligator would get me.

I got to the course, met Greg, got my white boiler suit and was told I would be out tomorrow with Russ the assistant caddie master.

Started walking back to the Super 8. Tired, in pain, not slept in two days.

Halfway back a car stops. A pastor from a local church. He took one look at me and offered me a lift. Dropped me back at the motel.

Thank God. Literally.

Five hours sleep. Back still killing me. Walk to the course. White jumpsuit on.

Now picture it.

I'm stood on that course for the first time, carrying two bags for the first time in my life, and I have never seen a single hole on this golf course.

There is no course guide at Secession.

I've got Andy's original Bushnell rangefinder. The thing is huge.

It's 90 degrees. I'm an overweight pasty white Scotsman. And there are alligators everywhere.

I'm trying to caddie for two people for the first time, on a course I did not know, with greens that defied gravity and balls that broke uphill.

Let's just say I wasn't great.

Russ said if you're coming from Scotland you better be better than what we have or there's no point in you being here.

His polite way of saying be better if you want to stay.

He was a good man, Russ. Retired marine. Great golfer. Drove a red Corvette. Drove a Harley.

I've got a wife and three kids back home in Scotland, and I was questioning my life choices hard.

David, what the f have you done. Why did you think this was a good idea.

What helped was a Glasgow boy called Paul who lived out there full time. I stayed with him after a night or two in the motel, and the work came pretty quickly.

Two Scots in South Carolina. Ancient tribal rivalry dissolved instantly. That is what happens when you put two Scots in a foreign country. You are strangers at home but family the moment you are both surrounded by alligators and grain on the greens.

And the greens. My God did they kill me.

Speed and grain. I'd never seen anything like it.

They made me look stupid regularly for the first month or so. It killed me inside. I hate bad reads. And every one felt bad to me at that point. It was a real dent to my confidence.

I was back to feeling like a 14 year old kid with no idea what I was doing.

Thousands of miles from home. Away from my kids for the first time ever. The heat and the humidity. Not knowing how much work I would get. Two bags, learning a new course. What felt like 100 mile walks all the time just to get around.

Sun glaring off the marshland. Stink eye from a few of the American caddies who were not delighted about the Scottish invasion.

I had to learn the basics for myself.

Dark side into the grain. Shiny side down grain.

And my friend Steve saved me out there. We started working together.

Steve is an ex pro. Shot a 63 at Carnoustie off a composite of the Hogans and the whites. He was a tour caddie for a bit. He is the best green reader I have ever seen. Just a master.

I learned a great deal from my time working with Steve. His mind is also sharp.

He also loved the banter with the players. I've seen him savage a few over the years.

One of my favourite people in the world.

And then there was Gdub. George. Proper South Carolina man. Family man. Redneck in the best possible sense, a working man who earned his colour from the sun. Salt of the earth.

He took me out on his boat. He showed me real southern hospitality and a real taste of America. He would also flip an alligator on its back for twenty dollars on the course. Absolutely crazy in the best possible way. One of my favourite people I have ever met in this game.

They call Secession Golf Club Disneyland for adults. Gibbes Island, Beaufort, South Carolina. Walking only. Holes named after Civil War battles. Tees named after generals. A course built on the mythology of Southern independence, set in the tidal marshes of the Lowcountry. And it has a special feeling around the place that is hard to put into words until you have been there.

As a Scottish caddie there you are elevated a little. Americans love Scottish caddies. They appreciate the relationship in a way that is genuinely touching. They want to buy you a beer at the end. They treat you like a professional.

Some of the American caddies did not love us. I understand why, we were getting requested for a lot of the good bags. But others became genuine friends.

It was also a serious drinking club. Guys from Chicago, New York, Atlanta, all over, coming in for two or three days. A very particular kind of place.

By the end of my time there I had the greens figured out. Got used to the heat. Got used to the culture.

The dream of going to America, ticked.

Next to Scottish people, Americans are my favourite people in the world. If I could not live in Scotland I would live in South Carolina.

text:
A Poker Champion, a Senator, a President, and a $6.25 Billion Gift.

On Dec 2nd, 2025, Michael and Susan Dell announced their $6.25 billion gift to 25 million American children. 

This is the story of what happened behind the scenes. It has been years in the making.

This story puts together a timeline of events of how Poker Champion Phil Hellmuth, Senator Ted Cruz, Investor Brad Gerstner, President Donald Trump, and others helped Michael and Susan Dell make their $6.25B gift a reality.

A family discussion helped start the idea
2020–2021—About five years before the announcement

Investor Brad Gerstner and his son Lincoln discussed the investment account established for Lincoln at birth. 

What about children without that advantage?

Gerstner proposed an investment account for every American child, with $1,000 from the government at birth. Families, employers, and donors could add money.

Michael and Susan Dell learned about the plan
2021—About four years before the announcement

Gerstner discussed the idea with the Dells. They supported it years before announcing their gift.

The proposal offered children something they could own and watch grow. But it still needed political support and a national system.

The team organized, but progress was limited
2023–2024—About two years before the announcement

Gerstner established the Invest America Foundation. Matt Lira helped organize support across government, business, and other groups.

Gerstner later said they tried to advance the proposal during the Biden administration. Those efforts did not produce the law they wanted.

Phil Hellmuth brought the idea to a poker game
April 2024—About 600 days before the announcement

According to Senator Ted Cruz, poker champion Phil Hellmuth told him about Invest America during a late card game.

A few weeks later, Gerstner travelled to Washington to explain the proposal.

Cruz became a leading advocate. The poker conversation helped connect an existing idea to a senator who would work to make it law.

Michael Dell helped secure presidential support
April 2025—About 230 days before the announcement

Gerstner later said Dell helped arrange discussions with President Donald Trump.

According to Gerstner, Trump supported the proposal and called House Speaker Mike Johnson. He wanted the accounts included in the larger tax and spending bill.

The team already had draft legislation. That preparation helped them act when the opportunity arrived.

The proposal entered Congress
12 May 2025—204 days before the announcement

Cruz introduced the Invest America Act.
A version also appeared in the House tax package. 

Michael Dell publicly supported it.

The larger bill gave the account program a route through Congress. Johnson, House Ways and Means Chairman Jason Smith, and Representative Blake Moore helped advance the provisions.

Business leaders made their support public
9 June 2025—176 days before the announcement

At a White House meeting, Trump credited Michael Dell with bringing the idea to his attention. Dell credited Gerstner with leading the effort.

Goldman Sachs chief executive David Solomon and Uber chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi also participated.

That June, Dell Technologies committed to match the government’s $1,000 contribution for qualifying newborn children of U.S. employees. This was separate from the Dells’ later personal gift.

The accounts became law
4 July 2025—151 days before the announcement

Trump signed the legislation that created Trump Accounts.

The federal program would provide $1,000 for eligible children born from 2025 through 2028.

Older eligible children could have accounts, but they would miss that federal starting contribution. This gap became central to the Dells’ gift.

The participants explained how difficult the goal had been
10 July 2025—145 days before the announcement

On a BG2 podcast released that day, Gerstner recalled his assessment from a year earlier. He had put the chance of passing the legislation at about 10%.

He also explained a problem for large donors: how could they give billions directly to children under consistent rules?

The proposed system would distribute large contributions through Treasury into individual accounts. It could give donors a common route to reach millions of children.

Michael and Susan expanded their plan beyond Texas
Before 2 December 2025 (Exact discussion dates are not public)

The Dells initially discussed a smaller gift focused on Texas.

They continued to examine the idea together. Their interest grew, and the amount increased.

At the announcement, both described those discussions. Their state plan had developed into a national commitment.

The original amount and the dates of those decisions remain private.

Senators sought more business support
1 December 2025—One day before the announcement

Cruz and Senator Cory Booker signed a letter to Fortune 1000 chief executives.

They encouraged companies to contribute through employee benefits, community investment, and philanthropy.

Michael and Susan Dell announced $6.25 billion
2 December 2025—DAY 0

Their commitment would provide $250 each for 25 million children.

The original plan focused on children aged 10 and under who missed the federal newborn contribution. It targeted ZIP codes with median family income of $150,000 or less.

Years of work had created the legal foundation for the gift. Michael and Susan had expanded its scale.

Treasury still had to complete important parts of delivery.

After the announcement

During 2026, Treasury and its financial partners developed the account system. Automatic enrollment later allowed eligible charitable contributions to reach children before their families claimed the accounts.

Invest America says the main Dell deposits were complete by 9 October 2026. The wider enrollment also changed the final ZIP code income limit.

The Dells say the money is deposited and invested. Separate funds reserved for children in foster care remain under development, with contributions expected in 2027.

text:
Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX Vision: AI Robots, Space-Based Computing and the $100 Trillion Valuation Claim

$TSLA 
$SPCX 

Elon Musk’s long-term ambitions for Tesla and SpaceX extend beyond electric vehicles and satellite internet. The broader vision combines autonomous transportation, humanoid robots, large-scale energy storage, artificial intelligence and space-based computing into an interconnected technology ecosystem.

The central idea is that advances in automation, computing and energy infrastructure could dramatically reduce the cost of transportation, manufacturing and other forms of labor. Musk’s companies are developing technologies that could contribute to that future, although achieving it at a global scale remains a substantial technical and economic challenge.

An investment thesis circulating online takes this vision further, suggesting that SpaceX could eventually become a $100 trillion company by combining space-based computing and connectivity with Tesla’s autonomous vehicles and robots. 

That figure is a speculative valuation scenario, not an established financial forecast, and the proposed relationship between the companies should be distinguished from their confirmed business activities.

SpaceX Is Building the Connectivity and Computing Infrastructure

SpaceX’s role in this proposed ecosystem begins with three areas: launch capacity, satellite communications, and orbital computing.

Starship: Making Large-Scale Space Infrastructure More Practical

SpaceX is developing Starship, a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry people and cargo into orbit and support missions beyond Earth. Reusability and greater payload capacity are central to the company's goal of reducing the cost of launching equipment into space.

That capability matters if SpaceX intends to deploy much larger satellite constellations or build computing infrastructure in orbit. However, the economics of frequent launches, full reusability, and large-scale orbital construction still need to be demonstrated at the scale envisioned by Musk.

SpaceX has already established a substantial commercial business through Starlink, its low-Earth-orbit satellite internet network.

Starlink provides broadband connectivity in areas where conventional wired and cellular networks can be expensive or difficult to deploy. 

Its direct-to-cell initiative also aims to extend connectivity to compatible mobile devices through partnerships with wireless carriers. 

These services provide a practical foundation for expanding communications coverage, although satellite connectivity does not eliminate every coverage gap or replace the capacity of terrestrial networks in every setting.

For autonomous vehicles and robots, reliable connectivity could support remote monitoring, software updates, fleet coordination, and access to cloud services. 

The extent to which individual machines depend on satellite connections would vary, however, because latency, bandwidth, availability and safety requirements differ across applications.

Starmind: The Proposed Orbital AI Computing Network

The next part of the strategy is more ambitious. SpaceX has outlined plans for a satellite-based AI computing system called Starmind, intended to expand computing capacity beyond conventional data centers.

According to SpaceX's recent description of its plans, the company aims to operate as many as 1 million Starmind AI satellites. The proposed network would complement Starlink's communications infrastructure and help address demand for computing resources.

The concept builds on a straightforward problem: advanced AI systems require enormous amounts of computing power, electricity and supporting infrastructure. Conventional data centers face constraints involving power availability, cooling, construction costs and access to suitable sites.

Orbital computing could offer access to solar energy and different thermal-management conditions. But operating powerful computing systems in space presents its own engineering challenges, including radiation exposure, hardware maintenance, heat rejection, launch costs and the need to transmit data efficiently back to Earth.

Consequently, an orbital AI network is a proposed long-term infrastructure strategy, not yet a demonstrated replacement for terrestrial data centers at planetary scale.

Tesla Is Developing the Robots That Could Use That Infrastructure

While SpaceX is focused on launch systems and connectivity, Tesla is investing in autonomous driving, humanoid robotics, battery technology and AI computing.

The investment thesis is that these businesses could eventually work together: Tesla supplies the machines, while SpaceX provides some of the communications and computing infrastructure they may need.

Tesla's autonomous-driving ambitions include its Full Self-Driving software, the planned expansion of robotaxi services and the Cybercab, a vehicle designed around autonomous transportation.

If autonomous vehicles become reliable and widely available without requiring a human driver, they could change the economics of transportation. 

A shared fleet could serve more passengers throughout the day, potentially reducing the cost per trip and making vehicle ownership less necessary for some consumers.

Tesla's current Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system, however, still requires active driver supervision. The company explicitly states that the feature does not make a vehicle fully autonomous.

That distinction is critical. The economic benefits associated with fully driverless fleets depend on technical performance, regulatory approval, operating costs, insurance, vehicle utilization and customer adoption. They cannot be assumed simply because a company has developed advanced driver-assistance software.

Tesla is also developing Optimus, a general-purpose humanoid robot intended to perform repetitive, physically demanding or potentially hazardous tasks.

The long-term opportunity extends beyond automotive manufacturing. If humanoid robots become sufficiently capable, affordable and reliable, businesses could deploy them in warehouses, factories and other environments where human labor is expensive or difficult to recruit.

Tesla's official AI and robotics materials describe work on the perception, navigation, balance and motion-planning systems needed to operate humanoid robots.

Still, replacing a substantial share of human labor requires much more than building a robot that can walk or manipulate objects. Machines must handle unpredictable environments, work safely alongside people, perform a wide range of tasks and justify their purchase and maintenance costs.

The prospect of billions of humanoid robots remains speculative. The nearer-term question is whether manufacturers can deploy robots at commercial scale and demonstrate measurable productivity gains.

Energy Storage Is Another Essential Part of the Plan

Robots and autonomous vehicles require electricity, and the infrastructure supporting them needs a dependable power supply.

Tesla's energy business includes battery storage systems, solar energy products and charging infrastructure. Large-scale batteries can store electricity when supply is plentiful and release it when demand rises, helping balance variable renewable generation and improve grid flexibility.

Combined with electric vehicles, charging networks and potentially more automated energy management, these technologies could support a system in which transportation and industrial equipment rely increasingly on electricity rather than fossil fuels.

But cheaper electricity is not the same as free energy. Battery manufacturing, charging equipment, grid upgrades, maintenance, land and electricity generation all carry costs. The eventual economics will depend on technology improvements, electricity prices, financing and utilization.

The broader argument is that improvements in batteries, renewable generation and automation could lower the cost of delivering many goods and services over time-not that energy costs will necessarily approach zero.

Terafab Could Address the Semiconductor Bottleneck

One of the most concrete links between Tesla and SpaceX is their Terafab semiconductor initiative.

Announced in March 2026, Terafab is intended to expand chip design and manufacturing capacity for the companies' growing AI, robotics and computing requirements. 

Musk has argued that existing semiconductor production may not grow quickly enough to meet the demand he anticipates.

The project is designed to support different categories of computing hardware, including chips for Tesla's terrestrial applications and hardware for SpaceX's planned orbital computing systems.

In August 2026, Reuters reported that Tesla and SpaceX planned an initial investment of $16.8 billion in a large semiconductor facility in Texas, with substantial additional spending possible as the project expands. The broader proposal is intended to support advanced logic and memory chips.

If successful, Terafab could give the companies greater control over chip design, manufacturing capacity and hardware optimization. That could be valuable for AI inference, which is the process of running a trained AI model to generate predictions or take actions.

However, building a semiconductor fabrication plant is an exceptionally complex undertaking. Advanced manufacturing requires specialized equipment, highly controlled environments, experienced engineers, reliable supply chains and significant capital investment. 

The project's ultimate capacity, production schedule, yields and commercial economics will determine how much of its ambition becomes reality.

It is therefore premature to describe Terafab as the world's largest chip factory or assume that it will become North America's largest semiconductor manufacturer. Those outcomes remain goals rather than established results.

Will Tesla and SpaceX Merge?

A merger could theoretically bring Tesla's robotics and autonomous-vehicle operations closer to SpaceX's computing, communications and launch infrastructure. It could also create opportunities to coordinate semiconductor investment and other shared technologies.

But strategic overlap does not, by itself, establish that a merger will occur.

As of October 16, 2026, speculation about a potential Tesla-SpaceX combination has intensified, with financial reporting discussing possible deal structures and the hurdles such a transaction would face. A merger would require decisions about valuation, ownership, governance, financing and regulatory and shareholder approvals.

Until a transaction is formally announced and its terms disclosed, the idea of a combined company should be treated as a possibility rather than a confirmed part of Musk's plan.

The two businesses can also collaborate on selected projects without merging. Terafab illustrates how shared investment and technical objectives can connect their operations while leaving their corporate structures separate.

Can SpaceX Really Become a $100 Trillion Company?

The $100 trillion figure is the most dramatic element of this investment thesis, but it needs careful context.

A company's market capitalization reflects the value investors assign to its equity. It is not simply the total value of the industries in which it operates, the number of robots it manufactures, or the economic benefits its technology might create.

To justify a valuation on that scale, SpaceX or a future combined business would need to generate extraordinary economic value over an extended period. 

That could theoretically involve launch services, satellite communications, computing infrastructure, AI services and other businesses that do not yet exist at comparable scale.

Yet the proposed valuation depends on several major assumptions:

Orbital computing must become commercially viable. The cost of deploying, powering, maintaining and upgrading computing satellites must be competitive with terrestrial alternatives.

Automation must achieve widespread adoption. Autonomous transportation and humanoid robots must work reliably enough to support large commercial markets.

Semiconductor production must scale. Terafab would need to manufacture advanced chips at competitive costs and yields.

Demand must translate into profits. Revenue growth alone would not justify an enormous valuation without sustainable margins, cash flow and returns on invested capital.

The businesses must capture the value they create. Lower transportation and labor costs could benefit consumers and other businesses without all those savings accruing to Tesla or SpaceX.

The distinction between a massive potential market and a company's addressable revenue is particularly important. Even if automation transforms the global economy, that does not mean one company will capture most of the resulting economic value.

The $100 trillion scenario is therefore best understood as a highly speculative investment thesis, not a verified valuation target supported by demonstrated earnings.

What This Vision Could Mean for Consumers

The most compelling part of Musk's broader strategy is not a particular market-capitalization prediction. It is the possibility that several technologies could reinforce one another.

Cheaper launches could make large satellite networks more practical. Better connectivity could expand access to digital services. 

More efficient AI hardware could reduce the cost of running models. Advances in robotics could automate additional physical tasks, while batteries and electricity infrastructure could support the machines doing that work.

If these developments progress together, consumers and businesses could eventually benefit from lower transportation costs, more affordable automation and improved access to computing.

There are significant uncertainties, however. Technical breakthroughs do not automatically translate into profitable businesses, and lower production costs do not always result in lower consumer prices. 

Regulation, competition, infrastructure investment and labor-market changes will all influence the outcome.

For now, Tesla has established businesses in electric vehicles, energy storage and AI development, while SpaceX operates launch services and Starlink. 

Humanoid robots, fully autonomous transportation at broad scale and a massive orbital AI-computing network remain at different stages of development.

The takeaway: Musk's Tesla-SpaceX vision connects several real technology programs into an ambitious theory about the future of automation and computing. 

Terafab and Starlink provide tangible examples of the infrastructure being developed, while the prospect of billions of robots, near-zero operating costs and a $100 trillion company remains far more uncertain. 

The success of the strategy will ultimately depend on execution, economics, and adoption—not the scale of the vision alone.

text: Infectious diseases (IDs) and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) pose significant threats to global health and biodiversity, yet their environmental and socio-economic drivers remain partly understood. While numerous research has focused on inland systems, marine environments, an important reservoirs for pathogenic bacteria (PPB) and AMR genes, have received less attention. Aquaculture, one of the fastest-growing sources of animal protein, contributes about 5.7% of global antibiotic use, contributing significantly to AMR emergence and spread in coastal ecosystems. Despite this, critical knowledge gaps hinder effective risk assessment and management, including a lack of inventory of marine pathogens, inconsistent data on antibiotic use in aquaculture, and unclear impacts of farming practices on microbial communities. To address the research gaps, this thesis aims to firstly develop a full-length 16S rRNA gene dataset (NEMESISdb) to enable the identification and tracking of potentially pathogenic bacteria (PPB) in humans, fish, and crustaceans. The second objective is to investigate the dynamics of both potentially pathogenic bacteria (by utilizing the NEMESISdb) and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in various environmental compartments. The final objective focuses on the potential circulation of PPB and ARGs between marine environments and human or aquaculture hosts. Results from metabarcoding and bacterial isolation analyses reveal a significant increase in potential human pathogenic bacteria, such as Prevotella copri, Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Escherichia coli, and Vibrio parahaemolyticus within human and marine animals (both wildlife and livestock) and in areas influenced by intensive anthropogenic activities. In contrast, these bacteria are less prevalent in natural environments, and areas with lower levels of anthropogenic impact. Antibiotic resistances of the bacteria also reflect the intensive use of diverse antibiotics in aquaculture practices, mostly from tetracycline, beta-lactam, MLS and multidrug. The resistome is primarily characterized by a high relative abundance of specific ARGs, including tetQ (21.5%), CfxA6 (17.7%), tetW (5.0%), tetO (4.2%) and ErmF (4.1%). Phenotypically, beta-lactam resistance is also predominant, as indicated by the presence of the blaKPC and blaVIM genes. Anthropogenic input, such as urban sewage runoff and/or aquaculture practice, is recognized as the most decisive driver beside seasonality and substrate type for the structure of both pathobiome and resistome of Nha Trang Bay. These factors contribute to higher abundances of both PHPB and ARGs, increase MAR indices in farmers, animals and aquaculture related areas compared to the nature environments, which are further supported by the widespread presence of intI1. Moreover, floating cage ecosystems also promote exposure rates to pathogen-rich environment and antibiotic residues, increasing selection pressures and circulation of pathobiome and resistome between humans, animals, and the surrounding environment. Overall, results from this thesis offers insights to help us better understand the health risks from marine pathogens and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) between human, animals and envrionment in contrasted areas of the Vietnamese coast. https://t.co/i9rsov0en7

text:
🇺🇸🇹🇷Turkey helped build the F-35, then lost the jets. Now it wants six back.

Turkey's Defence Ministry says talks with the US on delivering six F-35s built for Turkey are ongoing. The US expelled Turkey from the programme in 2019, after it bought Russia's S-400 air defence.

So is this a thaw, or Ankara testing what it can still get?

Why a deal is possible
→ The jets already exist, and Turkish firms made parts
→ Trump calls arms sales a "negotiating chip", so jets can be traded
→ Turkey is readying troops for Saudi Arabia, so Washington needs it

Why it may stall
→ The S-400 row is the likely sticking point
→ with borrowed arms, losing, one is undone, and winning, one is their captive

Talks aren't deliveries. Seven years on, Ankara still needs Washington's yes.

The newspaper making the charge is owned by Jeff Bezos, whose Amazon gave $5 million. BRAZIL DESERVES MORE THAN TWO EMPIRES. 🇬🇧🇫🇷🇧🇷

If Washington and Beijing are willing to compete for influence across the Global South, why should Europe stand idly by?

It is time Britain and France remembered that they, too, are global powers.

Europe has the history, institutions, economic strength, cultural reach, and diplomatic experience to become a serious competitor once again.

We should not be content with watching the United States and China shape the future of nations with which we have centuries of shared history.

We must be more assertive. More ambitious. More willing to project European influence beyond our own borders.

Not through conquest, exploitation, or the denial of sovereignty, but through investment, industrial development, technological cooperation, cultural diplomacy, and lasting partnerships.

I believe Europe can offer something different. But that difference must be demonstrated through our actions, not merely proclaimed through our history.

We must stop treating influence as something to fear and start treating it as a responsibility to exercise.

Britain and France must act again.

Europe must compete again.

And the Global South must have more choices than Washington or Beijing.

ANOTHER POWER MUST RISE.

Influence is Power.

🚨 TRUMP DOING PUTIN’S BIDDING IS EXPOSING RUSSIA’S REFINING EMERGENCY—NOT ITS STRENGTH.

Ukraine’s relentless refinery campaign is inflicting economic damage Moscow cannot simply absorb.

And Putin’s response? Seek relief through Washington.

Trump’s proposed Russian diesel deal is too small to meaningfully lower American fuel prices. Yet it offers Moscow something far more valuable: potential sanctions relief and political pressure to halt Ukraine’s devastating strikes.

Trump’s willingness to accommodate Putin exposes the very vulnerability Moscow wants concealed.

Russia is attempting to obtain through American diplomacy what its air defenses cannot reliably secure.

That is the strategic revelation: Putin is not negotiating from confidence. He is seeking relief from Ukraine’s economic warfare.

Europe and Kyiv should recognize the leverage they hold.

Do not rescue Putin’s refining sector precisely when his efforts to secure relief suggest the pressure is working.

text:
True story…

"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."

text:
Friday, October 16, 2026

Broken for the Outpouring

Scripture Reading: John 12:23–26  (“King James Version”)

23. And Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.

24. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.

25. He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal.

26. If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour.

Key Verse: Psalm 51:17 (“King James Version”)

17.  The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

Note to reader: All verses quoted are from "King James Version."

Additional Scripture for Meditation

II Corinthians 4:7–10

7. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us.

8. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair;

9. Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;

10. Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body.

Isaiah 33:23 (KJV)

23. Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not well strengthen their mast, they could not spread the sail: then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.

How Jehovah Turns Our Brokenness into His Glory and Fruitfulness

Jehovah’s pattern has never changed: He takes what is broken and makes it the channel of His greatest works. The grain must die. The alabaster box must be shattered. The pitchers must be broken. The human vessel must be emptied of self. Only then does the hidden light shine, the oil multiply, the fragrance fill the house, and the life of Christ flow out to others.

Charles Spurgeon observed that a broken spirit removes all sense of self-importance. Men despise a broken pot, yet Jehovah does not despise a broken and contrite heart. The more Jehovahuses a person, Spurgeon noted, the less that person thinks of himself; he becomes a broken vessel filled with wonder that Jehovahwould use him at all. Oswald Chambers taught that Jehovahnever forces the will into surrender; He waits until we willingly yield. True brokenness is being “united together in the likeness of His death” so that nothing appeals to us that did not appeal to Him. Chambers also said that if through a broken heart Jehovahcan accomplish His purposes, we may thank Him for the breaking—because through that doorway comes deeper fellowship with the Son. William Branham frequently preached that Jehovahrequires empty vessels: “Get weak so you can get strong.” In “Perfect Strength by Perfect Weakness” he declared that Jehovah’s strength is made perfect in our weakness; as long as we are full of ourselves, our education, or our abilities, Jehovahcannot fill us. Empty the vessel, and He pours Himself in.

Questions and Answers

Q1: Why does Jehovahinsist on brokenness rather than using our natural strengths and talents?

A: Natural strength and self-sufficiency tend to take the glory for themselves. Brokenness ensures “that the excellency of the power may be of Jehovah, and not of us” (II Corinthians 4:7). Jacob’s natural strength had to be broken at Peniel before he could walk in spiritual power. When we are weak, then we are strong in Him.

Q2: Does brokenness mean Jehovah wants me destroyed or useless?

A: No. The breaking is purposeful. The field is broken so the corn can grow. The alabaster box is broken so the perfume is released. The grain dies so it multiplies. The outcome is life, fruitfulness, and glory to Jehovah, not permanent ruin.

Q3: How do I know if my heart is truly broken and contrite before Jehovah?

A: A broken heart has lost its self-justification and self-importance. It agrees with Jehovah about its sin and need, offers no defense, and rests wholly on His mercy. It is the sacrifice He will not despise (Psalm 51:17 ). Spurgeon said such a heart is already prepared for God to heal and use.

Q4: What if I feel too broken already—too weak, too failed, too “lame?”

A:  That is precisely the condition Jehovah often chooses. “The lame take the prey” (Isaiah 33:23). Branham emphasized that Jehovah takes the weak and the empty so that His power alone is seen. Your sense of helplessness is not a disqualification; it is the invitation for Him to fill and use you.

How to Apply This in Daily Life

1. Begin each day with deliberate surrender. Before activity or plans, offer the day to Jehovahwith the prayer of the poem: “O break my heart… that life’s eternal well may flash abroad.” Yield any self-will, ambition, or reputation that competes with His will.

2. Welcome the breaking rather than resist it. When disappointment, weakness, or failure comes, refuse self-pity (Chambers warned that self-pity leads to a slow death). Ask instead, “Lord, what are You releasing or multiplying through this?”

3. Empty yourself of self-sufficiency. In practical decisions, resist the urge to rely first on your abilities, experience, or control. Pray for emptiness so the Holy Spirit can fill and direct. Branham’s counsel remains practical: “Get weak so you can get strong.”

4. Look for the outflow. Brokenness is never an end in itself. Ask Jehovah  to use the current breaking—whether in health, relationships, finances, or reputation—to produce fragrance, multiplication, or light that others can see and receive.

5. Practice humility in community. Spurgeon urged believers to act on the feeling of nothingness by becoming “less than the least” among the brethren. Serve quietly, receive correction without defensiveness, and give Jehovahthe glory for any fruit.

6. Meditate on the key verse and the grain of wheat daily. Let John 12:24 and Psalm 51:17 recalibrate your expectations: death to self is the pathway to fruit; a broken heart is the sacrifice Jehovahhonors.

In every season of breaking, remember that the same Jehovahwho terrified the mighty through Leviathan’s thrashing is the Jehovahwho, through the brokenness of His Son and the brokenness of His people, pours out living water, multiplies bread, fills houses with fragrance, and causes the lame to take the prey. Offer Him the broken vessel; He will fill it with His glory.

Job 41:25: “When he raiseth up himself, the mighty are afraid: by reason of breakings they purify themselves”), describing the terrifying power of Leviathan. Its thrashing or “breakings” cause even the mighty to withdraw or purify themselves. This natural image of overwhelming force through disruption is immediately spiritualized into a central biblical principle: Jehovah  most fully uses for His glory that which is most perfectly broken.

Acceptable sacrifices are “broken and contrite hearts” (echoing Psalm 51:17). Jacob’s natural strength is broken at Peniel so he can receive spiritual power. The rock at Horeb is struck and broken, releasing living water. Gideon’s three hundred break their pitchers so hidden light can shine and confound the enemy. The widow breaks the seal of her small pot of oil, and God multiplies it. Esther breaks court protocol and risks everything to save her people. Jesus breaks the loaves, and multiplication occurs in the very act of breaking. Mary breaks the alabaster box (rendering it useless for its original purpose), and the fragrance fills the house. Christ’s own body is broken by thorns, nails, and spear, pouring out life for the thirsty. A grain of wheat is broken by death in the earth and thereby multiplies (John 12:24).

The argument culminates in a universal pattern: “God must have BROKEN THINGS.” Those broken in wealth, self-will, ambitions, ideals, reputation, affections, and often health—those who appear despised, forlorn, and helpless—are precisely the ones the Holy Spirit seizes for Jehovah’s glory. Isaiah 33:23 is cited: “the lame take the prey.” Weakness becomes the arena of divine strength.

Thomas Toke Bunch’s poem, which turns the principle into prayer: “O break my heart” as a field is broken for corn, as buds are torn to release blossom, as the alabaster box is broken so perfume is set free, as captive trees break bonds to regain liberty. The goal is not destruction for its own sake but outflow—“life’s eternal well may flash abroad”—and ultimate victory sung in joy.

O break my heart; but break it as a field
Is by the plough up-broken for the corn;
O break it as the buds, by green leaf seated,
Are, to unloose the golden blossom, torn;
Love would I offer unto Love’s great Master,
Set free the odor, break the alabaster.
O break my heart; break it victorious God,
That life’s eternal well may flash abroad;
O let it break as when the captive trees,
Breaking cold bonds, regain their liberties;
And as thought’s sacred grove to life is springing,
Be joys, like birds, their hope, Thy victory singing.

This is a classic exposition of the death-to-self / life-in-Christ pattern. Pride and self-sufficiency block divine power; brokenness creates the empty vessel into which Jehovah pours Himself. The Job reference underscores that even the mighty are subdued by “breakings,” paralleling how spiritual brokenness purifies and positions a person for usefulness. The examples are not merely illustrative; they form a progressive typology pointing to Christ’s own brokenness as the supreme pattern and source of multiplication.

Prayer 🙏: The Broken Vessel and the Hidden Light

I come before You in the stillness of my heart, acknowledging that Your pattern throughout the ages has never changed, my merciful, omnipotent, and sovereign Heavenly Father.  I ask Jesus Christ to forgive us of our transgressions.    You do not despise what is broken; instead, You take the shattered pieces of human life and turn them into the channels of Your greatest grace and glory.

Lord, forgive me for the ways I hold on to self-sufficiency, clinging to my own strength and desire for wholeness. Teach my heart to understand the holy law of the kingdom: that the grain of wheat must fall into the ground and die before it can yield a harvest. Remind me that the alabaster box had to be shattered before its precious fragrance could fill the room, and Gideon’s earthen pitchers had to be broken before the hidden light could shine forth into the darkness.

Father, empty me of self. Break the stubborn pride, the human vanity, and the self-reliance that keep Your glory hidden within me. Like the widow’s empty jars, bring me to the end of my own resources so that Your oil of blessing and Holy Spirit may overflow without measure.

I surrender my life into Your hands as clay to the Potter. Let the vessel of my life be broken to my own ego and emptied of my own ambition, so that the life and power of Jesus Christ may flow unhindered through me to a hurting world. May Your fragrance fill every place I go, and may Your light shine clearly through every crack in my weakness.   I love You so much, Abba Father, and I offer myself to You through Yeshua HaMashiach, my Lord, Master, and Savior. Amen.

Adapted from L.B. Cowman, “Streams in the Desert Daily Devotional”

text:
Yes, it is important. So is John 1:42 (Jesus renames Simon “Cephas”), Luke 22:31–32 (Jesus prays specially for Peter that his faith not fail, and commissions him afterward to “strengthen your brothers”), John 21:15–17:  (Jesus three times commissions Peter to “feed my lambs,” “tend my sheep,” and “feed my sheep,” entrusting him with pastoral care of the whole flock), Ephesians 2:19–20 (the church is “built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone”), Revelation 21:14 (the wall of the New Jerusalem has “twelve foundations, and on them the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb”), and the multitude of passages displaying Peter's leadership in Acts (Acts 2, Acts 10, etc.). I'd also point to the witness of the early Church:

St. Clement of Rome (pope ~AD 96) – First Epistle to the Corinthians

Right is it, therefore, to approach examples so good and so many, and submit the neck and fulfil the part of obedience, in order that, undisturbed by vain sedition, we may attain unto the goal set before us in truth wholly free from blame. Joy and gladness will you afford us, if you become obedient to the words written by us and through the Holy Spirit root out the lawless wrath of your jealousy according to the intercession which we have made for peace and unity in this letter. We have sent men faithful and discreet, whose conversation from youth to old age has been blameless among us — the same shall be witnesses between you and us. This we have done, that you may know that our whole concern has been and is that you may be speedily at peace.

[...]

Send back speedily to us in peace and with joy these our messengers to you: Claudius Ephebus and Valerius Bito, with Fortunatus; that they may the sooner announce to us the peace and harmony we so earnestly desire and long for [among you], and that we may the more quickly rejoice over the good order re-established among you. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you, and with all everywhere that are the called of God through Him, by whom be to Him glory, honor, power, majesty, and eternal dominion, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen.

St. Ignatius of Antioch (~AD 107–110) – Epistle to the Romans

“Ignatius… to the Church which has obtained mercy… which also presides in the place of the region of the Romans, worthy of God, worthy of honor, worthy of the highest happiness, worthy of praise, worthy of obtaining her every desire, worthy of being deemed holy, and which presides over love, named from Christ and from the Father... ."

St. Irenaeus of Lyons (~AD 180–189) – Against Heresies, Book 3, Chapter 3

“But since it would be too long to enumerate in such a volume as this the succession of all the churches, we shall… point out here the successions of the bishops of the greatest and most ancient church known to all, founded and organized at Rome by the two most glorious apostles, Peter and Paul… With that church, because of its superior origin, all the churches must agree, that is, all the faithful in the whole world, and it is in her that the faithful everywhere have maintained the apostolic tradition.”

Pope Victor I (~AD 189–199).

Wishes to create a uniform date for Easter. He calls regional synods, accepts the decisions aligning with Rome, and threatens to excommunicate the dissenting churches—treating the issue as one requiring universal resolution under the pope's leadership.

Clement of Alexandria

“[T]he blessed Peter, the chosen, the preeminent, the first among the disciples, for whom alone with himself the Savior paid the tribute [Matt. 17:27], quickly grasped and understood their meaning. And what does he say? ‘Behold, we have left all and have followed you’ [Matt. 19:27; Mark 10:28]” (Who Is the Rich Man That Is Saved? 21:3–5 [A.D. 200]).

Tertullian

“For though you think that heaven is still shut up, remember that the Lord left the keys of it to Peter here, and through him to the Church, which keys everyone will carry with him if he has been questioned and made a confession [of faith]” (Antidote Against the Scorpion 10 [A.D. 211]).

“[T]he Lord said to Peter, ‘On this rock I will build my Church, I have given you the keys of the kingdom of heaven [and] whatever you shall have bound or loosed on earth will be bound or loosed in heaven’ [Matt. 16:18–19]. . . . Upon you, he says, I will build my Church; and I will give to you the keys, not to the Church” (Modesty 21:9–10 [A.D. 220]).

The Letter of Clement to James

“Be it known to you, my lord, that Simon [Peter], who, for the sake of the true faith, and the most sure foundation of his doctrine, was set apart to be the foundation of the Church, and for this end was by Jesus himself, with his truthful mouth, named Peter, the first fruits of our Lord, the first of the apostles; to whom first the Father revealed the Son; whom the Christ, with good reason, blessed” (Letter of Clement to James 1 [A.D. 221]).

Origen

“[I]f we were to attend carefully to the Gospels, we should also find, in relation to those things which seem to be common to Peter . . . a great difference and a preeminence in the things [Jesus] said to Peter, compared with the second class [of apostles]. For it is no small difference that Peter received the keys not of one heaven but of more, and in order that whatsoever things he binds on earth may be bound not in one heaven but in them all, as compared with the many who bind on earth and loose on earth, so that these things are bound and loosed not in [all] the heavens, as in the case of Peter, but in one only; for they do not reach so high a stage with power as Peter to bind and loose in all the heavens” (Commentary on Matthew 13:31 [A.D. 248]).

Cyprian of Carthage

“The Lord says to Peter: ‘I say to you,’ he says, ‘that you are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church.’ . . . On him [Peter] he builds the Church, and to him he gives the command to feed the sheep [John 21:17], and although he assigns a like power to all the apostles, yet he founded a single chair [cathedra], and he established by his own authority a source and an intrinsic reason for that unity. Indeed, the others were that also which Peter was [i.e., apostles], but a primacy is given to Peter, whereby it is made clear that there is but one Church and one chair. So too, all [the apostles] are shepherds, and the flock is shown to be one, fed by all the apostles in single-minded accord. If someone does not hold fast to this unity of Peter, can he imagine that he still holds the faith? If he [should] desert the chair of Peter upon whom the Church was built, can he still be confident that he is in the Church?” (The Unity of the Catholic Church 4; 1st edition [A.D. 251]).

Cyril of Jerusalem

“The Lord is loving toward men, swift to pardon but slow to punish. Let no man despair of his own salvation. Peter, the first and foremost of the apostles, denied the Lord three times before a little servant girl, but he repented and wept bitterly” (Catechetical Lectures 2:19 [A.D. 350]).

“[Simon Magus] so deceived the city of Rome that Claudius erected a statue of him. . . . While the error was extending itself, Peter and Paul arrived, a noble pair and the rulers of the Church, and they set the error aright. . . . [T]hey launched the weapon of their like-mindedness in prayer against the Magus, and struck him down to earth. It was marvelous enough, and yet no marvel at all, for Peter was there—he that carries about the keys of heaven [Matt. 16:19]” (ibid., 6:14).

“In the power of the same Holy Spirit, Peter, both the chief of the apostles and the keeper of the keys of the kingdom of heaven, in the name of Christ healed Aeneas the paralytic at Lydda, which is now called Diospolis [Acts 9:32–34]” (ibid., 17:27).

Ephraim the Syrian

“[Jesus said:] Simon, my follower, I have made you the foundation of the holy Church. I betimes called you Peter, because you will support all its buildings. You are the inspector of those who will build on Earth a Church for me. If they should wish to build what is false, you, the foundation, will condemn them. You are the head of the fountain from which my teaching flows; you are the chief of my disciples. Through you I will give drink to all peoples. Yours is that life-giving sweetness which I dispense. I have chosen you to be, as it were, the firstborn in my institution so that, as the heir, you may be executor of my treasures. I have given you the keys of my kingdom. Behold, I have given you authority over all my treasures” (Homilies 4:1 [A.D. 351]).

Pope Damasus I

“Likewise it is decreed . . . that it ought to be announced that . . . the holy Roman Church has been placed at the forefront not by the conciliar decisions of other churches, but has received the primacy by the evangelic voice of our Lord and Savior, who says: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it; and I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven . . . ’ [Matt. 16:18–19]. The first see, therefore, is that of Peter the apostle, that of the Roman Church, which has neither stain nor blemish nor anything like it” (Decree of Damasus 3 [A.D. 382]).

Jerome

“‘But,’ you [Jovinian] will say, ‘it was on Peter that the Church was founded’ [Matt. 16:18]. Well . . . one among the twelve is chosen to be their head in order to remove any occasion for division” (Against Jovinian 1:26 [A.D. 393]).

Pope Innocent I

“In seeking the things of God . . . you have acknowledged that judgment is to be referred to us [the pope], and have shown that you know that is owed to the Apostolic See [Rome], if all of us placed in this position are to desire to follow the apostle himself [Peter] from whom the episcopate itself and the total authority of this name have emerged” (Letters 29:1 [A.D. 408]).

Augustine

“Among these [apostles] Peter alone almost everywhere deserved to represent the whole Church. Because of that representation of the Church, which only he bore, he deserved to hear ‘I will give to you the keys of the kingdom of heaven’” (Sermons 295:2 [A.D. 411]).

“Some things are said which seem to relate especially to the apostle Peter, and yet are not clear in their meaning unless referred to the Church, which he is acknowledged to have represented in a figure on account of the primacy which he bore among the disciples. Such is ‘I will give unto you the keys of the kingdom of heaven,’ and other similar passages” (Commentary on Psalm 108 1 [A.D. 415]).

“Who is ignorant that the first of the apostles is the most blessed Peter?” (Commentary on John 56:1 [A.D. 416]).

Council of Ephesus

“Philip, presbyter and legate of [Pope Celestine I] said: ‘We offer our thanks to the holy and venerable synod, that when the writings of our holy and blessed pope had been read to you . . . you joined yourselves to the holy head also by your holy acclamations. For your blessedness is not ignorant that the head of the whole faith, the head of the apostles, is blessed Peter the apostle’” (Acts of the Council, session 2 [A.D. 431]).
“Philip, the presbyter and legate of the Apostolic See [Rome] said: ‘There is no doubt, and in fact it has been known in all ages, that the holy and most blessed Peter, prince and head of the apostles, pillar of the faith, and foundation of the Catholic Church, received the keys of the kingdom from our Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior and Redeemer of the human race, and that to him was given the power of loosing and binding sins: who down even to today and forever both lives and judges in his successors’” (ibid., session 3).

Pope Leo I

“Our Lord Jesus Christ . . . has placed the principal charge on the blessed Peter, chief of all the apostles, and from him as from the head wishes his gifts to flow to all the body, so that anyone who dares to secede from Peter’s solid rock may understand that he has no part or lot in the divine mystery. He wished him who had been received into partnership in his undivided unity to be named what he himself was, when he said: ‘You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church’ [Matt. 16:18], that the building of the eternal temple might rest on Peter’s solid rock, strengthening his Church so surely that neither could human rashness assail it nor the gates of hell prevail against it” (Letters 10:1 [A.D. 445).

“Our Lord Jesus Christ . . . established the worship belonging to the divine [Christian] religion. . . . But the Lord desired that the sacrament of this gift should pertain to all the apostles in such a way that it might be found principally in the most blessed Peter, the highest of all the apostles. And he wanted his gifts to flow into the entire body from Peter himself, as if from the head, in such a way that anyone who had dared to separate himself from the solidarity of Peter would realize that he was himself no longer a sharer in the divine mystery” (ibid., 10:2–3).

“Although bishops have a common dignity, they are not all of the same rank. Even among the most blessed apostles, though they were alike in honor, there was a certain distinction of power. All were equal in being chosen, but it was given to one to be preeminent over the others. . . . [So today through the bishops] the care of the universal Church would converge in the one See of Peter, and nothing should ever be at odds with this head” (ibid., 14:11).
