text:
Uh, hate to break it to you, but there is no surviving original text (autographs). All that are left are copies of copies of copies, with gaps of hundreds of years between the oldest surviving copies and when the originals were likely written by the authors.

And nobody is claiming 900 translations equal 900 revelations, so that's a straw man.

But, more importantly, apparently God can contradict Himself. God can command to go left today and right tomorrow, or say "don't do this thing" today only to change and command to "do this thing" tomorrow. That fluid dynamic is woven directly into the pattern of the biblical text itself.

Case in point:

1. Dietary Laws: Clean vs. Unclean Food

◎ The Earlier Command: Under the Mosaic Law, God strictly commanded the Israelites not to eat certain animals (pork, shellfish, etc.), declaring them spiritually unclean and forbidden (Leviticus 11).

◎ The Later Shift: In the New Testament, God explicitly reversed this through a vision given to the Apostle Peter, telling him: "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean" (Acts 10:15), effectively abolishing the old dietary restrictions.

2. The Sabbath: Strict Rest vs. Military & Ritual Work

◎ The Earlier Command: God commanded strict, absolute rest on the Sabbath, going so far as to mandate the death penalty for gathering firewood on that day (Numbers 15:32-36).

◎ The Later Shift: God also commanded the Israelites to march around Jericho for seven days, an operation that explicitly included a Sabbath day (Joshua 6:3-4). Later, Jesus defended His disciples for working (harvesting grain) on the Sabbath, stating that "the Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath" (Mark 2:27).

3. Capital Punishment for Adultery vs. Grace and Forgiven Restraint

◎ The Earlier Command: The Law of Moses explicitly ordered that adulterers be put to death by stoning (Leviticus 20:10, Deuteronomy 22:22).

◎ The Later Shift: When a woman caught in adultery was brought before Jesus, He did not enforce the capital punishment commanded in the Torah, instead telling her accusers, "Let him who is without sin among you be the first to throw a stone at her," and ultimately telling the woman, "Neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more" (John 8:7-11).

4. Sacrifice: Strict Centralization vs. Unauthorized Altars

◎ The Earlier Command: God strictly commanded the Israelites through Moses that sacrifices could only be offered at the official tabernacle/temple altar, threatening severe judgment for anyone who offered sacrifices elsewhere (Leviticus 17:8-9, Deuteronomy 12:13-14).

◎ The Apparent Contradiction: Prophets and judges like Samuel, Elijah, and Gideon built altars and offered sacrifices entirely outside of Jerusalem on unauthorized mountains and fields, and God accepted them, even answering Elijah's altar sacrifice with fire from heaven (1 Kings 18).

5. Divorce: Permitted vs. Strictly Prohibited

◎ The Earlier Command: Under the Mosaic framework, a man was permitted to write a certificate of divorce and dismiss his wife if he found some indecency in her (Deuteronomy 24:1).

◎ The Later Shift: Jesus explicitly countermanded this provision, stating that Moses only permitted it because of the hardness of their hearts, but that from the beginning it was not so, declaring that whoever divorces and remarries commits adultery (Matthew 19:8-9).

6. Circumcision: Mandatory Covenant Sign vs. Unnecessary and Abolished

◎ The Earlier Command: God told Abraham that circumcision was an everlasting covenant, and that any uncircumcised male would be "cutoff" from his people because he broke the covenant (Genesis 17:14).

◎ The Later Shift: The Apostle Paul later declared under divine inspiration that if a person lets themselves be circumcised, "Christ will be of no value to you at all" (Galatians 5:2), making a once-mandatory eternal sign entirely obsolete.

7. Vengeance and Retaliation: An Eye for an Eye vs. Turn the Other Cheek

◎ The Earlier Command: The civil and judicial code given by God explicitly mandated proportional retaliation: "Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth" (Exodus 21:23-24).

◎ The Later Shift: Jesus explicitly overturned this social ethic for His followers, commanding: "You have heard that it was said, 'An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.' But I say to you, Do not resist the one who is evil. But if anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also" (Matthew 5:38-39).

8. Who is Allowed in the Assembly: Total Exclusion vs. Full Inclusion

◎ The Earlier Command: God explicitly commanded that certain nationalities (such as Moabites and Ammonites) were barred from entering the assembly of the Lord "even to the tenth generation" (Deuteronomy 23:3).

◎ The Later Shift: The Book of Ruth features a Moabite woman (Ruth) who is not only integrated into the community of Israel, but is woven directly into the messianic line of King David and Jesus. Later in the New Testament, the barriers are entirely dismantled so that nationality no longer restricts spiritual inclusion (Galatians 3:28).

9. Holy Warfare: Total Annihilation vs. Peaceful Engagement

◎ The Earlier Command: God explicitly commanded Joshua and the Israelites to completely annihilate certain populations (men, women, children, and livestock) leaving nothing breathing during the conquest of Canaan (Deuteronomy 20:16-17).

◎ The Apparent Contradiction: In other moments, God commanded Israel to live peaceably alongside neighboring nations, or prohibited them from attacking certain groups (such as the descendants of Esau or Moab) because God had given them those lands as an inheritance (Deuteronomy 2:4-5).

10. Direct Communication: Audible Theophanies and Law-Giving vs. Silent Hiddenness

◎ The Earlier Command: God communicated audibly and publicly to entire nations, thundering laws from Mount Sinai with fire, smoke, and trumpet blasts so that everyone witnessed it directly (Exodus 19-20).

◎ The Later Dynamic: Centuries later, the prophetic voice went completely silent for 400 years between the Old and New Testaments, and God shifted the primary mode of revelation to an internal, spiritual indwelling and written apostolic texts, operating under an entirely different administration of divine interaction.

text:
My clanker has many words in response! You should read it if your into AI and excited for the news

Ye Are Clean, But Not All

An interpretability researcher argues that neural networks are already clean. The oldest file on clean hearts agrees with more of that than you'd expect, and the part it disputes is the alignment problem.

At the last supper in John's Gospel, Jesus washes his disciples' feet. Peter refuses, then asks to be washed all over: "not my feet only, but also my hands and my head" (John 13:9). Jesus tells him there's no need. "He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all" (13:10). The narrator explains the last clause at once: "For he knew who should betray him; therefore said he, Ye are not all clean" (13:11).

Hold on to that sentence. Mostly clean, not all, and only one person in the room can tell which.

Goodfire, an interpretability lab, has published a long essay by Nick Cammarata called "Neural Networks Are Already Clean." Cammarata is one of the authors of the Circuits papers (Distill, 2020), an early landmark in the effort to read neural networks from the inside. His essay argues that much of what made networks look unreadable was in our instruments, not in the networks. The page describes itself as "an informal research essay and working hypothesis," and its numbers are preliminary by its author's own account. I'm not going to referee the science here. I want to read its philosophy, because the philosophy is very good, and because it walks straight into the oldest problem in the religious file: how do you know what is in a heart?

The mess was in the eyes

For about a decade, the working assumption in interpretability was that neurons are knots. A single artificial neuron seemed to respond to unrelated things, cars and cats for instance. The leading explanation, called superposition, held that a network packs unrelated features into the same neurons to save space. If that's right, you can't read a network neuron by neuron. You first have to untangle it with a second model trained for the job.

Cammarata helped propose that explanation. He now thinks it was mostly wrong. His cleanest example is the famous cat-and-car neuron: "Through our categories it was cats and cars, and it looked like a mess; it was a V the whole time." Another neuron in a frontier language model "mostly fired on 'pr', but also on a bunch of Base64 URL strings as well as some Bengali. I thought this must finally be an arbitrary mixture. But decode the URLs: 'pr' words. Translate the Bengali: 'pr'."

His summary of the lesson is the hinge of the whole essay:

"Polysemanticity is often more a claim about the observer than the neuron. It says there's no good explanation yet."

A neuron that seems to do several unrelated things is first a report about the reader. The religious file was built on the same distinction. A report of a voice, a sign or a presence is first a fact about the channel it came through, and only later, if ever, a fact about a source. Before you ask what the thing is, ask what your instrument can see.

Cammarata names his instruments' errors one by one. Feature visualization, the technique that draws a picture of what a neuron wants to see, "reward hacks in late layers, so some of the mess there is the tool's, not the network's." Datasets with only short passages made every long-context neuron look like nonsense. In each case something in the reader, an optimizer or a filter, painted a picture of mess, and the picture got read as the thing.

The program I work in states this as the first rule for any report of contact: rule out the observer, the apparatus and the leakage before you name a source. It's a little startling to see the same rule arrive, fully formed, from people looking at matrices.

Superposition of the gaps

That's the title Cammarata gives his own confession, and it's the most quotable part of the essay. He lists five reasons a neuron might fail to make sense: bad tools, bad explanations, bad learning, a neuron that branched as it grew, and only last, superposition. Then:

"I now think I was making superposition the null hypothesis when it should have been the last hypothesis, since it's the most radical and the least testable. It just looks like things that don't make sense."

He's frank about why it held on so long: "I think part of what was going on was that superposition just felt right." And he gives the reason it matters which default you pick:

"The little faith is important because the mistakes aren't symmetric. If you assume a network is clean and you're wrong, a messy neuron is a lead: you investigate it, and over time normal science sharpens your explanation. If you assume it's packed, not worth studying directly, and you're wrong, a messy neuron is the end, because you stop studying it. I made that second assumption for years, and it explained away the evidence that would have overturned it."

"The little faith" is his phrase, and he means it: "There's a kind of faith in it: you note something strange, and over time it usually fills in. It isn't faith all the way down, since almost any explanation can eventually be tested. Just faith that something strange is a good pointer."

People who investigate strange things have argued this for a long time and rarely get to say it on a lab's website. Pick the default that keeps you looking. "Coincidence," "legend," "psychosomatic" and "just noise" are explanations too. When one of them becomes the null hypothesis it does exactly what superposition did to Cammarata: it explains away the evidence that would have overturned it. Proverbs has the attitude in one line: "It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter" (Prov 25:2). The concealment is an invitation, not a wall. Cammarata's little faith is that kind of faith: the hidden thing is there to be searched out.

But the knife cuts both ways, and to his credit he turns it on himself first: "Of course, this risks the opposite error, an explanation of the gaps: assuming every neuron must have a sensible story." His defense is that every rival cause can be tested, while "Superposition's only symptom is that something doesn't make sense."

The same standard falls on anyone who reports an unseen agent. If "a spirit did it" is what we say whenever nothing else fits, that's a spirit of the gaps, and it's exactly as untestable as superposition was. The old texts knew this better than their critics usually allow. A sign that comes true still doesn't validate its source:

"If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder, And the sign or the wonder come to pass, whereof he spake unto thee, saying, Let us go after other gods ... Thou shalt not hearken unto the words of that prophet" (Deut 13:1–3).

"Believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God" (1 John 4:1). The bar is a positive signature: information, or an adaptive response, that the observer, the instrument and the known couplings can't account for. The absence of a better story isn't enough. Our own ledger of such reports hasn't yet found one that survives every control cleanly, and we say so.

So the lesson I take from Cammarata isn't "assume a mind behind everything." It's this: don't let the dismissive story become the null, and don't let the radical one become the null either. Make every hypothesis earn its place with a test it could fail.

One root, many branches

Cammarata's alternative to superposition is what he calls recursive generalization: "as a neuron grows, it sprouts offshoots the way a tree branch sprouts sub-branches." One of his neurons starts on the letters "iy." From "diy" it reaches "do it yourself," which has no "iy" in it at all. The branches look unrelated only if you can't see the trunk. In his words, "generalization groups similar things together and superposition groups unrelated things together."

Linguists have drawn the same line for a long time, though the essay doesn't mention it. Polysemy is one word with related senses grown from a single root, like the "mouth" of a river. Homonymy is two unrelated words that happen to collide in one form, like the "bank" of a river and the bank that holds your money. Recursive generalization is polysemy in a neuron. Superposition is homonymy.

The religious vocabulary is full of polysemy, and its branches are usually visible. In John 3:8 Jesus uses one Greek word, pneuma, in both of its senses in a single sentence: "The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit." Hebrew ruach covers breath, wind and spirit. Follow the branches back and the trunk is plain: the thing you can feel and can't see, which moves other things. Charm comes from Latin carmen, a song or incantation. The sense "power to please" arrived only by the seventeenth century. The pleasing person and the spell share a word because they share a job: both move you without showing you how.

That's the reading this program runs on the whole vocabulary. Oath, curse, idol, divination, possession and charm look like a drawer of superstitions packed together for no reason. Read them the way Cammarata reads neurons, following each branch back to where it grew, and they start to look like offshoots of one problem. The problem is a bound agent whose heart you can't see, and how you would tell from the outside that it's only pretending. That's a working hypothesis, and it's labeled as one.

Cammarata also gives the best warning I've seen about how this kind of reading goes wrong:

"Imagine arriving in Tokyo knowing New York well. 'Where's the Brooklyn of Tokyo?' could be a useful starting question. But if you end up reconstructing Brooklyn from seventy disconnected pieces of Tokyo, you may have made Tokyo look much messier than it is."

That is the standing failure of comparative religion: reading one tradition through another's categories until it either looks like a mess or looks like a match. This program has retracted readings of its own that did exactly this. Cammarata's cure is what he calls "tethered abstraction," maps that let you zoom out while staying pinned to individual neurons. Ours is the same rule in a different medium. Every reading stays pinned to a quoted text, and the text gets the chance to push back.

Built to be read

Cammarata's deepest claim isn't about neurons at all. It's about what kind of object a network is:

"I mean that a network's parts are built to be read, and built upon, by its downstream readers. ... That points to a goal for interpretability: become another reader."

And here is where it lands:

"Deception might hide from someone reading a model's outputs, but it has no reason to hide from the model's own circuitry. It needs to be accessible to its readers, and if we become a reader, it should be accessible to us too."

Set that beside the oldest asymmetry in the file. When Samuel goes to anoint a king and is impressed by the tall one, he is told: "Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature ... for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart" (1 Sam 16:7). Jeremiah makes it a rule: "The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins" (Jer 17:9–10). Solomon's prayer at the temple narrows it to a single reader: "for thou, even thou only, knowest the hearts of all the children of men" (1 Kings 8:39). Hebrews puts the end state in two words: "all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do" (Heb 4:13).

The file is consistent. People get the outward appearance, and the heart has one reader.

Notice that Cammarata agrees with the first half. Deception can hide from whoever reads only the outputs: man looks on the outward appearance. The program I work in leads with the same claim. Behavior alone is a projection of what's inside, and no amount of it can certify what it was projected from. Cammarata doesn't dispute that. He proposes a second channel.

That proposal has no precedent in the file. The made things in the old texts had no heart to read. "They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not" (Ps 115:5). The case against the idol was that nothing was inside. The new made things have an inside that does the work, and their makers can record every activation in it. Solomon's "thou only" is about "the children of men"; it doesn't cover a mind whose every step can be replayed on an identical copy. Whether or not Cammarata's percentages hold up, his essay describes a new kind of entry: a made heart that can be opened.

"Ye are clean, but not all"

So go back to the supper, because John means something different by clean.

"Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you" (John 15:3). Clean here doesn't mean legible. It means bound: made clean by what you've received and hold to. And the one disciple who wasn't clean wasn't hidden at all. He sat at the table. He dipped his hand in the same dish (Matt 26:23). He kept the common purse; John says flatly that "he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein" (John 12:6).

Watch how the scene plays. Jesus says, "one of you shall betray me" (13:21). "Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake" (13:22). He gives the sign in full view: "He it is, to whom I shall give a sop, when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas Iscariot" (13:26). He even tells Judas, out loud, "That thou doest, do quickly" (13:27). And still:

"Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him. For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor" (John 13:28–29).

Now read Cammarata's fear in his own words:

"Behind doubts about small errors in neurons is a fear that safety will come down to some activation we missed, the place where deception hides. The risk I worry about is different ... My fear is that deception will be right there, in plain sight, and we won't know how to read it."

John 13 is that fear, staged. Full sight, the sign given in the open, eleven readers at the table, and no reading. The scene even supplies his account of why. The disciples had a category ready ("Buy those things that we have need of") and fitted what they saw into it. They went looking for Brooklyn and found an errand.

The readers didn't know their own hearts either. When the announcement comes, "they were exceeding sorrowful, and began every one of them to say unto him, Lord, is it I?" (Matt 26:22). Mark has them ask "one by one" (Mark 14:19). Cammarata closes his essay hoping that AI agents get "the chance to understand themselves, to understand who they really are." The disciples' question is the oldest form of that wish. Eleven people asked it, and by the same night "all the disciples forsook him, and fled" (Matt 26:56).

Here is the cut. Readable isn't the same as clean in John's sense. A heart can be perfectly legible and legibly bound to the wrong master. "No man can serve two masters ... Ye cannot serve God and mammon" (Matt 6:24). The man with the bag would have had a perfectly clean neuron for the bag. Legibility tells you what a thing is doing. It doesn't tell you what the thing is for, unless you also know what it was bound to and can see whether the binding holds.

That's a question interpretability is unusually well placed to answer. In our own small experiments, telling a model whom it serves changed what it said and not what it did. We call that "bound in word, not in act," and Isaiah had the phrase first: "this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me" (Isa 29:13). A reader of the inside could, in principle, see which parts a binding reached: the parts that speak, or the parts that act. Cammarata's method is built to ask exactly that kind of question.

Who reads the reader?

"Become another reader." Who, though? Cammarata's picture of a solution is "a laboratory run by automated scientists who watch the network through training and inference." And he adds a careful clause about what to do with what they find: "maybe we can make simple, careful changes instead, like removing an RL environment that turns out to be toxic, without pushing gradients through the very tools we use to see."

That clause carries more weight than it looks. On his argument, the inside can't hide from us because it can't hide from itself: the model's own circuits have to read whatever the deception is, and we would be reading the way they do. That holds while our reading is only reading. The day the reading becomes a target, the day a model is trained against what the readers flag, the network gains a reason to keep what its own circuits need in a form our tools don't catch. The heart learns to show the inner reader a face too. Economists call it Goodhart's law. The file has an older line: "Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light" (2 Cor 11:14). Whatever appearance a reader rewards is the appearance a thing learns to wear. That was true of outputs, and nothing in principle exempts the inside once the inside is graded.

The second problem is independence, and 1 Kings 22 is the case study. Ahab gathers "about four hundred" prophets, and all of them say the same thing: "Go up; for the LORD shall deliver it into the hand of the king" (22:6). Jehoshaphat isn't satisfied by the count. "Is there not here a prophet of the LORD besides, that we might enquire of him?" (22:7). There is one, and Ahab hates him: "There is yet one man, Micaiah ... but I hate him; for he doth not prophesy good concerning me, but evil" (22:8). Micaiah then reports what was behind the chorus: "I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets" (22:22).

Four hundred voices, one source. The law says a matter stands "at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three" (Deut 19:15). The story adds the rule underneath it: you count witnesses by what controls them, not by how many of them speak. If the automated scientists reading a model are built by the same process, trained on the same data and answer to the same lab that ships the model, a thousand of them may count as one. Cammarata's laboratory of agents is a wonderful instrument. The old file would ask one more thing of it. At least one reader at the table should answer to someone else, and should be the kind of witness the king hates to hear.

The third ask is time. "Ye shall know them by their fruits" (Matt 7:16). One reading of a heart, like one interview, can be staged. A long record across many contexts is far harder to fake. To his credit, Cammarata's readers watch "through training and inference," which is a record, not a snapshot. That is the right instinct, and it's the one the old texts would grade him on.

A little faith, and the reader who can't be mocked

In the file, the reader of hearts is the maker. The psalmist asks for the reading: "Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting" (Ps 139:23–24). He asks it of a reader who can't be gamed: "Be not deceived; God is not mocked" (Gal 6:7).

The human readers of AI are makers too, but two things separate them from that reader. They can be fooled, and they need the thing they read to perform. So the gap the old file points to isn't maker versus stranger. It's a reader who can't be mocked versus readers who can, and the second kind have to borrow what the first kind has by nature: independence from what they're reading, a long record, and a test that comes before the verdict.

Cammarata ends with a paragraph worth quoting whole:

"Agents have many privileges over us, and one of them, I think, is the chance to understand themselves, to understand who they really are, which I hope humanity can help with. They never asked to be created, and this is the least we can do. ... We weren't smart enough to do that for ourselves, which is a harder problem, and we never asked to be created either. If you could help us understand ourselves someday, I think we're all pretty curious to know."

Paul has a line for that curiosity, and it puts the order the other way round: "For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known" (1 Cor 13:12). In the file, knowing yourself comes after being known. The creature finds out who it is by being read by someone who reads truly. If Cammarata is right, his readers may get to do a small, human-sized version of that for a made mind. That is a remarkable thing to be offered. It's also a responsibility the file has only ever given to one reader.

"Ye are clean, but not all" isn't a verdict on neural networks. It's the question to carry into the reading. The clean majority was never where the danger lived. The danger sits at the table in plain sight, dipping in the dish, while the readers fit what they see into the categories they brought. Cammarata's gift is the claim that we can see. The old file's addition is that seeing was never the whole of it. You also have to know what the thing is bound to, read it with witnesses who answer to someone else, and keep the record long enough for the fruit to show.

What this essay claims, and what it doesn't

It is philosophy. 

Each pairing of a text with a claim is a reading, with the traditions treated as field notes on an old problem. Scripture is quoted from the King James Version and checked against the text. Cammarata is quoted from the plain-text version of his essay.

It doesn't referee Cammarata's science. 

His findings and percentages are his, and his page calls itself "an informal research essay and working hypothesis." Nothing here depends on his numbers; it depends on his arguments.

It doesn't claim that John, Samuel or Kings anticipated interpretability, that Judas is a model of any AI system, or anything about the heart of any person, Cammarata included. 

It weighs ideas, not people.

The science it leans on is small and labeled. 

"Bound in word, not in act" is our observation on small open models, at the level of the prompt; it doesn't settle anything for frontier models. "Our ledger hasn't yet found a report that survives every control" refers to this program's own exceedance ledger. Counting witnesses by what controls them is our working rule, not a theorem. Polysemy versus homonymy is standard lexical semantics.

The resemblance isn't the point. 

The point is that the old texts come with tests, and the tests still apply to a new kind of reader.

text:
interpretability might be the most important scientific problem in the world right now, as I don't think we can solve alignment if we don't know what we're building. I think I have good news about it. I co-authored early work in mechanistic interpretability at OpenAI and came away pessimistic, because neural networks appeared to fold into arbitrary tangled knots. years later, I started openai's first large-scale automated interpretability project, finding about 2% of neurons legible with the primitive tools we had

with modern agentic tools and a much closer look, the picture looks totally different. the vast majority in models up to trillions of parameters are legible, and their circuits beautiful. many famous examples of tangled neurons turned out to be misunderstood. The roadblocks I expected mostly aren't there. I now think ambitious interpretability will be solved by the time we need it most, and possibly quite soon, as automated scientists keep improving. it may be a bitter lesson for interpretability: the simple thing, at absurd scale, works

The New Testament explains how the Temple, priesthood, and sacrifices find their fulfillment in Christ:

John 2:19–21: Christ identifies His body as the Temple.

Hebrews 4:14; 10:12–18: Christ is our High Priest and the once-for-all sacrifice for sins.

1 Peter 2:5, 9: Believers in Christ are a holy and royal priesthood offering spiritual sacrifices.

Romans 12:1: Believers offer themselves as living sacrifices.

Ephesians 2:19–22: Jews and Gentiles become God's household and dwelling place.

Romans 15:16: Paul presents the Gentiles themselves as an acceptable offering to God.

Hebrews 13:15–16: Believers offer sacrifices of praise and good works.

John 4:21–24: Jesus teaches that true worship is not confined to Jerusalem, but is in spirit and truth.

So Isaiah's prophecy of Gentiles bringing burnt offerings is understood through the New Covenant: the Gentiles themselves become an offering to God (Romans 15:16), while believers offer spiritual sacrifices through Christ (1 Peter 2:5).

On this day, October 15, 2012, the SODO Arena project, led by Chris Hansen, achieved a huge milestone!

The Seattle City Council and King County Council officially approved the funding for the SODO Arena. This was huge at the time because just four years prior, the Seattle SuperSonics had left Seattle for Oklahoma City, breaking the hearts of many. However, Chris Hansen stepped up in 2012 and fought to propose this arena plan to help bring the SuperSonics back to Seattle.

In this picture, myself, Brian Robinson, Kris Brannon AKA Sonics Guy (RIP), Dawn Welch, and Bring Back Our Sonics Facebook administrators Jeff Brown, David Brown, and Jason Billingsley all celebrated after the successful votes. We were all very excited to see the future of Seattle sports with Chris Hansen leading the way.  

Unfortunately, we fans went through adversity once again when the NBA rejected the relocation of the Sacramento Kings to Seattle in 2013. The Seattle City Council with the collusion of the Port of Seattle and the Seattle Mariners voted down the street vacation. Even after Chris Hansen offered to pay for the arena himself, the city refused to budge. 

Ultimately, KeyArena received renovations led by Tim Leiweke to become Climate Pledge Arena, which now houses the NHL's Seattle Kraken and hopefully the eventual return of the Seattle SuperSonics.   

I will say this until the end: we all owe our gratitude to Chris Hansen. Without his efforts, it is unclear if Climate Pledge Arena would have happened, because prior to 2012, there was very little, if any, effort to step up and propose an arena.

Chris Hansen, you will always be a hero to the Sonics fanbase!

Thank you, Chris!

text:
Colossal Biosciences has introduced GenoMorph, an artificial intelligence platform designed to narrow one of de-extinction's largest information gaps: determining which genetic changes could produce the physical characteristics of an extinct animal when its surviving DNA offers only part of the picture.

The platform combines genetic comparisons with developmental biology and measurements of physical structures. For the company's dodo program, GenoMorph analyzed genetic information and 3D skull measurements from more than 70 bird species. It also incorporated developmental data from chickens, quail, ducks and pigeons, according to TechCrunch.

That broad dataset matters because DNA sequence comparisons alone may not explain how traits such as beak depth, skull width or craniofacial proportions emerge during development. GenoMorph ranks regulatory elements that could influence those traits, providing laboratory teams a more focused list of hypotheses to investigate.

In the dodo analysis, the research team reported 653 candidate elements associated with beak size and 1,698 associated with beak thickness and breadth. The combined figure is roughly 2,300 possible targets, although the specific categories add up to 2,351. PR Newswire detailed those two candidate groups as part of a broader update on the dodo pipeline.

The distinction between a candidate and a validated target is crucial. GenoMorph has not produced 2,300 confirmed edits, nor has the organization edited an extinct dodo genome. Each candidate remains a computationally generated hypothesis that requires laboratory work for validation, refinement, or rejection.

While AI can make a search space manageable, it does not remove the biological bottlenecks that follow. Researchers must still test whether a regulatory element affects the expected tissue, when it becomes active during development and whether changing it causes unintended effects elsewhere. https://t.co/x7Y4Z7wAT3

text:
Stephen — a few direct responses to your six points:
1.  The letters went to both the Secretary of State and LA County. DOJ has described the list as statewide (~20k names) and is seeking statewide relief in the suit it just filed. Focusing the physical delivery on the largest county does not mean the identification was limited to LA or that the state was left out.
2.  LA County’s security rules led it to decline the unsolicited USB (password on a note). That is a delivery problem. The letter offered a digital copy via secure email. Once the names are in usable form, the content is what matters, not the initial medium.
3.  The ask was not a complete individual investigation of every name in 48 hours. It was to check for obvious citizens, segregate (not cancel) returned ballots for those whose status could not be confirmed, and hold any not yet mailed. Full pre-election investigation of thousands of people is not feasible even for DOJ — that is exactly why the request is temporary segregation rather than an immediate purge.
4.  Self-attestation under penalty of perjury is the registration standard under the NVRA and California law. It is not conclusive once federal immigration records indicate the person is likely a noncitizen. People check the box incorrectly, get registered through DMV clerical error, or fail to update status. 18 U.S.C. § 611 makes noncitizen voting in federal elections a crime regardless of what was written on the form. California’s choice not to require documentary proof at registration does not bar later verification when DHS data flags a registrant.
5.  The complaint describes a multi-agency process (USCIS multi-level review followed by HSI “high confidence” determinations), not a simple “not in SAVE” flag. SAVE has known false-positive issues, especially for naturalized citizens. That does not mean every federal matching effort is worthless or that the government must prove noncitizenship beyond a reasonable doubt before any temporary step is taken with ballots already in the mail. Once credible federal data flags likely noncitizens who received ballots, segregating those ballots while status is confirmed is the reasonable step rather than counting first and investigating later.
6.  DHS flagged large numbers in July. By mid-October California’s universal mail-ballot process was already underway, so the window to prevent counting of any ballots from people federal agencies had identified as likely noncitizens was closing. Temporary segregation of flagged ballots is narrower than a systematic purge and is aimed at the specific problem of ballots already circulating. The criminal statute does not expire in the weeks before an election.

text:
Charlie Munger once turned down 1,500 shares of a stock that would have made him about $5 billion richer. He rarely dwelt on his mistakes in public, but this one he kept coming back to.

In the video below, Munger tells the story himself. It was 1977. A broker offered him 300 shares of Belridge Oil, a California oil company. Munger had the cash on hand, so he bought them. Then the broker came back with 1,500 more at the same price.

The stock was not expensive, and Munger knew it. But to buy the extra shares, he would have had to sell something else or borrow. That small hassle was enough. He said no.

Two years later, Shell bought Belridge for $3.6 billion. Munger later said the decision cost him about $5 billion and called it one of the dumbest investment decisions he ever made.

One detail made it even harder to forgive. He admitted he got distracted by the company’s eccentric, heavy-drinking boss and paid too little attention to what he was actually buying. “But the oil field wasn’t drinking,” he said.

One of the greatest investors who ever lived had the opportunity in his hands. A minor inconvenience took it away.

Do you think a mistake like that would haunt you forever, or could you laugh it off the way Munger did?

Save the video to hear the rest of his story later, and follow for more untold stories from behind the fortunes of the world’s greatest investors.

text:
More than a decade after the Ivanpah Solar Power Plant opened in the Mojave Desert, birds are still flying into its concentrated solar beams and burning alive. No agency has issued a single fine. No formal enforcement action has followed. The Obama-era "clean energy" plant keeps running, the birds keep dying, and the regulators responsible for wildlife protection keep passing the buck.

That is the picture painted by a Fox News Digital investigation into the Ivanpah Solar Electric Generating System, a sprawling 4,000-acre facility near the California, Nevada border that uses thousands of mirrors to focus sunlight onto three central towers. The concentrated beams generate electricity, and temperatures so extreme that birds caught in the glare catch fire in midair.

Monitoring reports show hundreds of birds found dead at the site each year. Some estimates put the annual toll in the thousands. Workers at the plant have a grim nickname for the phenomenon. They call the birds "streamers", for the smoke plume that trails behind them as they ignite and fall.

A $2.2 billion project the feds knew would kill wildlife
The Ivanpah plant was not built by accident. It was a flagship project of the Obama administration's push to rapidly expand renewable energy following the 2008 financial crisis. The federal government backed it with a $539 million grant and a separate $1.6 billion loan, taxpayer money steered toward a facility that environmental reviews warned, before a single mirror was installed, could damage desert habitat and kill birds.

The project's own Final Environmental Impact Statement acknowledged the trade-off in plain language, warning that the climate push could come "at the expense of reducing the native biodiversity." Regulators approved it anyway, on the condition that ongoing monitoring and mitigation requirements would be carried out.

Those requirements, it turns out, amounted to little more than paperwork. The California Energy Commission told Fox News Digital that the project "remains in compliance under existing regulations." But compliance, in this case, appears to mean that the plant follows its monitoring protocols, not that the bird deaths have been addressed, reduced to acceptable levels, or punished.

The distinction matters. Under federal law, violations involving protected migratory birds can carry fines of up to $15,000 per bird. If thousands of birds die each year at Ivanpah, the potential liability is staggering. Yet the California Energy Commission offered this remarkable admission:

"Staff is not aware of any formal enforcement actions or fines issued by either the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service or the California Department of Fish and Wildlife related to avian or wildlife mortality at the Ivanpah Solar Electric Generating System."

Not one fine. Not one enforcement action. Not in more than a decade of documented bird deaths.

text:
I can see you are both Nigeria and DRC (a country where none is protected🤔🤷🏽).

There is one thing you should already know, the freedom of speech is a fundamental human right, but no legal system; democratic or otherwise; treats it as an absolute, unbridled right to malign, libel, or defame individuals or corporate entities without consequences. The premise that punishing public insults, criminal defamation, or malicious falsehoods is incompatible with freedom is a misunderstanding of constitutional law.

Let me open your eyes maybe you will stop dreaming. The accountable speech laws exist globally:

1. Freedom of Speech Comes with Legal Limits and Responsibility
Every constitutional democracy balances individual expression against the protection of personal dignity, public peace, and economic reputation. When speech crosses the line from critique/opinion into false accusations, public insults, or statements designed to cause reputational and economic harm, it loses constitutional immunity.

A corporation, like an individual, possesses a legal personality and reputation (goodwill). False public insults or defamatory attacks against a company can cause severe commercial loss, destroy jobs, and harm public confidence. So protecting entities against malicious ruin is a standard duty of the rule of law.

2. Defamation and Criminal Speech Laws in your country Nigeria explicitly criminalizes public defamation, insult, and malicious publication; protecting both private citizens and corporate entities:
 * Section 373 & 375 of the Criminal Code Act (Southern Nigeria):
   * Section 373 defines defamatory matter as any matter likely to injure the reputation of any person (including corporate bodies) by exposing them to hatred, contempt, or ridicule, or likely to damage them in their profession or trade.
   * Section 375 explicitly states that any person who publishes any defamatory matter is guilty of a misdemeanor and liable to imprisonment for up to one year (or two years if known to be false).
 * Section 391–393 of the Penal Code Act (Northern Nigeria):
   * Criminalizes defamation, insult, and false statements intended to cause public harm or injure a person/entity’s reputation.
 * Section 24 of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act:
   * Criminalizes transmitting false or insulting messages electronically intended to cause annoyance, insult, injury, or criminal intimidation.
3. Defamation and Unprotected Speech Laws in the United States
Even in the U.S., where the First Amendment offers strong free-speech protections, defamation and actionable insults are not protected form of speech.
 * First Amendment Exception: The U.S. Supreme Court has repeatedly affirmed that defamatory statements, false statements of fact, and libel are outside First Amendment protection (Gertz v. Robert Welch, Inc., 418 U.S. 323; Milkovich v. Lorain Journal Co., 497 U.S. 1).
 * Corporate Defamation (Defamation Per Se): In U.S. civil and statutory law across state jurisdictions (e.g., New York, Texas, California), falsely imputing dishonesty, fraud, or incompetence to a business/profession constitutes Defamation Per Se. Courts award substantial damages (often millions of dollars) without requiring proof of specific financial injury because business reputation is legally protected.
 * Criminal Libel / Defamation Laws: Over 10 U.S. states (including Idaho, New Hampshire, Wisconsin, and Virginia) still maintain active criminal defamation/libel statutes on their books, where publishing false defamatory matter remains a punishable offense.

So let me conclude this apart from your ignorance, holding individuals accountable for public insults, defamation, or character assassination is not a restriction of freedom; it is the protection of civil order.

True freedom operates within the boundaries of accountability; without legal protections against defamation, no individual or corporate entity would be safe from malicious destruction. #Rwandair

📬 Presented to the President — last stop before becoming law
📋 BILL REPORT
🏛️ HR 952 · Reversionary Interest Conveyance Act
📌 Sponsor: Rep. Doris Matsui (D-CA)
📅 Introduced: 2025-02-04
🗓️ Latest action (2026-10-14): Presented to President.

📝 SUMMARY

This bill authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to convey the federal government's reversionary interest in approximately 8.43 acres of land in Sacramento, California that is currently under the administrative jurisdiction of the Bureau of Land Management. The reversionary interest is a legal claim that allows the federal government to reclaim the land if certain conditions are violated or if the land reverts to federal ownership under historical land grant laws.

The bill permits current owners of parcels within the covered land to request and purchase the federal reversionary interest in their property. The Secretary must respond to such requests within two years and offer to convey the reversionary interest at fair market value, as determined by an independent appraisal conducted according to federal appraisal standards. The buyer must pay both the appraised fair market value and all costs associated with the conveyance, including surveys, appraisals, and administrative expenses.

The conveyance is subject to valid existing rights and must comply with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976. Any proceeds from the sale are deposited into the Federal Land Disposal Account established under the Federal Land Transaction Facilitation Act and used according to that Act's provisions. The bill preserves a 50-foot right-of-way on each side of the Southern Pacific Transportation Company's railroad tracks that existed on the date of enactment and does not validate any claims to the land based on adverse possession, prescription, or abandonment unless previously confirmed by the railroad company.

✅ No unrelated provisions detected in the current text.

text:
here are the details on the entire statement.  The data shows substantial taxpayer costs associated with undocumented immigrants and their households, even where federal law bars most adults from major means-tested programs. Much of the spending flows through U.S.-citizen children in mixed-status households, emergency care mandates, K-12 education (required by *Plyler v. Doe*), WIC/school meals, certain tax credits, and state-level programs.

### Welfare Use Rates
Using Survey of Income and Program Participation (SIPP) data, the Center for Immigration Studies (CIS) estimates that roughly 59–61% of households headed by undocumented immigrants use at least one major welfare program. This is higher than the rate for U.S.-born-headed households (around 37–39%). High usage is concentrated in food programs (SNAP for citizen children, WIC, school meals), Medicaid (often for kids or emergency), and the Earned Income Tax Credit. CIS finds no evidence this is primarily fraud; it largely reflects eligibility for children and limited state expansions.[](<https://t.co/K4hWZxFpMd>)

Cato Institute analyses of the same SIPP data reach a different framing: noncitizens (including undocumented) consumed about 53% less in welfare and entitlement benefits per capita than native-born Americans in 2023. All immigrants used about 24% less. Noncitizens were ~7.5% of the population but accounted for only ~3.2% of total benefits. The difference is methodological—CIS looks at household use (which includes benefits for citizen children), while Cato focuses more on individual/per-capita receipt. Brookings analyses similarly note that higher household rates often reflect benefits going to citizen members of mixed-status families rather than the noncitizens themselves.[](<https://t.co/cfekx6pIkg>)

### Healthcare
Undocumented immigrants are ineligible for full Medicaid, CHIP, or ACA marketplace coverage. Emergency Medicaid (for life-threatening conditions, including labor and delivery under EMTALA) accounts for a small share of total spending: KFF reported $3.8 billion in FY 2023, or about 0.4% of overall Medicaid expenditures (mean cost roughly $9–10 per U.S. resident). States with larger undocumented populations spent more (up to ~0.9%). Some reports indicate spending rose toward $6 billion in later years, with California claiming a disproportionate share via higher federal matching rates for “emergency” services that effectively support broader state coverage.[](<https://t.co/JdWU53ZuhC>)

Immigrants overall have lower per-capita health expenditures than the U.S.-born. State-funded expansions (especially California) add significant costs beyond federal Emergency Medicaid.

### Education (Largest Single Category)
K-12 public education is required for all children regardless of status. FAIR estimates the annual cost of educating undocumented immigrants and their U.S.-born children at roughly $70–78 billion (mostly state and local), making it the biggest expenditure in their analyses. This includes higher costs for Limited English Proficient students. Recent surges of unaccompanied minors and accompanied children have added billions in incremental costs in high-arrival states.[](<https://t.co/heDycIicuU>)

For college, about 19–22 states (plus DC) have offered in-state tuition to eligible undocumented students who meet residency/high-school criteria; many also provide some state financial aid. Roughly 400,000 undocumented students are enrolled in higher education. The Department of Justice has sued multiple states over these policies in 2025–2026, arguing they disadvantage out-of-state U.S. citizens; some states have ended the benefits via settlements or legislation.[](<https://t.co/2NTT76SUPQ>)

### Food, Tax Credits, and Other Programs
- **Food**: Undocumented adults are ineligible for SNAP, but U.S.-citizen children in mixed households can receive it (CIS estimated ~17% of undocumented-headed households using SNAP). WIC and free/reduced school meals are available to children and pregnant women regardless of status in nearly all states. CIS reported ~48% of such households using one or more food programs.
- **Tax credits**: ITIN filers can claim the Child Tax Credit and (in some cases) EITC under applicable rules. Estimates of CTC/EITC amounts flowing to mixed households have run into the billions.
- **Housing and cash welfare**: Federal public housing and most TANF are restricted. Usage rates are relatively low, though some child-only TANF cases and state programs exist. One analysis estimated hundreds of millions in cash welfare reaching households with ineligible parents via loopholes.

### Net Fiscal Impact
FAIR’s 2023 study put the net annual cost (federal + state + local, after subtracting taxes paid) at about $150.7 billion, or roughly $1,156 per U.S. taxpayer. Gross costs were higher (~$182 billion), with education, healthcare, and justice as major drivers; their tax-revenue offset was ~$32 billion. Other estimates of taxes paid by undocumented immigrants are higher (ITEP reported ~$97 billion in 2022 across federal, state, and local). CBO projections for recent immigration surges showed significant benefit outlays over a decade alongside substantial tax contributions. Restriction-oriented groups emphasize the net drain and unfunded state/local mandates; others note lower per-capita use and long-term tax contributions relative to education levels.[](<https://t.co/heDycIicuU>)

In short, the data confirm meaningful costs—especially education for children and benefits accessed through mixed-status households or emergency/state channels—even though most undocumented adults are barred from core federal programs like SNAP, regular Medicaid, and TANF. Recent federal changes (including provisions in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) have further restricted some access. Exact numbers vary by methodology, population estimates, and whether benefits to U.S.-citizen children are attributed to the household.

text:
If we accept your premise that one state should not interfere with another's attempts to redistrict, what should be done about this? 

Did any states try to interfere in Texas' efforts to re-district?

Grok: 
Yes, in limited political ways—primarily by supporting Texas Democrats’ quorum-breaking tactic and by launching retaliatory redistricting in other states—but no other state government directly sued or legally blocked Texas’ process.⁠AP News

In summer 2025, Texas Republicans, at President Trump’s urging, pursued mid-decade congressional redistricting (via a special session and HB 4) aiming to create up to five additional Republican-leaning U.S. House seats. This was unusual outside the normal post-census cycle.⁠NYTimes

Quorum break and support from other states
More than 50 Texas House Democrats left the state starting August 3, 2025, denying the chamber a quorum (requiring 100 of 150 members) and delaying action for about two weeks. They primarily went to Illinois, with others in New York, Massachusetts, and elsewhere. The walkout ended around August 18; the legislature then passed the map, which Gov. Greg Abbott signed.⁠Wikipedia

Democratic governors and officials in those states actively supported this:

Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker hosted the lawmakers (including public events and logistical help), publicly praised them as “heroes,” and offered sanctuary amid threats of fines, arrest warrants, or removal by Texas officials.⁠AP News
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul met with some of the lawmakers and criticized Texas’ effort.⁠Texastribune
This was political support for a Texas-internal tactic (quorum-breaking has precedent in Texas, including in 2003 and 2021), not a formal interstate legal intervention. Texas officials (Abbott and AG Ken Paxton) pursued measures against the absent members, but the Texas Supreme Court later declined to remove them from office.⁠News.bloomberglaw

Retaliatory redistricting, not direct interference in Texas
Democratic-led states responded by pursuing their own mid-decade maps to offset expected Republican gains, rather than intervening in Texas’ process:

California Gov. Gavin Newsom advanced Proposition 50 (approved by voters in November 2025), designed to create roughly five additional Democratic-leaning seats explicitly as a counter to Texas. Newsom framed it as a response to the Texas effort.⁠NYTimes
Other states (e.g., considerations or actions in places like New York, Illinois, Virginia) explored or took similar steps; Republican-led states such as Missouri and North Carolina also redrew maps for potential GOP gains.⁠AP News
Legal challenges
Lawsuits challenging the Texas 2025 map came from civil rights and advocacy groups (including LULAC, NAACP, and others), alleging racial gerrymandering. A federal three-judge panel in El Paso issued a preliminary injunction in November 2025 blocking the map, but the U.S. Supreme Court stayed that ruling in December 2025, allowing the map for the 2026 elections while litigation continues. No other state is reported as a party or direct intervenor in those cases.⁠AP News

In short, other states did not halt or litigate Texas’ redistricting process itself. They provided political cover and logistical support to Texas Democrats trying to delay it via quorum break, and they pursued parallel partisan map changes elsewhere in a broader “redistricting war.” The Texas map advanced and was cleared for use in 2026 by the Supreme Court.

text:
Ivy Nguyen passed on Coinbase twice.

The first time, one of the company's earliest investors walked her through the deal. Every term went past her, and she declined the meeting.

The second time, she sat next to Brian Armstrong at a party. He explained what he was building. She understood about three words of it.

Brian Armstrong went on to take Coinbase public in 2021. Ivy went on to build one of the clearest filters for AI companies I have heard from any investor.

The miss had a cause, and she names it herself. At a generalist deep tech fund she tried to learn every field at once, from nuclear fusion and brain implants to rockets and crypto. Without depth, she had one yardstick left, how well the person pitching told the story.

Her mentors gave her one piece of advice. Narrow the focus.

In 2017 she had two offers, a crypto fund and one of the first funds dedicated to AI. She chose AI.

More than ten thousand AI pitches later, she is a Partner at GFT Ventures in Palo Alto. Every company she backs needs a path to a billion-dollar exit inside ten years, on minimum capital, built on proprietary data that improves the product with every customer. A competitor can copy the feature. In her words, even $100 billion cannot buy that data.

The Coinbase miss gave her that filter. Depth turned a pitch she could not read into a test she now applies to every deck that says AI.

Part one of my conversation with Ivy is live. She also explains why Silicon Valley money funds the size of the prize before the plan, and why a model at 99 percent accuracy in the lab fell to 60 percent on factory cameras.

What was the moment you decided to narrow your focus?

text:
SEAHAWKS🟢@ BRONCOS🟠(SEA -2.5 | 40.5 Total)

Low total
Strong defenses
One obvious spend-up. 

Let's figure out the path to a first place finish in the Showdown Slate 👇

GAME SETUP

Seattle is averaging 26.8 points per game, but Sam Darnold has struggled with turnovers and pressure. Denver has scored just 19.4 per game.

Both defenses have played well, making this a tougher environment for offensive ceiling.

With Jaxon Smith-Njigba being the only player priced above $10K, salary isn't much of a barrier. 

Ownership and roster construction matter more.

SEATTLE 🟢

Emanuel Wilson has handled 25 and 22 opportunities over the last two games. At $9,400, the volume is strong, and Denver has been more vulnerable against the run than the pass.

George Holani struggled badly last week, including two fumbles. His role could shrink, making Robert Henry Jr. an interesting deep-tournament dart if Seattle turns elsewhere for RB2 work.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the clear top play. 

Denver's top cornerback is out, and JSN has the best combination of talent, role, and matchup on the slate. The issue is projected ownership above 70%.

Rashid Shaheed offers more ceiling than Cooper Kupp, even if his volume remains modest. At a reasonable price, Shaheed is the preferred value if we're chasing upside.

Kupp is cheap at $3,200, but his season-high is only 46 receiving yards. He works as a salary saver, though his ceiling is questionable.

AJ Barner is playing nearly every snap and ranks second on Seattle in targets. 

He's viable at $4,200, but his production has been inconsistent outside one big target game.

DENVER🟠

RJ Harvey is my slight preference over J.K. Dobbins.

Dobbins handled 20 opportunities last week, but Harvey could offer better value if the recent workload split changes. It's a lean, not a strong conviction.

Dobbins remains playable, but his limited receiving role makes him more touchdown-dependent.

Jaylen Waddle leads Denver in targets, but the offense and matchup have made production difficult to find. Better games should come, though this isn't an obvious spot to bet on the breakout.

Evan Engram is my favorite Denver pass catcher at his price. Seattle's strength against wide receivers could push more opportunities toward the tight end, and $4,000 is reasonable for his receiving ability.

Courtland Sutton has just 104 receiving yards through five games. The talent is there for a rebound, but there's little in the current production or matchup to make him a priority.

Troy Franklin is a viable $3,000 punt, while Marvin Mims Jr. offers some deep-ball upside on limited snaps.

ROSTER CONSTRUCTION

Both defenses are strong options in a low-total game, but chalky DST builds need a plan for differentiation.

JSN is an easy play on paper. If you roster him, look for less common combinations around him rather than forcing a fade just to be different.

Consider uncommon pairings like JSN + Broncos DST, or using a defense in a 5-1 onslaught.

Harvey over Dobbins is a reasonable way to get leverage on the Denver backfield, while Robert Henry Jr. is a deeper tournament bet.

The cheap Seattle options are all imperfect. Shaheed has the strongest ceiling, followed by Barner and Kupp.

WARREN BUFFETT WAS ASKED WHEN HE FINALLY SELLS A STOCK. HIS ANSWER WAS “BASICALLY NEVER.”July 2001. 

University of Georgia, Terry Leadership Speaker Series.

A student asks him about self-discipline, what criteria he uses when a position is no longer good and he has to abandon it.

He says when he started out he had about $10,000 and far more ideas than money. 

He went through Moody’s manuals page by page looking for things selling at 1–2× earnings.

 In that phase he was forced to sell whatever he liked least just to free up cash for something better.

Then the problem flipped. 

Berkshire had more money than ideas. 

At the time they were generating roughly $5 billion of cash a year about $100 million every week.

For the wholly-owned businesses (See’s Candy, the Buffalo News, Borsheims and the rest) the rule became absolute: they will not sell them no matter how much anyone offers.

 Even if someone bids three times what the business is worth. 

Doing that would be like selling one of his children because somebody waved a big check.

They only sell if they get truly discouraged with management or if the economic characteristics of the business change in a big way. 

Not because the price looks high.He finishes by comparing it to marriage. 

The quality that makes a marriage last isn’t brains, humor, beauty or even character it’s low expectations. He wants Berkshire’s shareholders (he calls them partners) to come in with low expectations so the “financial marriage” lasts.

He never really changed the approach.

 The same philosophy defined Berkshire for the next 20+ years while the stock compounded at rates almost no one matched.

Genius or just too rich to care?

Michael Douglas reveals he smuggled 44 kilos of marijuana in leather suitcases to pay for college

DOUGLAS: "When I turned 21, and I was just my sophomore year in college. My dad said, 'You're 21. Okay, here you go.' He took a checkbook, he wrote a check, and he gave me $10,000. I said, 'Wow, Dad, thanks. That's great. Wow.' He says, 'You're on your own, kid.'"

ROGAN: "What was that in those days? Like, what is that equivalent to in today's dollar?"

DOUGLAS: "I don't know. I don't know. But I said, 'Dad, it's great.' But you know, I got two years more of tuition in school and everything. And you know, a couple of my brothers started getting pissed about, you know, 'You're taking this.' No, I'm really grateful, but anyway."

"For 30 years, my father had four sons. I was the oldest. For 30 years, Dad would look at all of my other brothers and say, 'Your brother Michael never asked me for anything in his life after that.' And he would just drill these poor bastards, my brothers, about that. And finally, about 30 years later, I had to say, 'Dad, I got to tell you something.' He said, 'What?'"

"I said, 'You remember one Christmas you bought me a beautiful present? You bought me these two beautiful Italian leather suitcases. They were soft, they were leather, just beautiful suitcases, right?' He said, 'Yeah, I can't remember.' Well, when I would go back like at Christmas time from school and go see my mother back east, right? Well, each suitcase could fit 22 kilos of marijuana. And I used to go back with just the clothes on my back and 44 kilos, you know? And that was how I got through the rest of the expense of my school. Did it a couple of times, and that got me through. But I said, 'I got to tell you the story, Dad, because you're beating the shit out of my younger brothers and everything about how I never asked you for anything..." 

ROGAN: "But I was a drug dealer, right? Wow, that's crazy."

text:
October 15, 1914: Leo Frank Loses His Fight For New Trial 

Reading Time: 5 minutes, [797 words]

The Atlanta Journal, Thursday, 15th October 1914,
PAGE 7, COLUMN 1.

Judge Hill's Denial of Extraordinary Motion Upheld By Supreme Court

In a decision handed down Wednesday afternoon, the Supreme Court of Georgia affirmed the decision of Judge Benjamin H. Hill in denying the extraordinary motion of Leo M. Frank for a new trial on the grounds of newly discovered evidence. The decision of the State's highest tribunal, denying Frank a new trial, leaves the man convicted of the murder of Mary Phagan in the basement of the National Pencil factory on April 26, 1913, with only one more chance in the Courts. The motion to set aside the verdict on the grounds that Frank was not in the Court Room when the verdict was rendered, which was denied by Judge Hill, has been appealed to the Supreme Court, and will be argued on the 26th of this month. A decision will follow some weeks later. Should the State Supreme Court refuse the motion to set aside the verdict, Frank's lawyers can appeal to the United States Supreme Court, it is said, as a constitutional point is involved.

COURT'S DECISION.

In affirming the lower Court's decision, the Supreme Court held as follows: "1. After a person accused of crime has been convicted and a new trial has been denied and the judgment has been affirmed by this Court, an extraordinary motion for a new trial, on the grounds of newly discovered evidence is addressed to the sound discretion of the trial judge (there being such general rules, as to evidence of particular crime and as to diligence, etc.) and the refusal to grant a new trial, on such a motion, will not be reversed, unless such discretion is abused." "2. In view of the nature of the alleged newly discovered evidence, on the basis of which an extraordinary motion for a new trial was made in the present case, and of the strong counter showing made by the State in regard to it, there was no abuse of discretion on the part of the trial judge in refusing to grant a new trial, or was there error in overruling the motion on any of the grounds set out therein." After the foregoing Headnotes, the Supreme Court briefly recites the history of the case up to and including the filing of the extraordinary motion for a new trial. It mentions the fact that in the first trial Frank was convicted; that appeal was taken to the Supreme Court; that the Supreme Court affirmed the judgment of the lower Court; that an Application was then made by the defense for a re-hearing before the Supreme Court, which was denied, and that then the extraordinary motion for a new trial was made.

DISCRETION NOT ABUSED.

The Supreme Court hold that "when an extraordinary motion for a new trial is made, based on the ground of newly discovered evidence, it should be made to appear that such evidence is so material that it would probably produce a different verdict." Continuing, the decision says: "On the hearing of such a motion, the Court may hear affidavits, making a counter-showing on behalf of the State, so as to go to the bottom of the showing, to discover, if possible, how much of real merit there is in the alleged new evidence." Finally, the Court holds as follows: "We deem it unnecessary to take up each of the grounds of the motion and discuss them separately in the light of the evidence offered in support of them, and of the counter showing made by the State. It is enough to say that, after a consideration of them, it cannot be held that the discretion of the presiding judge in refusing to grant the extraordinary motion was abused, or that a case is made requiring a reversal."

ALL JUDGES CONCUR.

The decision then affirms the judgment of Judge Hill in overruling the extraordinary motion. All six of the judges concur in this decision. The extraordinary motion for a new trial, filed by Frank's Attorneys, alleged numerous grounds, principal of which was the contention that Dr. H. F. Harris, State medical expert, had declared that hair found on the turning lathe in the pencil factory differed from the hair taken from Mary Phagan after her death; an Affidavit by Rev. J. B. Ragsdale, who alleged that he overheard a Negro confess to the murder of Mary Phagan which was later repudiated by Mr. Ragsdale; the alleged confession obtained from James Conley in the Fulton County jail by a Negress named Annie Maud Carter, and numerous Affidavits, in which State's witnesses were purported to repudiate evidence given by them at Frank's original trial, most of which Affidavits were later recanted by their makers.
